Back-fill: for cross-validation, also check 2013-2015 and 2020-2021 strong-global-equity periods where NBIM rebalancing was widely reported in financial press.
implementation_notes: Counter-signal strategy: counters long_SPY and long_QQQ momentum. QQQ as primary short is correct here because the mechanism is specifically about NBIM forced-selling of Mag-7 / large-cap US tech names it holds at 1-1.6% float each. RSP (equal-weighted S&P) as the long leg reduces pure market-beta and isolates the large-cap-concentration rebalancing channel. AAII sentiment overlay is optional but strengthens the thesis: NBIM rebalancing coincides with bull-sentiment extremes, amplifying the counter-signal. Backtester may also build a direct Mag-7 equal-weight basket short vs SPY as an alternative target to compare Sharpe ratios. Execution assumption: enter on close of disclosure date; no short-selling restriction assumed for QQQ.

name: BARDA H5N1 Pre-Pandemic Stockpile Award -> Long MRNA/NVAX on APHIS+SAM.gov Trigger
rule: When BOTH conditions hold: (1) USDA APHIS HPAI dashboard shows confirmed H5N1 detection in dairy cattle with mammalian-to-mammalian transmission signal OR confirmed human case, AND (2) BARDA opens an emergency RFP modification on SAM.gov referencing pandemic influenza vaccine procurement (search: "pandemic influenza" + "BARDA" + "RFP/amendment" in SAM.gov opportunity feed), then enter long MRNA and NVAX in 60/40 ratio at close on day+1 after SAM.gov posting. Hold for 20 trading days. Stop-loss: exit if position down >20% from entry. If SAM.gov award goes to NVAX but not MRNA, shift to 100% NVAX.
entry_conditions: USDA APHIS HPAI dashboard shows H5N1 in non-poultry mammal (dairy cattle cluster OR human case)
BARDA emergency RFP or contract modification for pandemic influenza vaccine appears on SAM.gov
MRNA and/or NVAX not already up >30% in prior 20 trading days (not chasing)
exit_conditions: Hold 20 trading days from entry
Exit early if APHIS downgrades threat level or SAM.gov RFP is cancelled
Stop-loss: exit if MRNA+NVAX basket down >20% from entry

data_sources_concrete.prices: MRNA, NVAX, BNTX, SPY via yfinance
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: USDA APHIS HPAI livestock dashboard (aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultry-disease/avian/avian-influenza, free); SAM.gov contract opportunities API (sam.gov/api, free with registration); USASpending.gov award search API (usaspending.gov/api, free); CDC HAN (Health Alert Network) RSS for human case confirmation (free)

backtest_approach: Event study using proxy pandemic procurement triggers: (1) 2009 H1N1 pandemic OWS-precursor: USDA confirmed sustained H1N1 spread Apr 26 2009; measure NVAX return vs SPY over subsequent 20, 40 trading days. (2) 2020 COVID OWS: Operation Warp Speed officially announced May 15 2020; measure MRNA return vs SPY over subsequent 20, 40 trading days. (3) 2024 H5N1 dairy: APHIS confirmed mammalian outbreak Mar 25 2024; BARDA H5N1 contract modification June 2024; measure MRNA/NVAX vs SPY. PnL = long MRNA+NVAX (60/40) vs SPY hedge over 20-day windows from each trigger. Distinguish: APHIS-only trigger vs APHIS + BARDA-SAM.gov combined trigger.
implementation_notes: bt_feasibility 3: only 2 clean analogs (2009 H1N1 for NVAX, 2020 OWS for MRNA). MRNA listed Dec 2018, so 2009 H1N1 is NVAX-only. BNTX listed Oct 2019, so 2020 is first event for full basket. 2024 H5N1 dairy event: APHIS confirmation happened but H2H transmission never confirmed -> weak trigger, MRNA/NVAX did NOT rally (both declined). Strong entry signal requires BOTH APHIS mammalian transmission AND SAM.gov emergency RFP — APHIS alone is insufficient (shown in 2024 data). Backtester should test both combined and single-trigger variants. SAM.gov API requires free account registration; USASpending.gov is fully public.

name: WHO PHEIC Declaration -> Short CCL, NCLH, RCL, HOG (Cruise + Big-Ticket Discretionary Collapse)
rule: Trigger: WHO Director-General issues a PHEIC (Public Health Emergency of International Concern) press release (who.int). Entry on close of the next trading session after PHEIC publication timestamp. Short equal-weight basket: CCL (25%), NCLH (25%), RCL (25%), HOG (25%). Counter-signal to long-discretionary and long-SPY momentum. Hold for 14 calendar days (approx 10 trading sessions) post-entry. Exit on day 14, or if any single name drops >40% (lock partial profit and rebalance remaining hold). Size: 4% portfolio notional per name (16% total gross short). Benchmark: SPY (short SPY would be the naive trade; this captures the 3-5x amplification vs index).
entry_conditions: WHO Director-General formally declares PHEIC per IHR Article 12 (press release published on who.int with timestamp)
Entry on close of T+1 (next full trading session after WHO declaration)
exit_conditions: 14 calendar days after entry (hard stop, ~10 trading sessions)
Any single name down >40% from entry (partial take-profit trigger, lock remaining position)
WHO lifts PHEIC or declares 'end of PHEIC' (exit immediately)

data_sources_concrete.prices: CCL, NCLH, RCL, HOG, THO, SPY via yfinance
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: WHO IHR PHEIC declarations (who.int — free, timestamped press releases); FRED none needed

backtest_approach: Event-study backtest on all WHO PHEIC declarations since 2009 (sufficient for NCLH, which started 2013): H1N1 2009-04-25, Polio 2014-05-05, Ebola 2014-08-08, Zika 2016-02-01, Ebola 2019-07-17, COVID-19 2020-01-30, Mpox 2022-07-23, Mpox 2024-08-14. For each event, compute forward 5-day, 10-day, and 14-day returns for CCL, HOG, RCL vs SPY. NCLH available only from 2013 onwards — exclude pre-2013 events for NCLH leg. PnL = equal-weight short basket forward return minus SPY forward return (excess return). Report: mean excess return, Sharpe, hit rate per event. Pre-2013 events use CCL+HOG+RCL 3-name basket only. COVID-19 event (2020-01-30) will dominate; assess Sharpe with and without that outlier.
implementation_notes: Counter-signal: counters long_SPY and long_discretionary. Broad equity shorts are correct here because the mechanism is a specific event (PHEIC) that disproportionately hits cruise and big-ticket discretionary vs. the index. THO (Thor Industries, RV maker) included as additional check ticker for the backtester. COVID-19 is the dominant analog — backtester should report results with and without that event to avoid single-event Sharpe inflation. Execution: WHO declarations often occur outside US market hours; use T+1 close for realistic entry. Short borrowing for CCL/NCLH/RCL post-PHEIC may be costly — note in implementation.

name: FINRA Top-Decile Short Interest + High Borrow Fee -> Long Crowded-Short Squeeze Basket vs Short XRT
rule: After each FINRA bi-monthly short-interest publication (FINRA publishes ~15th and last business day of each month at finra.org/finra-data), screen for names where: (a) Short Interest / Float >= 25%, AND (b) Days-to-Cover >= 7 (SI / 30-day ADV). Cross-filter: IBKR public stock-loan borrow fee page (ibkr.com/softhardtoborrow) shows fee >15% APR. From candidates, select up to 4 names with the highest SI/float ratio. Enter long equal-weight basket of selected names vs short XRT (S&P Retail ETF) in 1:1 dollar-notional. Hold for 6 weeks from entry or until SI/float for any name drops below 15% on the next publication. If borrow fee drops below 5% APR, exit that single leg and rebalance. Size: 3% portfolio notional per long name; XRT short sized to match gross long notional. This captures idiosyncratic squeeze alpha while hedging sector beta via XRT.
entry_conditions: FINRA short-interest report (bi-monthly) shows name SI/Float >= 25%
Days-to-Cover >= 7 (computed as FINRA SI / yfinance 30-day ADV)
IBKR public borrow-rate feed shows stock-loan fee > 15% APR for the name
exit_conditions: 6 weeks after entry (hard stop)
Next FINRA publication shows SI/Float drops below 15% for that name (short covering complete)
Borrow fee on IBKR drops below 5% APR (loan inventory replenished, squeeze pressure relieved)
Name rallies >35% from entry (partial take-profit; size down to 50%)

data_sources_concrete.prices: KSS, W, CVNA, BYND, XRT, SPY via yfinance (daily OHLCV + ADV)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FINRA short-interest bi-monthly CSV (finra.org/finra-data/browse-catalog/short-sale-volume-data); IBKR public borrow-fee page (free); SEC FTD dataset (sec.gov/data) optional

backtest_approach: Reconstruct FINRA SI/Float time series for KSS, W, CVNA, BYND from the FINRA historical CSV archive (available monthly going back to 2013 per FINRA data portal). For each bi-monthly period where a name met SI/Float >= 25% AND Days-to-Cover >= 7 threshold, record entry date. Compute forward 3-week, 5-week, and 7-week returns vs XRT (pair trade P&L). Key known squeeze events to validate: CVNA mid-2023 rally from $4 to $85+, W Aug 2022 squeeze, KSS 2024 squeeze following ESG activist pressure. Borrow-fee data: use IBKR public hard-to-borrow list as binary indicator (hard-to-borrow = proxy for >15% fee). Compute Sharpe on rolling 52-week window; report mean excess return vs XRT, max drawdown, hit rate.
implementation_notes: The basket composition is DYNAMIC — FINRA screening will identify different names each period. KSS/W/CVNA/BYND are illustrative names for backtest purposes; the live strategy would screen all FINRA-covered names each publication date. BYND (Beyond Meat) has very high SI/Float but thin liquidity — enforce a minimum $50M 30-day ADTV filter. XRT is the hedge leg because the mechanism is retail-sector-specific (most crowded shorts are retail names). For non-retail crowded shorts, consider replacing XRT with the appropriate sector ETF (e.g., XLI, XLY). FINRA SI data lags the publication date by ~2 weeks — position entry reflects confirmed data, not real-time.

name: Transpacific Air Cargo Rate Spike (TAC WACI / Baltic Air Freight) -> Long FDX Express + EXPD
rule: Trigger: Baltic Air Freight Index (BAI00_CXFE, published weekly by Baltic Exchange) or TAC Index WACI PVG-LAX spot rate rises >2 standard deviations above trailing-52-week mean YoY. Entry: close of first trading session following weekly index publication showing the spike. Long FDX (55% weight) and EXPD (45% weight). FDX Express segment is directly exposed to air cargo yield; EXPD is the largest freight-forwarding name with strong transPackfic air exposure. Hold for 4 weeks (approx 20 trading sessions) or until BAI/WACI rate falls back within 1 stdev of mean. Benchmark: SPY. Size: 4% portfolio notional in FDX, 3% in EXPD.
entry_conditions: Baltic Air Freight Index (BAI00_CXFE, published weekly by Baltic Exchange) weekly spot rate > 2 standard deviations above trailing 52-week mean (YoY comparison)
Alternatively: TAC Index WACI PVG-LAX or PVG-FRA spot rate > 2 stdev above 52-week mean (from tacindex.com newsletter archive or Baltic Air)
Entry on close of first trading session after publication date confirming the spike
exit_conditions: 4 weeks after entry (hard stop, ~20 trading sessions)
Baltic Air Freight Index falls back to within 1 standard deviation of 52-week mean
FDX or EXPD up >20% from entry (partial take-profit, size down to 50%)

data_sources_concrete.prices: FDX, EXPD, UPS, SPY via yfinance
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: Baltic Air Freight Index (BAI) weekly data via Quandl/Nasdaq Data Link or Baltic Exchange API (freemium); TAC Index WACI newsletter (tacindex.com); FRED none needed

backtest_approach: Use Baltic Air Freight Index (BAI00_CXFE) weekly data from Quandl/Nasdaq Data Link (freemium tier) as the primary trigger proxy — more accessible than TAC WACI newsletter archive. Compute 52-week rolling mean and stdev of BAI. Enumerate all weeks from 2010 onwards where BAI exceeded mean + 2*stdev. Record entry date (Monday following spike week). Compute forward 4-week total returns for FDX and EXPD vs SPY. Key known spike periods: Q4 2020 (e-commerce surge), Q1 2021 (Suez Canal congestion spill-over to air), Q4 2021 (peak holiday season + Omicron uncertainty), Q4 2022 (Temu/Shein surge). Note: AAWW (original idea target) is delisted (acquired by Apollo Oct 2023); FDX + EXPD are the best-available liquid proxies for ACMI yield and freight-forwarding margin respectively. Report Sharpe, mean 4-week excess return vs SPY, max drawdown, hit rate per event.
implementation_notes: AAWW (Atlas Air Worldwide) was the original primary target in the idea thesis — acquired by Apollo and delisted in October 2023. FDX Express segment and EXPD are the best liquid substitutes: FDX has direct express-air revenue sensitivity; EXPD has ~30% revenue from air freight forwarding. Baltic Air Freight Index (BAI) is used as the primary accessible trigger proxy for TAC WACI; both indices track similar transpacific air cargo rate movements. Backtester should download BAI data from Nasdaq Data Link (free tier, code BAVERAGE or Baltic Exchange specific series). Beware that FDX also has large ground/express-ground revenue that dilutes air-specific exposure; the air-cargo signal is cleaner for EXPD. UPS included as tertiary check ticker.

name: Fed Z.1 Broker-Dealer Balance Sheet Expansion -> Long GS vs Short MS Pre-Earnings Pair
rule: Step 1 - Leverage filter (quarterly): Download FRED BOGZ1FL664090005Q (Z.1 broker-dealer total financial assets, quarterly). Compute rolling 12-quarter (3-year) percentile rank. Signal is 'on' if current quarter rank > 0.75 (above 75th pct of prior 3-year window). The Z.1 data is released with ~4-week lag after quarter-end; use the most recent available vintage. Step 2 - Entry timing: When signal is 'on', enter the pair trade 10 trading days before GS quarterly earnings date (GS typically reports: ~2nd Mon of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct). Long GS, short MS at 1:1 notional (each 5% of portfolio). Step 3 - Exit: Close pair at close of the trading day 1 day before GS earnings (pre-earnings drift window). Stop-loss: exit if pair drawdown exceeds 5% (GS underperforms MS by 5+ pts) before scheduled exit. Benchmark: XLF (track GS-MS spread vs XLF-neutral to isolate PB revenue signal from sector beta).
entry_conditions: Fed Z.1 broker-dealer total financial assets (BOGZ1FL664090005Q) rolling 12-quarter rank > 0.75 (above 75th pct of prior 3-year window)
Within 10 trading days before GS quarterly earnings date (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct mid-month)
GS has not already outperformed MS by >8% in the prior 20 trading days (no chasing)
exit_conditions: Close long GS / short MS pair at T-1 before GS earnings (pre-earnings drift capture)
Stop-loss: exit if GS underperforms MS by >5% from entry (pair drawdown)
If Z.1 leverage signal turns 'off' (percentile rank drops below 0.60), exit immediately regardless of timing

data_sources_concrete.prices: GS, MS, XLF, JPM, SPY via yfinance (daily OHLC, adjust=True)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FRED BOGZ1FL664090005Q (broker-dealer total financial assets, quarterly Z.1); FRED SOFR (SOFR) for financing spread context

backtest_approach: Rolling-regime event study. For each quarter where BOGZ1FL664090005Q rolling 12Q pct rank > 0.75, identify the GS earnings date for that quarter (use known dates: Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct mid-month cadence). Measure GS vs MS pair return over the 10-day pre-earnings window (T-10 to T-1 close relative to earnings). PnL = (GS return - MS return) over each event window. Compare: (1) high-leverage quarters (>75th pct) vs (2) low-leverage quarters (<50th pct). Report: mean pair return, t-stat, Sharpe, hit rate. Exclude 2008-09 financial crisis quarters (GS/MS both in stress, non-representative). Secondary test: does the pair also work at 90th pct (tighter but rarer signal)? Available events: ~56 quarters above 75th pct since 2000, ~11 above 90th pct (all clustered in 2007-08 and 2025). GS listed on NYSE since 1999, MS since 1986; full overlap available.
implementation_notes: Original idea used GS proprietary Weekly Hedge Fund Trend Monitor (GS Marquee, paywalled) as the leverage signal. This has been reformulated to use Fed Z.1 broker-dealer total financial assets (BOGZ1FL664090005Q, free FRED) as a publicly available proxy for aggregate balance-sheet leverage. The mechanism is similar: when dealer balance sheets are elevated, GS prime brokerage generates outsized financing revenue that accrues to the highest-margin lines. Note: Z.1 data has ~4 week lag after quarter-end; entry timing must account for data availability. The strategy may show reduced edge if GS/MS mix of PB vs other revenues converges (GS PB ~25% of revenue; MS ~18%). Do NOT use SPY or QQQ as the primary target — GS vs MS pair is the specific mechanism.

name: BTS T-100 Amazon Air Domestic ATM Share >18% → Short FDX
rule: Counter-signal strategy: BTS Form 41 T-100 segment data shows Amazon Air (ATSG/ATI + Sun Country wet-lease, carrier codes 5Y and MN) cumulative rolling-12-month US domestic available ton-miles (ATM) share crosses above 18% of total US domestic cargo ATM. On the next monthly BTS T-100 release confirming the threshold breach, initiate short FDX. Hold for 3 months (one full quarter to allow guidance cut). Exit after one FDX earnings release post-signal OR after 12 weeks, whichever first. Size: 1 unit short FDX, 0.5 unit long UPS as pair hedge (UPS has lower Express mix). Stop-loss: close position if FDX appreciates >8% from entry.
entry_conditions: BTS T-100 monthly release: Amazon Air rolling-12-month domestic ATM share >= 18% of total US domestic cargo ATM
Signal confirmed on BTS publication date (roughly 60 days after reporting month)
FDX is not already down >15% from 52-week high (avoid chasing fallen knife)
exit_conditions: FDX reports earnings with domestic Express volume guidance cut (take profits)
12 calendar weeks elapsed since entry
FDX appreciates >8% from short entry (stop-loss)
BTS T-100 data shows Amazon Air share retreats below 16% for 2 consecutive months (invalidation)

data_sources_concrete.prices: FDX, UPS, SPY via yfinance
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: BTS Form 41 T-100 Segment data: https://www.transtats.bts.gov/DL_SelectFields.aspx?gnoyr_VQ=FMF (free download, carrier-level domestic ATM monthly). Carrier codes: 5Y (Amazon Air Services/ATI), MN (Sun Country Airlines wet-lease). No FRED series - use BTS bulk download.

backtest_approach: Event-study with known Amazon Air fleet expansion milestones as entry dates. Key events: (1) 2019-03: Amazon announced ATSG 19.5% equity stake + 20 additional 767s — first structural signal that Amazon Air was scaling to displace FDX domestic. (2) 2021-05: Amazon Air fleet reached ~80 aircraft, T-100 share estimated crossing 15%. (3) 2022-Q4: BTS T-100 data shows Amazon Air approaching 17-18% domestic ATM share. For each event date, compute FDX vs SPY excess return over next 6-12 weeks. Also compute FDX-minus-UPS spread return to isolate Express-mix sensitivity vs ground-heavy UPS. Use monthly close prices (FDX, UPS, SPY) from yfinance. Construct signal series: for each month where Amazon ATM share (from BTS bulk CSV) exceeds threshold, hold short FDX / long UPS pair.
implementation_notes: ATSG (ATSG) was taken private in 2023 and delisted — do NOT use as ticker. BTS T-100 data requires manual download from BTS transtats portal; no API. Backtest must approximate Amazon Air ATM share from BTS bulk files or use fleet-count proxy (number of aircraft filed under operator code 5Y in FAA registry). Counter-signal: targets the downside of existing long-logistics ideas (PL725, PL455). UPS hedge leg justified because UPS has lower US domestic Express revenue mix than FDX.

name: CCC/COCOBOD Seasonal Farmgate Announcement Window + High CC=F Regime -> Long CC=F, Short HSY/MDLZ
rule: Step 1 - Price regime filter (daily): Compute CC=F rolling 3-year (756 trading day) 90th percentile. Signal is 'on' if CC=F close is above this rolling 90th pct for at least 5 consecutive trading days (elevated-price regime indicating boards face pressure to delay forward selling). Step 2 - Seasonal window: CCC Cote d'Ivoire and Ghana COCOBOD announce farmgate prices each year in the first two weeks of October (main crop) and the first two weeks of April (light crop). Enter on the first day the price-regime filter fires within the window Sep 25 - Oct 15 OR Mar 25 - Apr 15. Step 3 - Position: Long CC=F front-month at open on entry day (5% of portfolio notional). Short HSY + MDLZ equal-weight (2.5% each) as confirmation leg (grinders paying up for cocoa). Step 4 - Exit: After 20 trading days from entry (approximately 4 weeks). Stop-loss: Exit CC=F long if it falls >8% from entry. Step 5 - If CC=F regime filter is NOT active (price below 90th pct), skip the seasonal window entirely.
entry_conditions: CC=F close > rolling 756-day 90th percentile for at least 5 consecutive trading days (high-price regime)
Calendar date falls within Sep 25 - Oct 15 OR Mar 25 - Apr 15 (CCC/COCOBOD announcement window)
CC=F is not already up >15% in prior 20 trading days (avoid chasing post-announcement spike)
exit_conditions: 20 trading days after entry (hard exit, ~4 calendar weeks)
Stop-loss: CC=F down >8% from entry close
If CC=F price regime drops below 75th pct rolling percentile (structural supply improvement signal), exit early

data_sources_concrete.prices: CC=F (ICE cocoa front-month continuous), HSY, MDLZ, COCO, SPY via yfinance (daily OHLC, adjust=True)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: none required — uses CC=F price regime as proxy for marketing board forward-selling suppression; ICCO Daily Prices reference (icco.org, free) as supplementary check

backtest_approach: Rolling-regime seasonal event study. For each year 2000-2025: (1) Check if CC=F rolling 756-day 90th pct condition is met during Sep 25 - Oct 15 or Mar 25 - Apr 15 window. (2) If yes, record entry date and compute CC=F + HSY/MDLZ pair returns over subsequent 10, 15, and 20 trading days. (3) PnL = CC=F return minus (HSY + MDLZ)/2 return (commodity vs downstream pair). (4) Compare vs unconditional seasonal: all Sep 25 - Oct 15 windows regardless of price regime. Known high-price-regime years: 2010-2011 (cocoa bull run), 2023-2024 (supply shock era). Expected signal: ~4-6 active windows in the 25-year test period when CC=F is in top decile AND in seasonal window. HSY COGS exposure: ~40% cocoa, so HSY should underperform when CC=F is high. Note: yfinance CC=F is the front-month continuous contract; test both front-month and 3-month deferred.
implementation_notes: Original idea used CCC press-release announced farmgate price in XOF with >15% YoY hike as trigger AND LIFFE origin differential >$200/tonne as secondary filter. Both are hard to backtest with free data (XOF farmgate historical archive requires manual CCC scraping; LIFFE differential requires paid ICE data). This reformulation uses CC=F price level in the top decile of its 3-year rolling range as a proxy for the board's pricing pressure, combined with seasonal announcement timing. The mechanism is the same: when cocoa is expensive, boards delay forward selling, tightening nearby supply. COCO (VanEck Cocoa ETF) included as check ticker; prefer CC=F directly for the primary long. CC=F futures roll risk: yfinance front-month has negative roll in contango; backtester should note this but for 20-day holds the roll cost is minimal.

name: Brazil Arabica Frost Window Lapse (No Sub-2C by Aug 31) -> Short KC=F Premium Decay
rule: Step 1 - Frost premium build filter (June - August): Compute CFTC COT managed-money net long in Coffee C futures (CFTC market code 083731, available free from cftc.gov weekly). If managed-money net long for Coffee C is above the rolling 52-week 75th percentile as of the last COT report before Aug 31 (i.e., specs are loaded long), the frost premium build condition is satisfied. Step 2 - Frost window lapse trigger: On September 1 of each year (or next trading day), confirm via NOAA GFS 7-day ensemble (freely available) that no polar air mass is forecast to enter southern Brazil through Sep 7. If no INMET station (Pocos de Caldas, Varginha, Patrocinio) recorded sub-2C during June 1 - Aug 31 AND the GFS 7-day shows no cold threat, the frost window is officially closed. Step 3 - Position: Short KC=F front-month at open on Sep 1 (3% notional). Long HSY + SBUX equal-weight (1.5% each) as COGS-relief beneficiary legs. Step 4 - Exit: 25 trading days from entry (approximately 5 weeks), or when managed-money net long drops below 50th pct in subsequent COT reports (spec unwind complete). Stop-loss: Exit if KC=F rises >8% from entry (frost delayed or new weather surprise).
entry_conditions: CFTC COT Coffee C managed-money net long position is above 75th pct of rolling 52-week range as of last report before Aug 31 (spec premium build confirmed)
No INMET station (Pocos de Caldas/Varginha/Patrocinio) records sub-2C during June 1 - Aug 31 (frost window closes)
NOAA GFS 7-day ensemble shows no polar incursion for southern Brazil through Sep 7 (no delayed frost threat)
Entry at open Sep 1 (or next trading day)
exit_conditions: 25 trading days after Sep 1 entry (hard exit, ~5 calendar weeks)
CFTC COT managed-money net long drops below 50th pct rolling 52-week (spec unwind complete — take profit early)
Stop-loss: KC=F rises >8% from entry (unexpected frost or new weather shock)

data_sources_concrete.prices: KC=F (ICE Coffee C front-month continuous), HSY, MDLZ, SBUX, SPY via yfinance (daily OHLC, adjust=True)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: CFTC COT weekly data for Coffee C (market code 083731), available free from cftc.gov/MarketReports/CommitmentsofTraders/; NOAA GFS ensemble free from nomads.ncep.noaa.gov (7-day forecast); INMET Brazil daily minimum temp by station at portal.inmet.gov.br (free, historical back to 1961)

backtest_approach: Annual event study (Sep 1 entry dates) from 2000-2025. For each year: (1) Check CFTC COT: was managed-money net long above 75th pct rolling 52-week by last Aug report? Years where COT data unavailable (pre-2006 for disaggregated COT), use KC=F momentum proxy (price up >15% May-Aug). (2) Confirm no historical frost: Brazil major frost years 2000-2025: 2000 (minor), 2021 (significant but limited), 2013 (minor scare). For frost years, skip the trade (do not enter). For non-frost years with high spec positioning: enter Sep 1 short KC=F, measure 10/15/25 trading day returns. (3) PnL = short KC=F return + (HSY + SBUX)/2 long return. (4) Compare vs unconditional Sep 1 short (no COT filter). Expected signal: ~12-15 active years in 25-year window (most years have no significant frost). Counter-signal nature: this is a fade of spec-driven weather premium in softs. CFTC COT disaggregated (managed money) available from 2006; legacy combined COT from 1986.
implementation_notes: Counter-signal: counters long_softs and long_commodity_supply_shock. Major frost years to exclude: 1994 (catastrophic), 1997 (partial), 2021 (significant but contained). 2021 frost hit Sul de Minas but was less severe than 1994; KC=F rallied ~40% then reversed. The COT managed-money filter is critical: without spec loading, there is little premium to decay. INMET historical station data requires download from portal.inmet.gov.br BDMEP portal (free but manual). Backtester simplification: use KC=F price change May 1 - Aug 31 as proxy for 'frost premium build' (if KC=F +15% or more May-Aug, specs are likely loaded; skip if -5% or more, no premium to extract). HSY has ~15% COGS exposure to coffee (much less than cocoa); SBUX is better pure-play. MDLZ is lower coffee exposure; prefer SBUX as primary downstream long.

name: DOL FUTA Credit-Reduction State Cluster -> Short Regional Banks (KEY/MTB/COLB) vs Long KBE
rule: Entry: When the DOL August preliminary FUTA credit-reduction list includes >=3 states AND the DOL UI Trust Fund Solvency Report (quarterly) shows >=3 states with AHCM < 0.5 for 2 consecutive quarters, enter the trade in late August / early September. Go short equal-dollar weight KEY + MTB (each 40%) + COLB (20%) and long KBE (hedge leg) with 1:1 gross notional (net short exposure 100%). Alternatively, where COLB lacks price history for a given event window, use just KEY + MTB 50/50 short vs KBE long. Exit: Cover the short on any of these first: (a) 16 weeks elapsed from entry; (b) FOMC announces first rate cut; (c) DOL removes the credit-reduction state cluster from the following year list; (d) KEY or MTB issues positive guidance surprise at quarterly earnings. Stop-loss: close if the short basket rises >8% relative to KBE from entry.
entry_conditions: DOL August preliminary FUTA credit-reduction list includes >=3 states
DOL UI Trust Fund Solvency Report shows >=3 states with AHCM < 0.5 for 2+ consecutive quarters
Entry window: August 15 - September 30 in the year preceding the credit-reduction tax year
exit_conditions: 16 weeks elapsed from entry date
FOMC announces first rate cut in the current cycle
DOL removes states from next-year credit-reduction list
Stop-loss: short basket +8% relative to KBE from entry

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: KEY, MTB, COLB, KBE, KRE, SPY (daily adjusted close)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: DOL UI Trust Fund Solvency Reports at oui.doleta.gov (quarterly PDF releases); DOL FUTA credit-reduction preliminary list (annually, August); no FRED series required

backtest_approach: Event-study approach using known FUTA credit-reduction years as event anchors. Historical event dates: 2011 credit-reduction year (California, Indiana, Michigan, etc.) with Aug-2010 preliminary list; 2012 (same states plus additional); 2013; 2014 as the last major cluster year. For each event year, define entry as the August DOL preliminary list release date. Measure forward returns of short(KEY+MTB) vs long KBE at 8, 12, 16 weeks. Compute per-event PnL as a dollar-neutral pair (long  KBE, short  (KEY+MTB basket)). Average across events, compute Sharpe ratio on the 4-event series. Also test whether exit triggers (FOMC, earnings) shorten the hold and improve risk-adjusted returns.
implementation_notes: COLB (Columbia Banking System) went public as COLB in current form after the Umpqua Bank merger (2023); prior to 2023 use COLB legacy ticker or substitute PBCT (acquired) - backtester should use KEY+MTB 50/50 for pre-2023 windows. KBE is the most appropriate benchmark (all US bank ETF); KRE is an alternative regional-bank ETF and can be used for cross-validation. The 2010-2014 FUTA credit-reduction cluster was concentrated in states with large manufacturing and service-sector employment (CA, IN, MI, NY, NJ, OH, WI). KEY has significant OH/NY exposure; MTB heavy in NY/NJ/PA. The mechanism requires at least 3-4 states in the cluster to create meaningful SMB payroll-tax drag; single-state events are noise.

name: NJ/CT Property-Tax Delinquency + High-Income Outmigration -> Short SPG/SKT vs Long REZ
rule: Counter-signal against the long_SPY consumer-discretionary consensus. Entry: When NJ residential property-tax delinquency rate YoY rises >150bp in the same quarter that IRS SOI county-to-county migration data (most recent annual release) shows NJ+CT combined net AGI outflow to FL+TX exceeding B, enter the trade. Go short SPG (50%) + SKT (50%) equal-dollar notional and long REZ (residential REIT ETF) equal dollar notional as a hedge. Exit: Cover on any of: (a) 14 weeks elapsed from entry; (b) NJ/CT delinquency rate decelerates YoY; (c) SPG issues positive same-store-NOI guidance surprise; (d) Stop-loss: SPG+SKT basket rises >7% relative to REZ from entry. Where FOIA USPS data is unavailable, IRS SOI file date can substitute for migration confirmation.
entry_conditions: NJ residential property-tax delinquency YoY change > +150 basis points (quarterly NJ Treasury data)
IRS SOI county-to-county file shows NJ+CT combined net AGI outflow to FL+TX > B in latest annual release
SPG and/or SKT are trading within 10% of 52-week highs (crowded long condition)
exit_conditions: 14 weeks elapsed from entry date
NJ/CT property-tax delinquency rate decelerates vs prior quarter YoY reading
SPG positive same-store-NOI guidance surprise at earnings
Stop-loss: SPG+SKT basket +7% relative to REZ from entry

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: SPG, SKT, REZ, MAC, SPY (daily adjusted close)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: NJ Department of Treasury quarterly property-tax collections and delinquency report (state.nj.us/treasury/taxation/); IRS Statistics of Income county-to-county migration files (irs.gov/statistics/soi-tax-stats-migration-data) annual releases; no FRED series required

backtest_approach: Event-study using observable delinquency + migration trigger dates. Primary backtest window: 2008Q3-2012Q4 GFC/post-GFC period when NJ/CT property-tax delinquency spiked materially and high-income households began Florida migration. Identify calendar quarters when NJ delinquency YoY delta > 150bp (from NJ Treasury publications). Match with IRS SOI annual file confirming AGI outflow threshold. Entry on the first trading day of the month following trigger confirmation. Measure forward 6-week, 10-week, 14-week returns of short(SPG+SKT equal-weight) vs long(REZ). Compute excess return of pair at each horizon, aggregate across events. Also use 2020-2021 COVID-era urban-to-suburban shift as a validation window. MAC (Macerich) included for robustness cross-check but not primary target.
implementation_notes: IRS SOI migration data has 18-24 month publication lag (e.g., 2022 migration data released in 2024). In backtesting, use the data as if it were the annual release date for each year. The entry trigger for real-time use requires the delinquency quarterly data to be primary signal, with SOI as secondary confirmation. REZ (iShares Residential and Multisector Real Estate ETF) began trading 2014-05-01; for pre-2014 backtest periods use IYR or VNQ as the hedge leg. SKT (Tanger Factory Outlet) is outlet-center focused, not purely Mid-Atlantic, but has significant NJ/CT tenant exposure. SPG has ~40 properties in NJ/CT region. MAC (Macerich) is a secondary cross-check name with West Coast focus — include as a robustness check ticker but not in the primary short basket. This is a counter-signal against the long_SPY consumer-discretionary consensus; trading SPG/SKT directly (not SPY) per the spec preference for specific names.

name: FDA Purple Book Interchangeability Designation Cascade -> Short JNJ / Long AMRX+TEVA Biosimilar Pair
rule: Entry: When FDA grants an interchangeability designation to a biosimilar of a top-5 JNJ Innovative Medicine franchise drug (Stelara/ustekinumab, Tremfya/guselkumab, Darzalex/daratumumab, or Erleada/apalutamide) in the Purple Book update, enter the pair within 5 trading days of the designation date. Go short JNJ (single name, 50% gross notional) and long equal-weight AMRX+TEVA (50% gross notional each side, 25% each). Use XPH as sector hedge to neutralize broad pharma beta: optional long XPH position can offset JNJ sector exposure. Net position: short JNJ vs long AMRX+TEVA (2:1 notional toward biosimilar longs). Exit: (a) 8 months elapsed from entry; (b) JNJ lowers Innovative Medicine segment revenue guidance at quarterly earnings; (c) AMRX or TEVA reports >10% volume beat on the specific molecule; (d) Stop-loss: JNJ appreciates >6% relative to XPH from entry.
entry_conditions: FDA Purple Book lists a new interchangeability designation for a Stelara/ustekinumab, Darzalex, Tremfya, or Erleada biosimilar
JNJ biosimilar-affected franchise revenue still >B annual run-rate in most recent 10-Q (ensuring material impact)
Entry within 5 trading days of FDA Purple Book update date
exit_conditions: 8 months elapsed from entry date
JNJ Innovative Medicine segment revenue guidance cut by >5% in quarterly earnings
AMRX or TEVA reports confirmed volume gain >10% on the designated molecule
Stop-loss: JNJ outperforms XPH by >6% from entry date

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: JNJ, AMRX, TEVA, XPH, SPY (daily adjusted close)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FDA Purple Book (biologics.fda.gov/biologics-information/purple-book-database-of-licensed-biological-products) for interchangeability designation dates; JNJ 10-Q quarterly segment revenue disclosures (SEC EDGAR); no FRED series required

backtest_approach: Event-study using FDA Purple Book interchangeability designation dates as event anchors. Known historical interchangeability grants relevant to JNJ molecules: (1) Cyltezo (adalimumab, Humira biosimilar, not JNJ but establishes the mechanism - July 2021); (2) Hyrimoz interchangeability (adalimumab SC, Nov 2023); (3) Stelara biosimilar interchangeability designations: Samsung Bioepis / Sandoz received biosimilar approval (Feb-Mar 2025 wave) with interchangeability designations following. For each event date, measure forward returns: short JNJ return minus long (AMRX+TEVA)/2 return at 4, 8, 12, 16 weeks. Compute per-event PnL on a dollar-neutral pair, aggregate across events. JNJ and TEVA have 20+ year price histories; AMRX has history from IPO (2017 as Amneal Pharmaceuticals). Use only events where all three tickers had >1 year of price history at the event date.
implementation_notes: CDMO (Avid Bioservices, a potential biosimilar CDMO play) was acquired by Lonza in 2024 and is no longer publicly traded - exclude from strategy. HIK.L (Hikma) trades on LSE and lacks ADR; exclude in favor of US-listed AMRX and TEVA. XPH (SPDR Pharma ETF) is used as optional sector-beta neutralizer for JNJ short. The interchangeability mechanism is molecule-specific and non-linear: each new interchangeability stacks the prior one, so the 2nd and 3rd designations on the same molecule are more impactful. The backtester should check if JNJ had already discounted the first designation and model incremental revenue impact per new designation. For Stelara specifically, JNJ flagged .6B 2024 revenues at risk; biosimilar interchangeability typically captures 30-40% script share within 90 days of PBM formulary tier change.

name: IRS 48E Tech-Neutral ITC Final Regs + Domestic Content Safe Harbor -> Long FLNC Backlog Acceleration
rule: Entry: When IRS/Treasury publishes final regulations under IRA Section 48E (tech-neutral investment tax credit for energy storage) OR a significant safe-harbor guidance notice clarifying standalone BESS domestic-content bonus adder mechanics (via Federal Register or IRS Internal Revenue Bulletin), enter long FLNC within 5 trading days of the publication date. Size: 100% notional long FLNC, with SPY hedge at 50% notional short to neutralize broad market beta. Target: hold into FLNC next quarterly earnings (backlog and bookings disclosure). Exit: (a) 12 weeks elapsed; (b) FLNC quarterly earnings with backlog/coverage ratio beat vs consensus (take profit on the beat); (c) FLNC backlogs miss guidance by >15%; (d) Stop-loss: FLNC falls >12% from entry close.
entry_conditions: IRS/Treasury publishes 48E final regs OR major guidance notice in Federal Register/IRB clarifying standalone BESS ITC eligibility or domestic content bonus adder
FLNC most recent 10-Q shows backlog coverage ratio (backlog / NTM consensus revenue) > 1.2x (indicating pipeline health)
Entry within 5 trading days of publication date
exit_conditions: 12 weeks elapsed from entry date
FLNC quarterly earnings: backlog coverage ratio beat >10% vs consensus (take profit)
FLNC quarterly earnings: backlog miss >15% vs prior quarter guidance
Stop-loss: FLNC falls >12% from entry date close

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: FLNC, FSLR, ENPH, SPY (daily adjusted close)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: Federal Register API (api.federalregister.gov) for IRS/Treasury final reg publication dates with 48E/standalone storage keywords; IRS Internal Revenue Bulletin index (irs.gov/irb) for Notice dates; FLNC 10-Q backlog disclosures (SEC EDGAR, quarterly); EIA Form 860M for BESS planned capacity additions (proxy for market demand); no FRED series required

backtest_approach: Event-study using IRS/Treasury guidance publication dates as event anchors. FLNC trades since Oct 2021 (IPO), limiting history. Known 48E guidance events within FLNC price history: (1) IRA enacted Aug 16 2022 (initial signal - standalone storage ITC confirmed); (2) Treasury Notice 2023-29 (April 2023, bonus adder preliminary guidance); (3) Treasury final rules on domestic content adder (May 2024, Notice 2024-41); (4) 48E proposed regs published December 2023; (5) 48E final regs expected publication (use actual date when available). For each event date, measure FLNC forward returns at 4, 6, 8, 12 weeks versus SPY. Compute excess return (FLNC - SPY) at each horizon. FSLR and ENPH included as sector control instruments: measure FLNC excess return vs clean-energy sector to isolate storage-specific (not solar) response. Note: with only 4-5 events, statistical confidence is limited; treat as illustrative evidence, not high-confidence backtest.
implementation_notes: FLNC (Fluence Energy) went public via SPAC/IPO on Oct 28 2021. History is limited to ~4 years. The number of independent 48E guidance events within this window is 4-5, which is thin for a conventional backtest. The backtester should note this explicitly and use wider confidence intervals. FSLR (First Solar) and ENPH (Enphase) are included as sector controls to separate FLNC's response from broad clean-energy sector moves. The domestic content angle is specifically relevant to FLNC because Fluence partners with US-manufactured cell suppliers (Samsung SDI US plant for battery cells), making its product stack eligible for the 10% domestic content bonus adder that competitors cannot easily match. The backlog conversion mechanism is confirmed in FLNC 10-Ks: orders typically convert to revenue within 1-3 quarters. Post-guidance-clarity, FID conversion rate historically accelerates by 15-30% per FLNC investor day materials.

name: USPTO PTAB Final Written Decision Invalidates Orange Book Patent -> Long TEVA/AMRX vs Short Brand Sponsor
rule: Step 1 - Event trigger: Monitor USPTO PTAB Electronic Filing System (EFS) and PTAB API (petitions.uspto.gov/ptab-web/api/query/) for Final Written Decisions (FWD) where: (a) at least one Orange Book-listed patent is invalidated (as unpatentable), (b) the patent is tied to a drug with >$500M annual US revenue (top-50 brand), AND (c) at least one generic ANDA applicant has Paragraph IV certification with tentative or final FDA approval. Step 2 - Position sizing: On T+1 after FWD publication date, enter: Long TEVA (50%) + long AMRX (50%) as generic beneficiaries at 3% notional each (6% total long). Short the brand sponsor at 4% notional. If multiple sponsors (Eliquis = BMY + PFE), short equal weight. Step 3 - Hold period: 90 calendar days from FWD date, or until Federal Circuit appeal panel issues a stay of the FWD (rare, requires brand to show likelihood of success on appeal). Step 4 - Exit: At 90 days, or earlier if TEVA/AMRX basket up >30% (lock in), or if brand sponsor down >25% (lock in short profit). Stop-loss: Exit entire position if brand wins Federal Circuit stay within 30 days of FWD.
entry_conditions: USPTO PTAB issues Final Written Decision (FWD) invalidating as unpatentable at least one Orange Book-listed patent for a drug with >$500M US annual revenue
At least one generic ANDA applicant has Paragraph IV certification AND tentative or final FDA approval for the molecule
No Federal Circuit stay of the FWD currently in effect
Brand sponsor stock not already down >15% in prior 10 trading days (not chasing delayed reaction)
exit_conditions: 90 calendar days after FWD publication date (hard exit)
Federal Circuit grants emergency stay of PTAB FWD within 30 days (exit immediately — trade thesis invalidated)
TEVA/AMRX basket up >30% from entry (take profit, close longs)
Brand sponsor down >25% from entry (take profit, close short)

data_sources_concrete.prices: TEVA, AMRX, VTRS, MRK, ABBV, BMY, PFE, JNJ, SPY via yfinance (daily OHLC, adjust=True)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: USPTO PTAB API (petitions.uspto.gov/ptab-web/api/query/, free JSON API — filter on proceedingStatus=FWD-WRITTEN and subjectMatterType=DRUG); FDA Orange Book patent listings (accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/ob/, free); FDA Para IV Certification list (fda.gov/drugs/hatch-waxman-challenges, free)

backtest_approach: Event-study backtest on historical PTAB FWD events from 2012-2025 (PTAB started 2012). For each qualifying FWD (invalidation of Orange Book pharma patent, >$500M drug): (1) Record FWD date, brand sponsor, and available generic names (with ANDA), (2) Compute brand sponsor stock return vs SPY on T+1, T+5, T+10, T+30, T+90 from FWD date, (3) Compute TEVA + AMRX pair return over same windows, (4) PnL = (long TEVA/AMRX portfolio) - (short brand sponsor) - SPY net. Known analog events: Oct 2017: PTAB FWD invalidating Restasis patents (Allergan/AGN, Dec 2016 + Oct 2017); 2018-2019: Lyrica (pregabalin) patent events (PFE vs generics); 2021-2022: Humira (adalimumab) secondary formulation IPRs (AbbVie); 2022-2023: Eliquis (apixaban) polymorph and dosing patents (BMY/PFE). AMRX listed May 2018 — pre-2018 events use TEVA + VTRS only. Exclude events where brand company announced LOE guidance pre-FWD (already priced). Report: mean brand sponsor 30-day return post-FWD (expected negative), t-stat, hit rate.
implementation_notes: PTAB API returns JSON with proceeding number, patent numbers, final decision outcome, and dates. Filter: proceedingType=IPR, subjectMatterType contains 'drug' or patent linked to FDA Orange Book. Cross-reference with FDA Orange Book via drug product listing (NDA/ANDA linkage). Key limitation: not all PTAB IPRs are on Orange Book-listed patents; manual review of patent numbers required to confirm Orange Book listing. Backtester should note: AMRX IPO May 2018, so pre-2018 long leg uses TEVA only (or TEVA + VTRS after VTRS formed Nov 2020 via Viatris Mylan/Pfizer Upjohn spin). HIK.L (Hikma) is UK-listed and harder to pull via yfinance — use TEVA/AMRX/VTRS as US-listed proxies.

name: India DGFT Sugar Export Quota Release OGL >1 MMT -> Short CANE / Long Indian Sugar Mills Pair
rule: When India DGFT issues an Open General License (OGL) notification permitting sugar exports of >=1 MMT after a minimum 2-month export suspension: (1) Short CANE ETF (proxy for ICE NY11 SB=F sugar futures); (2) Long equal-weight basket: BALRAMCHIN.NS + EIDPARRY.NS. Leg sizes: short 1 unit CANE, long 0.5 unit each of BALRAMCHIN.NS + EIDPARRY.NS. Exit after 15 trading days OR when CANE drops >8% from entry (take profit). Stop-loss: close if CANE rises >5% from entry. Indian mill longs exit simultaneously to close the pair.
entry_conditions: DGFT publishes OGL notification for Indian sugar export quantity >= 1 million metric tons
Notification follows a prior export suspension or quota of >= 2 months duration
CANE not already down >5% in preceding 5 trading days (avoid chasing move)
exit_conditions: 15 trading days elapsed after entry (time-exit)
CANE drops >8% from entry (take-profit on short leg)
CANE rises >5% from entry (stop-loss on short leg)
DGFT issues reversal notification reinstating export ban (exit long mills immediately)

data_sources_concrete.prices: SB=F (ICE NY11 sugar futures), CANE (Teucrium Sugar ETF), BALRAMCHIN.NS, DHAMPURSUG.NS, EIDPARRY.NS, SPY via yfinance
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: DGFT Notifications portal: https://www.dgft.gov.in/CP/?opt=notification (free, text-search OGL notifications with sugar export quantity). ISMA monthly stock data at isma.in for domestic supply context. USDA FAS GAIN India sugar reports at apps.fas.usda.gov for event date verification. No FRED series needed.

backtest_approach: Event-study backtest on confirmed DGFT OGL release dates for sugar export tranches. Known historical events: (1) 2021-11-01: DGFT allowed 6 MMT sugar export for MY2021-22 (OGL after multi-season ban). (2) 2022-05-24: DGFT capped FY2022-23 exports at 10 MMT. (3) 2023-10-15: DGFT suspended ALL exports for MY2023-24 (inverse event: long CANE, short mills). (4) 2024-09-15: DGFT announcement on MY2024-25 policy. For each OGL-release event: compute CANE return vs SPY over T+1 to T+15 trading days. Compute BALRAMCHIN.NS + EIDPARRY.NS equal-weight return over same window. Compute pair P&L: short CANE + long 0.5x each (BALRAMCHIN.NS + EIDPARRY.NS). FX-normalize: use USDINR=X from yfinance to convert INR mill returns to USD.
implementation_notes: DGFT notifications have no API; backtest uses manual event dates from USDA FAS GAIN reports. Indian equity legs trade on NSE; yfinance provides INR-denominated daily adjusted prices. FX (INR/USD) affects pair P&L when mixing USD CANE vs INR mills; normalize using USDINR=X. SB=F front-month rolls create gaps; prefer CANE for clean daily returns in event study. Strategy has bilateral logic: OGL release = short CANE/long mills; OGL ban = long CANE/short mills. Indian market hours differ from US; T+1 lag for US-listed CANE entry after Indian announcement.

name: Illinois Pension Funded Ratio Drift Below 45% -> Short MHD / Long MUC Muni CEF Pair
rule: When the combined Illinois pension system (TRS + SERS + SURS) market-value funded ratio falls below 45% for 3 consecutive quarterly reports: Enter pair trade: short MHD (BlackRock MuniHoldings Fund, national with IL exposure) vs long MUC (BlackRock MuniHoldings California Quality Fund, CA-concentrated). Size: 1 unit short MHD, 1 unit long MUC (dollar-neutral). Hold until: (a) Illinois GO 10y spread to AAA MMD widens >40bp from entry (take profit), (b) Moody's/S&P issues negative watch/downgrade on Illinois GO bonds (exit within 2 days), or (c) 12 weeks elapsed (time-exit). Stop-loss: close if MHD outperforms MUC by >4% from entry (spread tightening signal).
entry_conditions: Illinois TRS + SERS combined market-value funded ratio < 45% for 3 consecutive quarterly CAFR reports
Illinois GO 10y spread to AAA MMD not already at >3x historical mean (avoid blown-out spread entry)
MHD discount to NAV not already >15% (CEF dislocation risk)
exit_conditions: Illinois GO 10y spread to AAA MMD widens >40bp from pair entry date (take-profit)
Moody's or S&P issues negative watch or downgrade on Illinois GO bonds (exit within 2 trading days)
12 calendar weeks elapsed from entry (time-exit)
MHD outperforms MUC by >4% (stop-loss: spread tightening, trade wrong)
Illinois TRS funded ratio recovers above 48% (fundamental invalidation)

data_sources_concrete.prices: MHD, MUC, HYD, MUB, SPY via yfinance
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: Illinois TRS quarterly funded ratio: trsil.org CAFR publications (PDF, manual extraction). Illinois SERS quarterly: srs.illinois.gov CAFR filings. Illinois GO spread: MSRB EMMA (emma.msrb.org) trade prints. Moody's/S&P credit watches: news search. FRED proxy for macro control: ILUR (Illinois unemployment rate).

backtest_approach: Event-study on known Illinois pension/credit stress episodes. Known historical trigger events: (1) 2016-08: Illinois TRS funded ratio 39%; Moody's downgraded IL GO to Baa3 in 2016. (2) 2017-06: Illinois went 736 days without budget; S&P downgraded IL GO to BBB-. (3) 2020-04: COVID market crash pushed pension funded ratio to ~38-40%. (4) 2022-09: Rising rates impacted pension assets. For each event date: compute MHD minus MUC price return over 4-12 week windows. Also compute MHD vs MUB (national muni benchmark) to isolate IL-specific underperformance. Report cumulative return: short MHD / long MUC vs SPY benchmark.
implementation_notes: MUI (BlackRock MuniHoldings Quality Fund II, the originally specified IL-heavy fund) is delisted and unavailable on yfinance. MHD is the closest available proxy (~12-15% IL). Backtester should note that MHD has broader national exposure, diluting the IL-specific signal. HYD (VanEck HY Muni) may be a better IL proxy since HY munis have higher IL concentration. Illinois pension funded ratio requires manual extraction from CAFR PDFs; use known event dates. MHD and MUC are CEFs: use market price not NAV for P&L calculation. Check CEF liquidity: target avg daily volume >$1M for position sizing.

name: LFP Cell Spot Price Crash + Tesla Megapack Price-List Cut -> Short FLNC/STEM Gross Margin
rule: Counter-signal against long_storage / long_clean_energy consensus. Entry: When BOTH conditions are met within the same 45-day window: (a) LFP cell spot price (proxied by Tesla Megapack online price-list ASP or news-confirmed BNEF battery price survey showing >15% QoQ cell cost decline), AND (b) Tesla publicly cuts or removes its listed Megapack price (documented via Wayback Machine snapshot at tesla.com/megapack showing lower $/MWh or price removed from public listing - historically signals active discounting), enter short equal-weight FLNC (50%) + STEM (50%) vs long SHLS (alternative storage-adjacent name less exposed to ASP compression) as a partial hedge. Alternatively, use SPY as the long hedge leg given the counter-signal nature. Exit: (a) 8 weeks elapsed; (b) FLNC or STEM confirms gross margin guide-down at earnings; (c) LFP cell prices stabilize (no further QoQ decline for 2 quarters); (d) Stop-loss: FLNC+STEM basket rises >9% relative to SPY from entry.
entry_conditions: LFP battery cell spot price proxy (BNEF survey, S&P Global CI LFP index, or CATL/BYD quarterly pricing disclosed via earnings) shows >15% QoQ decline
Tesla Megapack public price-list shows a reduction OR Tesla Megapack pricing removed from public listing (documented via Wayback Machine or news coverage)
Both conditions confirmed within a 45-day rolling window
FLNC or STEM trading within 20% of 52-week highs (elevated crowded-long risk)
exit_conditions: 8 weeks elapsed from entry date
FLNC or STEM quarterly earnings confirms gross margin compression >300bp vs prior quarter guide
LFP cell prices stabilize: no further decline for 2 consecutive months
Stop-loss: FLNC+STEM basket rises >9% relative to SPY from entry

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: FLNC, STEM, SHLS, RUN, SPY (daily adjusted close)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: Tesla Megapack price-list archive via Wayback Machine (web.archive.org/web/*/tesla.com/megapack) for price-cut event dates; BNEF Battery Price Survey annual and interim commentary (public summaries); S&P Global Commodity Insights LFP cell spot index (some public data via press releases); FLNC and STEM 10-Q gross margin and ASP disclosures (SEC EDGAR); no FRED series required

backtest_approach: Event-study using documented Tesla Megapack price-list cut dates and confirmed LFP cell price decline episodes as event anchors. Tesla Megapack price-list history via Wayback Machine: (1) Late 2022: Tesla first posted Megapack prices publicly (~.8M/MWh); (2) Q1 2024: Tesla Megapack web price removed from public listing (signals bid discounting); (3) Q3 2024: BNEF reported 20% YoY pack cost decline; (4) 2025 competitive bids showed further ASP compression. For each event date where FLNC and STEM had price history, measure forward returns of short(FLNC+STEM equal-weight) minus long(SPY) at 2, 4, 6, 8 weeks. Cross-check gross margin trajectory in subsequent FLNC/STEM quarterly earnings to confirm the mechanism fired. STEM has history from Oct 2020; FLNC from Oct 2021.
implementation_notes: This is a counter-signal against long_storage consensus; per the strategy spec, trading the specific names (FLNC, STEM) rather than a broad ETF is correct here. SHLS (Shoals Technologies) is included as a possible long hedge leg because its revenue model (BOS electrical components, not the battery cells) is less sensitive to LFP cell ASP compression than FLNC/STEM which are full-system integrators. The key asymmetry: FLNC/STEM lock in project bids 2-4 quarters in advance using forward cell cost assumptions. When spot LFP cell prices drop rapidly, new competitor bids undercut in-flight FLNC/STEM bids, forcing ASP reductions that are not offset by cell cost savings (those savings arrive 2+ quarters later). The BNEF Battery Price Survey is paywalled but annual headline figures are publicly released via press release and academic citing. Proxy: Tesla Megapack ASP cuts are fully observable via Wayback Machine and industry news.

name: EU ETS MSR Intake Confirmation (TNAC >833M + Legislative Signal) -> Long KRBN / KEUA
rule: Two-leg signal: (1) EU Commission annual TNAC report (published each May) confirms Total Number of Allowances in Circulation exceeds the 833M tonne MSR activation threshold. (2) EU Parliament ENVI committee or Council Presidency signals approval/maintenance of the 24% MSR intake rate (Phase 4 mid-term review). On the day BOTH legs are confirmed, enter: long KRBN (KraneShares Global Carbon ETF, ~60% EUA weight). Add KEUA (KraneShares European Carbon, 100% EUA) if available. KRBN not already up >10% in preceding 20 trading days (avoid chasing)

CCR allowances released (confirms compliance demand > supply at CCR price)
NRG and/or VST are not already down >15% from 52-week highs (avoid chasing fallen knife)
Enter short NRG / long CEG at open of day following auction results publication
exit_conditions: Next RGGI quarterly auction date arrives (rolling re-evaluate each quarter)
2 months elapsed from entry (time-exit)
NRG outperforms CEG by >8% from entry (stop-loss: NRG rallying despite RGGI cost)

name: NIC MAP Senior Housing Occupancy Surprise -> VTR/WELL SHOP NOI Drift Long

Hold through 5 trading days after the next VTR/WELL earnings release (whichever comes first). Hedge: short XLRE (equal notional to the VTR+WELL long) for beta neutrality.
entry_conditions: NIC MAP Vision primary-market quarterly occupancy report just released (observable via NIC press release).
AL+IL weighted occupancy q/q change > prior 4-quarter average q/q change by >= 50 bps.
Sell-side SHOP NOI growth consensus for VTR or WELL unchanged for >= 30 days (use IR consensus pages or static analyst models as proxy).
Go long VTR + WELL (equal notional), short XLRE (equal notional), on day-after-NIC-release open.
exit_conditions: 5 trading days after the earlier of VTR or WELL next quarterly earnings release.
Hard stop: close the position if VTR+WELL basket draws down more than 7% vs XLRE hedge.

data_sources_concrete.prices: VTR, WELL, XLRE via yfinance daily OHLCV
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: NIC MAP Vision quarterly senior housing reports (public press release occupancy tables); Census Vintage 65+/80+ population data (FRED: POP65UP, or Census Bureau API); VTR/WELL earnings dates from yfinance .calendar

On surprise events, construct a daily PnL series: long (VTR + WELL)/2 per dollar, short XLRE per dollar, from T+1 open to 5 days post-earnings. Aggregate across events. Compute Sharpe, CAGR (annualized), max drawdown. name: CMS SNF Staffing Rule Rollback -> OHI Tenant Coverage Relief Event Long

Hedge: additionally short XLRE at 50% of OHI notional to dampen broad REIT beta.
exit_conditions: Close after 10 trading days from entry.
Stop-loss: exit if OHI/SBRA spread draws down more than 8% from entry.

data_sources_concrete.fundamental: PACER N.D. name: CBP UFLPA Solar Detention Spike or Entity List Expansion -> Short RUN/SEDG vs TAN

NOVA (Sunnova) is delisted; replace with ARRY (Array Technologies) or ENPH (Enphase) as secondary US solar installer exposure. Hold 20-35 trading days or until exit condition fires.
entry_conditions: CBP UFLPA Statistics Dashboard (monthly release) shows solar HTS-8541 shipment denial rate >35%
OR FLETF Federal Register notice adds major polysilicon/wafer entity to UFLPA Entity List
RUN, SEDG not already down >35% from 52-week high (avoid shorting into capitulation)
TAN not already in confirmed bear-market decline (price below 200-day MA by >15%)
exit_conditions: CBP denial rate drops below 20% in following month (enforcement easing)
US Congress passes UFLPA solar carve-out or safe harbor legislation
RUN or SEDG issues 8-K confirming alternate module supply chain (UFLPA-clean)
Position held 35 trading days (time stop)
Short basket down >25% from entry (profit take)

name: stETH Curve Depeg + EigenLayer TVL Drawdown -> Short COIN Long IBIT BTC-Dominance Rotation
rule: Counter-signal: when ETH-USD underperforms BTC-USD by more than 5% over a rolling 5-day window AND COIN has had positive returns YTD (i.e., the 'long crypto equity' consensus is crowded), short COIN and go long IBIT in equal notional for a 10-trading-day hold. The stETH/ETH depeg trigger (>50bps on Curve pool) serves as the fundamental catalyst confirmation; approximate it via the ETH/BTC ratio breaking below its 50-day moving average as a tradable proxy (stETH depeg historically co-occurs with ETH/BTC ratio breakdown). This is a counter-signal to the crowded long-crypto-equity/long-BTC basket; structure: short COIN, long IBIT (both in equal notional), benchmark vs SPY.
entry_conditions: ETH-USD 5-day return minus BTC-USD 5-day return < -5% (ETH underperforms BTC by 5% in 5 trading days).
ETH-USD / BTC-USD ratio breaks below its 50-day moving average.
COIN cumulative return over the prior 60 trading days > 0 (crowded long condition).
Enter: short COIN, long IBIT, equal notional, at next day open.
exit_conditions: Hold 10 trading days, then exit.
Stop-loss: if IBIT minus COIN spread draws down more than 8% from entry, close all.
Profit target: if spread exceeds +12% within 10 days, close early.

Signal: (1) ETH-USD 5d return minus BTC-USD 5d return < -5%; (2) ETH/BTC ratio below 50-DMA; (3) COIN 60d return > 0. Validate against known analog events: May 2022 stETH depeg (ETH/BTC ratio collapse), Nov 2022 FTX collapse (BTC dominance spike), and any 2024-2025 ETH underperformance periods. 2022-11-09: FTX collapse, BTC dominance spike, ETH underperformance

The COIN short is the alpha source; IBIT long is for crypto-beta hedge (not sector-neutral).

name: SFDR Article 9 → Article 8 Downgrade Wave → Short ICLN/TAN, Long EU Transition Utilities
rule: Counter-signal pair trade. When triggered, enter short ICLN and short TAN in equal dollar weights, and long an equal-weight basket of EOAN.DE + IBE.MC (EU transition utilities) as the hedge. Hold for 10-15 trading sessions or until net pair P&L exceeds +12% (take profit) or -8% (stop-loss), whichever comes first.

Trigger dates identifiable from Morningstar SFDR quarterly reviews, asset-manager press releases, or ESMA national NCA fund classification statistics
ICLN is trading above its 20-day SMA (not entering into an existing drawdown)
No major positive clean energy legislative event in prior 10 days (e.g., IRA amendment)
exit_conditions: 10-15 trading sessions elapsed from entry (time stop)
Net pair P&L exceeds +12% from entry (take profit)
Net pair P&L falls below -8% from entry (stop-loss)
ESMA issues formal guidance reversing or pausing SFDR reclassification requirements

2023-Q1: Continued downgrade wave, Amundi and BNP Paribas AM announced reclassifications

EU utility names (EOAN.DE, IBE.MC) are the long hedge; use USD-denominated return (yfinance returns EUR-denominated prices — backtester must account for EUR/USD FX).

Exit on: (a) CPUC rejects or delays subsequent AL series, (b) EIX or VST issues negative forward guidance revision, (c) 180 calendar days elapsed (time stop), (d) spread to SPY is +20% (profit take).

CAISO LCR Technical Study flags Aliso Canyon sub-area shortfall
EIX not already up >15% YTD at entry (avoid chasing)
VST not in active regulatory investigation by FERC or CPUC at entry
exit_conditions: CPUC issues ruling substantially rejecting or deferring Aliso Canyon BESS RA program
EIX or VST earnings print with negative BESS capacity revenue revision
180 calendar days elapsed (time stop)
EIX+VST pair up >20% vs SPY (profit take)

name: CATL Sodium-Ion BESS Share Inflection: Short ALB, Long FLNC Pair

Enter pair short ALB / long FLNC at equal dollar notional. Hold 60-90 days. Exit when lithium carbonate spot recovers >10% from the trough OR CATL sodium-ion shipments quarter-over-quarter show a deceleration in their investor presentations.
entry_conditions: China sodium-ion stationary BESS share crosses 8% of awarded MWh per CNESA quarterly data (proxy: CATL shipment guidance + ALB/SQM earnings commentary on demand)
China battery-grade lithium carbonate spot price declines >15% over 60 calendar days (proxy via FRED series PIORECUSDQ or ALB quarterly volume guidance cuts)
ALB or SQM revenue guidance cut or sell-side downgrade cluster in trailing 30 days
exit_conditions: Lithium carbonate spot price recovers >10% from measured trough
CATL sodium-ion shipment guidance decelerates quarter-over-quarter
90-day maximum holding period

+10% adverse move on short position (stop loss)

name: TSA Throughput Decel + Jet Fuel Crack + XLY Breadth → JBLU Short
rule: A triple-confirmation signal triggers a short JBLU position: (1) TSA daily checkpoint throughput 4-week rolling YoY growth decelerates by more than 5 percentage points versus the prior 4-week average, (2) the WTI-kerosene jet fuel crack spread (DJFUELUSGULF minus DCOILWTICO) is above its trailing 2-year average plus $3/bbl, AND (3) the percentage of XLY S&P 500 components trading above their 50-day moving average falls below 40%. When all three confirm simultaneously, short JBLU at close. Hold until TSA YoY reaccelerates above the signal threshold (+5pp recovery) OR crack spread falls below 2-year average OR XLY breadth recovers above 55%, whichever comes first. Hard stop: +20% adverse move on JBLU.

WTI-kerosene jet fuel crack spread > 2-year trailing average + $3/bbl (FRED: DJFUELUSGULF minus DCOILWTICO)
Percentage of XLY components above 50-DMA < 40% (computed from yfinance daily prices)
exit_conditions: TSA 4-week YoY reaccelerates: growth recovers to within 0pp of prior-month level
Jet fuel crack spread falls to or below 2-year trailing average
XLY breadth recovers above 55% of components above 50-DMA
Stop-loss: JBLU moves +20% adverse from entry

data_sources_concrete.prices: JBLU, LUV, ALK, XLY + XLY constituents, SPY via yfinance

backtest_approach: Build daily time-series of all three indicator variables from 2020-01-01 to present. TSA throughput: load historical CSV, compute 4-week rolling YoY, detect >5pp deceleration. Crack spread: FRED daily series, compute 2-year rolling mean + $3/bbl threshold. XLY breadth: daily from yfinance, compute % of current XLY constituents above 50-DMA. Signal fires on first day all three conditions are simultaneously met. Short JBLU at signal date close; exit on first condition clearing or stop. Compute per-trade PnL, aggregate Sharpe, CAGR, max drawdown vs SPY benchmark. Note: COVID period (2020-2021) will show strong TSA decel signal — include but flag as an outlier period; sensitivity-test 2022+ only.
implementation_notes: TSA historical data requires downloading CSV from tsa.gov (backtester should cache locally). URL: https://www.tsa.gov/coronavirus/passenger-throughput (public, free, no API key). DJFUELUSGULF is a weekly FRED series (Wednesday observation); forward-fill to daily. DCOILWTICO is daily. XLY constituent list changes over time; use current constituent list as a static proxy for simplicity (survivorship bias acceptable given XLY rebalance is minor). COVID period (March 2020 - June 2021) will generate a prolonged short signal — this is valid as an out-of-sample stress test but should be reported separately. JBLU is the primary target (highest leisure/ULCC mix, no corporate premium cushion, no Spirit merger revenue synergies post-block). LUV is secondary if JBLU liquidity issues. name: CARB Post-2030 Cap-and-Trade Tightening: Short VLO vs Long MPC/PSX Pair on Rulemaking Trigger
rule: Monitor CARB Cap-and-Trade rulemaking docket (ww2.arb.ca.gov/our-work/programs/cap-and-trade-program) for workshop deck releases or draft regulation publications indicating post-2030 cap trajectory tightening above 45% reduction from 1990 levels. CCA futures proxy: confirm directional signal using LCFS credit price levels (Bloomberg or EPA CITSS data) as corroboration — if LCFS credits spike >10% within 5 days of CARB announcement, strengthen confidence. Hold 4-8 weeks. Exit on CARB regulatory pause/delay announcement or when relative spread (VLO - MPC/PSX basket) reverts to entry level.

CCA futures (ICE) or LCFS credits reprice >10% upward within 5 trading days of CARB release
VLO PADD 5 refining throughput confirms >200kbpd CA exposure in most recent 10-Q
Enter short VLO / long MPC+PSX equal-weight basket within 3 days of CARB trigger
exit_conditions: 8-week maximum hold from entry
CARB announces delay or rollback of post-2030 tightening (regulatory risk reversal)
VLO-MPC/PSX spread narrows to within 2% of entry (pair mean-reversion)
Stop-loss: VLO outperforms MPC/PSX basket by >10% from entry (pair moves against)

name: ETH ETF NAV Discount + High Funding Rate: Short COIN (Counter-Signal vs Long Crypto)
rule: Counter-signal vs long-crypto consensus. When: (a) aggregate ETHA + FETH 3-day average closing price falls below ETHA+FETH ETH-implied NAV (computed as ETH-USD * shares_outstanding_ratio, proxied by ETHA_close/ETH-USD_close rolling ratio) by >25bps for 3 consecutive sessions, AND (b) ETH funding rate (proxied by FETH-ETHA spread momentum or Coinglass 8h annualized data) is still above 15% annualized — enter: short COIN equity (100% of notional). This is a defensive rotation to cash (no long-BTC hedge since both tend to fall together). Hold until ETHA premium returns to flat (within 10bps of NAV) AND ETH-USD 10-day momentum turns positive. Approximate proxy trigger: use ETHA_close < 0.9975 * (ETH-USD * fixed_ratio) for 3 days.

FETH same condition (confirms signal across two issuers)
ETH-USD 10-day momentum still positive (crowded longs not yet capitulated)

Short COIN only - no long-BTC or long-IBIT hedge

AND ETH-USD 10-day momentum turns negative (capitulation confirmed - cover)
Stop-loss: cover if COIN rises >15% from entry (thesis wrong)
Or hold max 4 weeks (20 trading days)

name: Retail Crowding Exhaustion: VIX Term Structure Flat + ARKK Inflow Spike -> Long VIXY / Short QQQ

exit_conditions: ^VIX spikes >30% absolute from entry level (take profit on VIXY leg)
6-week maximum hold from entry

name: USITC Section 337 Final Determination LEO / CDO: Short Named US-Listed Semi Respondent vs SOXX

Close at 45-day mark regardless of outcome

name: MAS Semi-Annual MPS Hawkish Surprise: Short EWS + Short Singapore REITs (Counter Asia Carry)

Hold 10 trading days. Exit fully on day 10. Position size: equal-weight EWS vs SREIT basket, dollar-neutral.
entry_conditions: MAS Monetary Policy Statement release day (April or October MPS)
MAS holds or steepens S$NEER slope when OIS/SGD forwards implied easing (hawkish surprise); OR simplified: enter on MPS day for event study
Entry at open on MPS release day
exit_conditions: Exit all positions at close on day +10 (trading days) after MPS
Hard stop: +5% adverse move on EWS position exits immediately

name: PTAB IPR Institution on NVO Semaglutide Patents: Long LLY / Short NVO Pair
rule: Monitor USPTO PTAB E2E database (developer.uspto.gov/ptab-api) for IPR petitions against Novo Nordisk semaglutide Orange Book patents (US 8,536,122; US 10,335,462; US 11,376,242 and related formulation/dosing claims). Institution decision date confirmed via USPTO PTAB case number lookup

exit_conditions: Exit at close on day +63 (trading days) from institution decision
If PTAB Final Written Decision cancels patent before day 63: extend hold to day 126 then exit

Hard stop: if pair moves >15% against the trade (long LLY / short NVO), exit at next open

name: CFTC ETH Commodity Jurisdiction Assertion: Long ETHA (or ETH-USD) / Short COIN Pair
rule: Trigger: CFTC publishes formal jurisdictional assertion over ETH as a commodity — defined as ANY of: (a) CFTC enforcement order citing ETH as commodity under CEA 1a(9), (b) CFTC Chair or Commissioner formal speech before Congress or in published remarks explicitly asserting exclusive CFTC jurisdiction over spot ETH, (c) CFTC no-action letter protecting ETH staking from SEC enforcement. On trigger day: enter long ETHA (spot ETH ETF) and simultaneously enter short COIN (Coinbase Global) beta-weighted 1.5x notional (i.e., short COIN notional = 1.5 * long ETHA notional, to neutralize COIN's ETH price beta). Hold 30 trading days. Exit at close on day +30.
entry_conditions: CFTC publishes formal press release, order, or formal Chair testimony asserting ETH-as-commodity jurisdiction under CEA 1a(9)
Verify on cftc.gov press release RSS feed or CFTC.gov/LawRegulation/Enforcement docket
Enter at open on day after CFTC publication (or same day if publication is pre-market)
Beta-weight: short COIN at 1.5x ETHA notional (COIN historical ETH beta ~0.6-0.8, so 1.5x ~ beta-neutral)
exit_conditions: Exit at close on trading day +30 from entry
If SEC issues counter-announcement claiming ETH is a security within 5 trading days of CFTC ruling: close all positions at next open
Hard stop: if pair moves >15% against trade (ETHA falls + COIN rises), close all at next open

data_sources_concrete.prices: JKS, CSIQ, FSLR via yfinance (all available 2010+)

backtest_approach: Time-series signal backtest: construct monthly signal from PVInfoLink module ASP history (2014-present; free weekly data available for 2019+; for earlier period use BNEF Solar Module Index proxy or JKS/CSIQ gross margin trend as alternate signal). Signal = 1 (short JKS+CSIQ, long FSLR) when estimated module ASP has been below estimated breakeven for 3+ weeks; signal = -1 or 0 otherwise. Backtester can proxy pre-2019 signal by using JKS/CSIQ gross margin trend: when TTM gross margin is declining QoQ for 2+ quarters and inventory days rising, use that as signal trigger. FSLR is the best long leg: US utility-scale focus with long-dated fixed-price ASP contracts insulates it from spot mono-PERC price. JKS and CSIQ have clean yfinance data from 2010. Avoid including 2020-2021 pandemic period in primary backtest due to supply chain distortion. name: FSLR Backlog ASP/Spot Spread > 200% + Cancellation Rate Inflection -> Short FSLR (Counter-Signal)
rule: When (1) global solar module spot price (PVInfoLink mono-PERC) sustains below $0.12/W for >= 8 consecutive weeks AND (2) FSLR most-recent 10-Q reported backlog ASP is >= $0.28/W (implying spread > 133%), AND (3) FSLR reported trailing-12-month cancellation rate exceeds 10% OR FSLR book-to-bill < 0.90 in most recent quarter, then go short FSLR at next open. Hold for 10 calendar weeks (50 trading days). Stop-loss: cover if FSLR rises more than 12% from entry. Profit target: cover if FSLR falls 25% from entry.
entry_conditions: PVInfoLink module spot price < $0.12/W for >= 8 consecutive weeks
FSLR 10-Q backlog ASP >= $0.28/W (spot-to-ASP spread > 133%)
FSLR trailing-12M cancellation rate > 10% OR book-to-bill < 0.90 per most recent quarter
Enter short FSLR at next open after all three conditions met
exit_conditions: Hold 50 trading days (10 calendar weeks)
Stop-loss: cover if FSLR +12% from entry
Profit target: cover if FSLR -25% from entry

Cross-reference with contemporaneous PVInfoLink spot price (use quarterly BNEF/PVInfoLink summary for historical reconstruction; spot below $0.10-0.12 was reached in late 2023 and 2024). Flag quarters where all three conditions trigger. Measure FSLR return from 10-Q filing date over next 50 trading days vs SPY. Counter-signal against long-FSLR thesis: confirm negative excess return during high-spread quarters. Supplement with option-implied vol analysis around earnings (put spread entry for elevated vol events).

2024-Q1 module spot reached $0.09/W (BNEF), FSLR backlog ASP at $0.31/W

implementation_notes: This is a counter_signal strategy (counters: long_FSLR, long_US_solar_fab). FSLR broad-basket targets are intentionally NOT used here - the mechanism implicates FSLR specifically via its unique long-dated contracted backlog model; other solar names (ENPH, SEDG) are module-price beneficiaries or are not backlog-model businesses. PVInfoLink historical spot data pre-2020 may require manual reconstruction from trade press; BloombergNEF provides free quarterly summaries sufficient for signal dating. FSLR 10-Q backlog ASP has been disclosed since ~2013; treat pre-2013 as unavailable. Cancellation rate was not always disclosed before 2021; use book-to-bill < 0.90 as primary proxy for 2013-2021 period. bt_feasibility=4: all data free or reconstructible; FSLR specific-name target is correct.

name: NTSB Major Rail Derailment Investigation -> Short Named Class I Carrier vs Long Peer Basket
rule: When NTSB opens a major investigation (formal docket with DCA/RRD prefix, Go-Team dispatched) into a Class I rail derailment within 7 days of the incident, short the named carrier at next open (T+1) after the NTSB docket publication date, and simultaneously go long an equal-weighted basket of the other US-listed Class I carriers (if NSC is named: long UNP+CSX+CP+CNI equally weighted; if UNP: long NSC+CSX+CP+CNI; etc.). Hold for 60 trading days (12 calendar weeks). Stop-loss: exit if named carrier outperforms peer basket by more than 8% from entry. Exit if named carrier underperforms peer basket by more than 20% (take profit).
entry_conditions: NTSB opens major investigation docket (DCA/RRD prefix) for a Class I rail derailment
Go-Team dispatch confirmed on NTSB press release (ntsb.gov/news)
Named carrier identified from NTSB incident report
Entry at T+1 open (next trading day after NTSB major investigation announcement)
Short named carrier, Long equal-weighted basket of other US-listed Class I carriers
exit_conditions: Hold 60 trading days (12 calendar weeks)
Stop-loss: exit if named carrier outperforms peer basket by >= 8%
Profit target: exit if named carrier underperforms peer basket by >= 20%
Force exit at next earnings if carrier reports > $500M reserve charge (confirms thesis; harvest gains)

data_sources_concrete.fundamental: NTSB Surface Accident Database / CAROL Query (data.ntsb.gov/carol-main-public, free); filter to RailroadAccident mode, major-investigation flag; cross-reference with NTSB press releases at ntsb.gov/news; FRA Office of Railroad Safety emergency orders (railroads.dot.gov, free); SEC 10-Q ASC 450 loss-contingency reserve disclosures for named carrier

For each event: compute named-carrier return minus equal-weighted-peer-basket return from T+1 open over 60 trading days. Normalize by sector beta (regress on SPY). East Palestine: NSC underperformed UNP/CSX basket by ~15% over 6 months per idea thesis. Report: N events, mean pair return, hit rate, Sharpe.

2021-09 UNP Loup City NE derailment (NTSB investigation)

Peer basket includes only US-listed Class I carriers (CP and CNI are Canadian-listed with US ADRs; use CP and CNI via yfinance which has both). East Palestine is the cleanest analog with full financial disclosure available. Pre-2015 event sample may be thin; backtester should note if N < 5. Small sample caveat: Class I major NTSB investigations are rare (1-3 per decade at severity level triggering significant equity impact). If NTSB investigation database search returns < 3 clear events, supplement with FRA major-accident investigations where carrier-specific reserve charges exceeded $100M. bt_feasibility=4: all data sources are free and programmatic; primary analog well-documented.

name: NTSB DOT-117 Hazmat Finding -> PHMSA HM-251 Retrofit Acceleration -> TRN/GBX Backlog Surge Long
rule: Entry: Within 20 trading days of an NTSB safety recommendation citing a DOT-117 tank-car design failure mode (puncture resistance, thermal protection, or outlet valve) published in NTSB CAROL database, enter long equal-weight TRN + GBX at close. Confirm that PHMSA has either (a) issued an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking or a Federal Register notice in response, or (b) a floor vote on a rail-safety bill is scheduled within 90 days. Exit: (1) 20 weeks after entry; or (2) if TRN or GBX individual position draws down >15% from entry price; or (3) if PHMSA issues a no-action letter or congressional action fails.
