Recommendation is on railcar puncture resistance, thermal protection, top/bottom fitting failure, or similar tank-car integrity issue
PHMSA has either issued a Fed Register ANPRM/NPRM in response OR a floor rail-safety vote is expected within 90 days
Enter long TRN + GBX equal-weight at next close after the 20-day confirmation window

Stop-loss: exit any single name position if it draws down >15% from entry
Fundamental exit: PHMSA issues no-action letter, or HM-251 final rule is delayed >12 months past the recommendation

From 2018 onwards, GBX becomes the sole public railcar builder proxy. GATX is a lessor, not a builder, but can serve as confirmation that lessor demand for new cars is rising. Two known event dates give a thin N=2 event study - treat as proof-of-concept; forward signals must confirm via real-time PHMSA Fed Register monitoring. bt_feasibility=3 due to small event count; originality=8 because the NTSB->PHMSA->backlog channel is untracked.

name: USCG MISLE Houston Ship Channel Casualty Cluster -> Inland Tank-Barge Day-Rate Spike -> KEX Long
rule: Entry: When USCG MISLE marine casualty records for the Houston Ship Channel COTP zone show 3+ serious casualties (allisions, collisions, groundings, or significant oil discharges) within any rolling 14-day window—representing a z-score >2 vs. the trailing 12-month daily mean—and the USCG Sector Houston has issued a Marine Safety Information Bulletin imposing one-way traffic, daylight-only, or draft restriction orders, enter long KEX at next-day close. Exit: (1) 6 weeks (30 trading days) after entry; or (2) USCG lifts restrictions and MISLE cluster returns to baseline (no new casualties for 10 consecutive trading days); or (3) KEX draws down >10% from entry.

Casualty count represents z-score >2.0 vs. trailing 12-month daily baseline for that COTP zone
USCG Sector Houston Marine Safety Information Bulletin or Captain-of-the-Port order imposes transit restrictions (one-way, daylight, or draft caps)
KEX price is within 10% of its 52-week high (avoid buying into ongoing fundamental distress)
exit_conditions: Time exit: 30 trading days (6 weeks) from entry
Fundamental exit: USCG lifts all transit restrictions AND no new MISLE casualties on HSC for 10 consecutive trading days
Stop-loss: KEX position down >10% from entry price

For each event, compute daily PnL of long KEX vs. SPY benchmark over 30-trading-day hold window starting t+1. Use KEX adjusted close from yfinance. Supplemental: scan MISLE CSV for all HSC COTP zone incidents 2005-2024 meeting the 3-in-14-day threshold to identify additional analog dates (est. 4-8 events total). Run full event study across all dates. Target: median excess return >5% over hold period, Sharpe>0.7.

MISLE CSV data is updated quarterly with ~6-month lag, so this strategy is better suited to forward event monitoring than a clean quantitative backtest from the CSV alone; the known documented events (ITC fire 2019, fog 2024) are the most reliable backtest seeds. Inland barge day-rate data from Clarksons/Informa requires paid subscription; use KEX stock price as the observable proxy. Two confirmed seeds give N=2 event study; backtester should supplement with any additional HSC events identified in the MISLE CSV to increase N. KEX also has offshore marine exposure (~25% of revenue), so not all KEX moves will be HSC-driven; this is a known noise source.

name: Italian Legge di Bilancio Tobacco Excise Hike -> Short BTI / Long IMB.L Pair
rule: Entry: Each year, when Italy's MEF Draft Budgetary Plan (DBP, due October 15) includes an 'accise tabacchi' line item showing a hike of >5% per pack of 20 cigarettes (confirmed in the Relazione Tecnica annex), enter short BTI and long IMB.L equal notional at the first close after October 15 (or when DBP confirmation is public). Exit: (1) 16 weeks (80 trading days) from entry; or (2) BTI reports Italy/Europe AME revenue beat > 3% vs. consensus; or (3) ADM publishes updated tariffa di vendita showing no change or a rollback; or (4) Either leg draws down >12% from entry.

ADM (adm.gov.it) confirms updated tariffa di vendita implementing the hike
No active BTI profit warning or separate Italy-specific positive catalyst in the prior 30 days

Fundamental exit: BTI Italy/Europe AME revenue beats estimates by >3% OR ADM rolls back or delays the hike
Stop-loss: either leg individually down >12% from entry (close entire pair)

For each event: compute short BTI / long IMB.L pair PnL from t+1 close over 80-trading-day hold. Normalize to equal notional at entry. Compute Sharpe and max-drawdown for the pair. PMI has IQOS pricing power that partially offsets combustible volume declines; BTI does not have a comparable heated-tobacco platform in Italy, making it more vulnerable. IMB.L has minimal Italy exposure (primarily UK, Germany, Spain) making it a reasonable long hedge. Note IMB.L is GBP-denominated; use GBP/USD FX adjustment for USD PnL or trade as ADR if preferred. bt_feasibility=4 because annual DBP excise hike data is publicly visible, BTI segment data is in annual reports, and yfinance data covers both tickers for relevant event windows.

name: OFAC Shadow-Fleet SDN Tranche (>=8 Crude Tankers) -> Long INSW + FRO / Short BDRY
rule: Entry: When the OFAC SDN daily delta CSV (treasury.gov) shows a single-tranche designation of >=8 crude tankers flagged as Russia-evasion shadow fleet vessels (Liberia/Gabon/Comoros/Palau flag, VLCC/Suezmax class, narrative contains 'Russia' or 'petroleum' or 'oil'), enter long INSW + FRO equal-weight and short BDRY at the next-day close. Pair ratio: long INSW 40% + long FRO 40%, short BDRY 20% of notional per leg. Exit: (1) 8 weeks (40 trading days) from entry; or (2) INSW+FRO combined position gains >20%; or (3) Baltic Dirty Tanker Index (BDTI) falls >20% from entry level (macro tanker demand shock); or (4) INSW or FRO individually falls >12% from entry.
entry_conditions: OFAC SDN delta CSV shows >=8 crude tanker designations in a single update targeting Russia-evasion shadow fleet
Designated vessels are VLCC or Suezmax class (>80,000 DWT) with Russia/petroleum narrative in SDN entry
At least one major shipping news outlet (Lloyd's List, TradeWinds) confirms the designation tranche within 24 hours
INSW and FRO share prices are not already up >10% in prior 5 trading days (avoid chasing a prior move)
exit_conditions: Time exit: 40 trading days (8 weeks) from entry
Profit take: long legs (INSW+FRO combined) up >20% from entry
Macro exit: BDTI drops >20% from level at entry (global tanker demand shock overrides supply squeeze)
Stop-loss: INSW or FRO individually down >12% from entry price

data_sources_concrete.prices: INSW, FRO, BDRY, STNG, SPY via yfinance (INSW listed ~2016; FRO 2004+; BDRY ETF 2018+)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: OFAC SDN delta CSV (https://www.treasury.gov/ofac/downloads/sdn_delta.csv, free daily); US Treasury press releases for Russia shipping designations; Baltic Exchange BDTI proxy via BDRY ETF or news reports

Event 2: OFAC Dec 20, 2023 tranche — additional Sovcomflot-linked vessels; use 2023-12-20 as t=0. Event 3: OFAC Feb 23, 2024 tranche — Sovcomflot subsidiaries, ~10 tankers; use 2024-02-23 as t=0. Event 4: OFAC Jan 10, 2025 tranche — largest to date, ~180 vessels (including tankers); use 2025-01-10 as t=0. For each event: compute INSW+FRO equal-weight long vs BDRY short PnL from t+1 close over 40-day window. Also compute INSW+FRO vs SPY for excess return. Track whether INSW/FRO individually beat STNG (partial Russia exposure) as mechanism check. Target: median pair return >8% over hold window, Sharpe>0.7.
implementation_notes: BDRY is an ETF tracking dry-bulk not tankers; it's an imperfect short hedge. If a cleaner short leg is needed, consider STNG (Scorpio Tankers, more Russia-route exposure historically) vs INSW/FRO (all-compliant fleets). The Jan 2025 OFAC tranche was historically large (~180 vessels including non-tanker ships) and may have had different market dynamics; treat it as a separate scenario. INSW was IPO'd ~2016 so the event study only has 4 seeds with varying ticker availability. The SDN delta CSV is machine-readable and amenable to systematic screening. bt_feasibility=4 because all 4 event dates are well-documented public record and yfinance data covers all relevant periods.

name: BTP Retail Subscription Miss -> Italian Bank Sovereign Doom-Loop Short
rule: When MEF publishes final BTP Valore or BTP Italia retail subscription totals showing a raise of <60% vs the comparable prior-issuance-window nominal (or absolute raise <EUR 8B for BTP Valore, <EUR 6B for BTP Italia), enter short ISP.MI (60% weight) and BMPS.MI (40% weight) at next-day open. Hold for 4-10 weeks. Cover when: (a) BTP-Bund 10y spread retraces to within 10bp of pre-event level, OR (b) next MEF government auction bid-to-cover exceeds 1.4x, OR (c) 10-week holding period expires. Use EWI as sector-hedge reference; do not hold through Italian election events.
entry_conditions: MEF Dipartimento del Tesoro final BTP Valore/Italia subscription total published
Subscription nominal < 60% of most recent comparable prior issuance window
OR absolute raise < EUR 8B (BTP Valore) / EUR 6B (BTP Italia)
BTP-Bund 10y spread > 150bp at time of signal (regime filter: elevated stress environment)

Subsequent MEF government bond auction bid-to-cover ratio > 1.4x
10-week maximum holding period from entry date
Hard stop: ISP.MI or BMPS.MI individually rises >8% from entry (position-level stop)

BMPS.MI (Banca Monte dei Paschi) had a massive capital restructuring in 2016-2022 and was government-owned until 2024 partial privatization - price history pre-2022 may be unreliable; consider weighting heavily toward ISP.MI for pre-2022 events. BTP Italia and BTP Valore are distinct instruments but share the retail absorption mechanism; treat both as triggers. FRED BTP-Bund spread is monthly; use daily EWI returns as a higher-frequency Italian risk proxy for exit signaling. ISP.MI (Intesa Sanpaolo) is the cleaner long-history primary name; BMPS.MI is the high-beta tail. This is a counter_signal=true idea (counters long_quality/long_SPY).

name: G7 Price-Cap Attestation Tightening: Short Indian Refiner (Reliance) Long US Refiner Pair

Monitor: EU Official Journal (eur-lex.europa.eu) sanctions updates + US Treasury OFAC FAQs (sanctionssearch.ofac.treas.gov). SIZE: Use 1x gross leverage each side; hedge neutralizes global crack-spread beta. EXIT: Cover after 8 weeks OR when Urals/Brent discount widens back above -/bbl (reversal signal), whichever comes first. Hard stop: +12% on the short leg (RELIANCE.NS) against the pair.
entry_conditions: EU Official Journal publishes new Attestation Regulation (Regulation amending EU/833/2014) tightening certification requirements for G7-service providers in same calendar week as OFAC designation of >=2 Russian crude trading intermediaries
Urals/Brent spot discount at time of trigger is tighter than -/bbl (confirming crack-spread margin compression thesis is live)
RELIANCE.NS within 10% of 52-week high (ensuring margin is not already priced in)
exit_conditions: Hold 8 weeks from entry (base case horizon)
Urals/Brent spread widens back beyond -/bbl (reversal of compression signal)
Hard stop: short RELIANCE.NS leg +12% adverse (pair unwind)

data_sources_concrete.fundamental: DCOILBRENTEU (Brent spot) via FRED; Urals discount approximated via DCOILBRENTEU minus EIA data on Russian crude import cost; OFAC/EU designation event dates collected manually from public sources

For each event: compute RELIANCE.NS - VLO pair return over [0, +40 trading days]. Also compute excess return vs SPY. With N=3 events, report mean/median pair return and t-stat. Note: SRS.MI (Saras) was delisted in 2024 via Vitol acquisition — RELIANCE.NS is used as primary mechanism proxy. Use RIGD.L (LSE-listed GDR) for pre-2022 coverage if needed.
implementation_notes: SRS.MI (Saras) was the original thesis instrument but was acquired by Vitol in late 2024 and is delisted from Borsa Italiana. RELIANCE.NS is the best remaining liquid proxy: 30-40% of crude inputs are Russian-origin, high analyst coverage. RIGD.L (GDR on LSE) can substitute for USD-denominated exposure. Urals discount data is not freely available intraday; Argus/Platts spot quotes require subscription. Weekly EIA import data and monthly Indian PPAC reports serve as free proxies. Only 3 clean trigger events exist in 2022-2025 window — low statistical power; results directional only. bt_feasibility=3 due to: thin event count, manual trigger identification, and Indian NSE liquidity caveats for backtesting.

name: Lloyd's JWC Listed-Area Expansion -> Long Specialty Reinsurer Pair (RNR/EG) War-Risk Premium Hardening
rule: TRIGGER: Lloyd's Joint War Committee publishes a Listed Areas of Enhanced Risk update adding new geographic zones related to Russia-Black-Sea-Baltic corridors OR Red Sea/Bab-el-Mandeb, AND within 14 days the International Group of P&I Clubs publishes a circular signaling restriction or withdrawal of cover for shadow-fleet voyages on affected routes. Monitor: lloyds.com/market-resources/market-directives (free), igpandi.org circulars (free). ENTRY: Buy RNR and EG equal-weight within 3 business days of dual trigger. SIZE: Equal notional per leg; total gross = 2x vs SPY benchmark. EXIT: Sell after 12 weeks (base holding period for reinsurance-cycle transmission) OR if VIX spikes above 40 (systemic risk-off that would overwhelm specialty premium tailwind), whichever is first. Counter-signal: this trade is designed as a hedge against broad SPY risk-off since RNR/EG historically decouple from SPY on geopolitical war-risk events.
entry_conditions: Lloyd's JWC Listed Areas document shows new geographic addition to Enhanced Risk zones (check JWC archives at lloyds.com)
IG P&I Clubs circular issued within 14 days of JWC update, explicitly referencing shadow-fleet or above-cap Russian/sanctioned-vessel cover restrictions
Marine war-risk additional premium (AP) news reports show >=200bps increase on affected routes (qualitative confirmation via Lloyd's List, TradeWinds headlines)
exit_conditions: Hold 12 weeks from entry (base case reinsurance renewal cycle)
VIX close above 40 (systemic dislocation overwhelms specialty mechanism — exit both legs)
JWC issues Listed Areas removal/narrowing update (reversal trigger)

data_sources_concrete.prices: RNR, EG, ACGL, SPY — all via yfinance
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: VIX via yfinance (^VIX); JWC event dates and IG P&I Clubs circular dates collected manually from public archives

backtest_approach: Event-study design using identifiable JWC Listed Area expansion dates. Seed events: (1) Feb 24 2022 — Russia invades Ukraine, JWC Black Sea expansion (3 Mar 2022); (2) Dec 19 2023 — JWC expands Bab-el-Mandeb/Red Sea after Houthi attacks on shipping; (3) Mar 2024 — JWC updates Red Sea zone after IG P&I Clubs Feb 2024 circular on shadow fleet. For each event: compute equal-weight RNR+EG portfolio return over [0, +60 trading days]. Compute excess return vs SPY over same window to measure counter-signal quality. With N=3 events report mean pair return, Sharpe estimate, and max drawdown. Counter-signal: ACGL included as robustness check (similar specialty reinsurance exposure).
implementation_notes: This is explicitly a counter-signal vs long_SPY: RNR and EG provide marine war-risk premium exposure that tends to appreciate when SPY is pressured by geopolitical events. ACGL is included as a benchmark/robustness ticker (Arch Capital, also heavy specialty reinsurance). RE (Everest Re old ticker) is now EG (Everest Group) after 2023 rebrand — use EG throughout. JWC event dates may lag actual risk deterioration by days; use news-based confirmation to refine entry timing. Reinsurance premium hardening takes 1-2 renewal cycles to flow through to EPS — the 12-week horizon captures the equity re-rating phase, not the actual earnings impact. N=3 events provides directional evidence only; recommend forward paper-trading before live deployment.

name: ICC IBC 2021/2024 Tall Mass Timber State Adoption Acceleration -> Long WY/LPX/RYN Basket
rule: Entry: When ICC state adoption tracker (iccsafe.org) shows the cumulative count of US states/jurisdictions formally adopting IBC 2021 or later (which includes Types IV-A/B/C tall mass timber provisions up to 18 stories) crosses a 6-month rolling high for the first time in that calendar year, AND WoodWorks annual project count shows >25% YoY growth in announced mass-timber projects, enter long equal-weight WY + LPX + RYN at next-month-end close. Signal is annual — check each January after ICC publishes its state adoption survey and WoodWorks publishes its annual report (typically Q1). Exit: (1) 9 months (189 trading days) from entry; or (2) US housing starts fall below 900k annualized SAAR for 2 consecutive months (structural demand collapse); or (3) any single position draws down >15% from entry.
entry_conditions: ICC state adoption count for IBC 2021+ (tall mass timber provisions) crosses 6-month rolling high
WoodWorks annual mass-timber project count shows YoY growth >25%
US housing starts (FRED: HOUST) are above 1.0M SAAR in the most recent month
Signal checked annually in Q1 after both ICC and WoodWorks annual reports are published
exit_conditions: Time exit: 189 trading days (~9 months) from entry
Macro exit: US housing starts (HOUST) falls below 900k SAAR for 2 consecutive monthly prints
Stop-loss: any single position (WY, LPX, or RYN) down >15% from entry price

data_sources_concrete.prices: WY, LPX, RYN, WOOD, SPY via yfinance (all tickers available from 2004+; WY back to 1999)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: ICC state adoption map (iccsafe.org, free annual survey); WoodWorks mass-timber project database (woodworks.org, free, annual report Q1); FRED HOUST (US Housing Starts, monthly); FRED WPUSI (US Producer Price Index lumber)

backtest_approach: Threshold-crossover event study using annual IBC adoption milestones as signal dates. Use the following proxy entry dates based on documented ICC/WoodWorks milestones: t=0: 2022-03-01 (ICC 2021 IBC formally adopted by first wave of ~12 states; WoodWorks 2022 report showed 40% YoY project growth); t=0: 2023-02-01 (ICC adoption expanded to 20+ states; WoodWorks 2023 report showed 35% YoY growth); t=0: 2024-02-01 (ICC adoption reached 25+ states; WoodWorks 2024 reported 1,963 projects). For each seed date, compute equal-weight WY+LPX+RYN daily PnL over 189-trading-day hold vs SPY benchmark. Also compute vs WOOD ETF (iShares Global Timber & Forestry) as sector benchmark. Use FRED HOUST to confirm housing-start threshold was above 1M SAAR at each entry. Cross-check WY/LPX/RYN revenue growth in subsequent quarterly earnings to verify mechanism.
implementation_notes: This is a slow-moving, structurally-driven signal — not a daily-frequency event study. Annual signal with 9-month hold means only ~3-4 non-overlapping backtest windows are available since 2022. bt_feasibility=3 due to thin event count and the need for manual ICC/WoodWorks data lookup. LPX (Louisiana-Pacific) is primarily OSB/siding, not pure CLT; exposure is via broader engineered-wood demand. RYN is a REIT timberland owner, less direct than WY's manufacturing integration. WY is the highest-fidelity ticker: owns 11M acres US timberland, runs CLT JV, and has direct softwood lumber/engineered wood products exposure. WOOD ETF can be used as benchmark to isolate alpha from the IBC adoption signal vs. generic timber.

name: GSA Buy Clean GWP Threshold Tightening for Cement (>10%) -> Short CX+EXP+MLM / Long STLD+WY
rule: Entry: When GSA publishes a Buy Clean program bulletin (gsa.gov/buyclean) showing the portland cement Global Warming Potential threshold tightened by >10% vs. the prior quarter's limit AND the EPA Federal Buy Clean Initiative confirms the revised limit applies to new federal procurements within 90 days, enter short equal-weight CX + EXP + MLM (3 longs of the short basket) and long equal-weight STLD + WY (2 longs of the long basket). Notional: 3% per leg short / 3% per leg long (15% gross). Exit: (1) 6 months (126 trading days) from entry; or (2) GSA rolls back or delays the threshold; or (3) any short-side position individually gains >15% (forced cover one leg); or (4) macroeconomic recession signal (FRED USREC = 1).
entry_conditions: GSA Buy Clean program bulletin shows portland cement GWP limit tightened by >10% vs. prior published limit
EPA Federal Buy Clean Initiative confirms the revised limit is effective within 90 days of GSA publication
California DGS Buy Clean California Act (AB 262) compliance threshold is consistent with or more aggressive than GSA (confirms state follow-on risk)
CX, EXP, or MLM has NOT announced a major plant decarbonization capex program in the prior 90 days that could offset the demand loss
exit_conditions: Time exit: 126 trading days (~6 months) from entry
Regulatory exit: GSA rolls back or grants a waiver delaying the threshold beyond 12 months
Short squeeze risk: any single short position up >15% from entry — cover that leg only
Recession exit: FRED USREC indicator = 1 for 2 consecutive months (construction demand collapses across all materials)

data_sources_concrete.prices: CX, EXP, MLM, STLD, NUE, WY, SPY via yfinance (all available 2003+; CX NYSE since 2002)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: GSA Buy Clean program bulletins (https://www.gsa.gov/real-estate/facilities-management/buy-clean, free); EPA Federal Low-Embodied-Carbon Procurement Guidance (epa.gov, free); California DGS Buy Clean California Act compliance data (dgs.ca.gov); FRED USREC recession indicator

backtest_approach: Event study with 2 primary seed dates from the GSA Buy Clean launch and update cycle: Event 1: GSA Buy Clean program launch with initial GWP concrete limits, September 2023 — use 2023-09-15 as t=0. Event 2: GSA Buy Clean GWP threshold tightening update, Q4 2024 (confirm exact date from gsa.gov/buyclean bulletin) — use 2024-10-01 as provisional t=0. For each event: compute short equal-weight (CX+EXP+MLM) vs long equal-weight (STLD+WY) pair PnL from t+1 close over 126-trading-day window. Normalize to equal gross notional. Compute pair Sharpe, max-drawdown. Supplemental: track cement price indices (PPI for cement FRED: WPU133) and structural steel prices to confirm the substitution channel is visible. Supplemental: use MLM/EXP earnings transcript mentions of 'federal procurement' or 'Buy Clean' as mechanism validation. N=2 events is thin; treat as proof-of-concept. Forward signals should monitor GSA quarterly bulletins.
implementation_notes: GSA Buy Clean launched September 2023; prior to that date there are no real historical analogs for this specific trigger. This means the strategy effectively only has live history from 2023, making the backtest extremely thin (N=2). bt_feasibility=3 rather than the idea's stated 3 (consistent) — the data is accessible but the event sample is very small. CX is a Mexico-domiciled company (Cemex) with global operations; US federal procurement is a fraction of revenue, so effect may be small for CX. EXP (Eagle Materials) and MLM (Martin Marietta) are more US-focused. STLD (Steel Dynamics) is ~75% EAF scrap-based steel with ~0.5 tonne CO2/tonne steel vs ~2.0 for blast furnace; clear beneficiary of carbon procurement preference. WY benefits via mass timber displacement of concrete in mid-rise construction. This strategy may be better suited to the Watchlist as a forward-monitor than a historical backtest, but 2 event dates from 2023-2024 are available so attempting the backtest is reasonable.

name: AIA Architecture Billings Index Sustained Contraction -> Duration Long + Construction Short
rule: When AIA Architecture Billings Index prints sub-45 for 3+ consecutive months (based on AIA monthly release date), enter: Long TLT (50% weight) + Long IEF (50% weight) at next-month-open after 3rd consecutive sub-45 print. Simultaneously short BLD (Topbuild Corp, 100% construction-exposed) if price data available. Hold for 4 calendar months. Exit: (a) 4-month holding period expires, OR (b) ABI recovers above 50 for 2 consecutive months. Optional divergence filter (higher Sharpe): only enter if SPY is within 5% of rolling 52-week high AND FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 HY OAS < 400bp at time of signal (late-cycle complacency screen). Counter-signal to long_SPY: long TLT+IEF benefits from the eventual equity drawdown that follows construction cycle roll.
entry_conditions: AIA Architecture Billings Index sub-45 for 3+ consecutive months (from AIA monthly release, aia.org)
Entry at open of first trading day in the month following the 3rd consecutive sub-45 print
Optional: SPY within 5% of rolling 52-week high (late-cycle divergence filter)
Optional: BAMLH0A0HYM2 HY OAS < 400bp (tight credit environment filter)
exit_conditions: 4 calendar months from entry date (primary time exit)
ABI recovers above 50 for 2 consecutive months (construction recovery exit)
Hard stop: TLT + IEF combined position down 8% from entry (rate spike scenario)
For BLD short: cover if BLD rises 12% above entry or 4-month period expires

data_sources_concrete.prices: TLT, IEF, BLD, SPY (yfinance); BLD available 2015-06 onward
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: BAMLH0A0HYM2 (ICE BofA US HY OAS, FRED daily); ABI event seed dates (manually compiled from AIA public reports): 2007-09 (sustained contraction start), 2008-01 (deep contraction), 2020-03 (COVID collapse, ABI ~33 in Apr 2020), 2022-09 (post-hike construction slowdown, sustained through mid-2023); TLNRESCONS (FRED nonresidential construction spending, monthly, confirmation series)

backtest_approach: Event-study with 4 known ABI sustained-contraction trigger dates (Sep-2007, Jan-2008, Mar-2020, Sep-2022). For TLT+IEF long: compute 1M, 2M, 3M, 4M cumulative returns from each trigger date. For BLD short: apply only to Sep-2022 trigger (BLD available from 2015). Compare TLT+IEF combined returns vs SPY over equivalent holding periods (excess return). Apply optional divergence filter retroactively (was SPY near 52w high? Was HY OAS <400bp?) to subset of events. Report: mean and median forward TLT+IEF return, hit rate (% positive), Sharpe estimate using monthly FRED 3-month T-bill as risk-free rate. Note: 2020-03 was COVID shock (anomalous forced risk-off) - flag as potentially unrepresentative.
implementation_notes: AIA ABI is NOT on FRED - it is published monthly at aia.org (Architecture Billings Index). Historical ABI data is available in AIA's annual reports and published research. Backtester must use the pre-compiled event dates above; no API pull available. BLD (Topbuild Corp) IPO was June 2015 - short leg only applicable to 2022-2023 trigger. The compound divergence trigger (ABI sub-45 + SPY near ATH + HY tight) is very rare and may have zero historical occurrences; use simpler ABI sub-45 for 3+ months as primary trigger. TLT/IEF long is the main testable hypothesis; BLD short is supplementary. counter_signal=true, counters long_SPY: duration benefits from eventual equity repricing.

name: HY Credit-Equity Divergence: OAS Widening with SPY Strength -> Short SPY
rule: When FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 (ICE BofA US HY OAS) widens 75+ bps over the trailing 20 trading sessions AND SPY total return over the same 20 sessions is between -2% and +10% (equity complacency / flat-to-up), enter short SPY at next-day open. Size: 1x; benchmark with SH (ProShares Short S&P500) as alternative if preferred. Hold for up to 8 weeks. Exit: (a) 8-week holding period expires, OR (b) BAMLH0A0HYM2 retraces 40+ bps from the trigger level (credit rally = thesis invalidated), OR (c) SPY falls 12% from entry (take partial profit: exit 50% of position). Re-entry: if OAS remains elevated (>75bp above 20-session starting level) after SPY recovers >4% from interim low, re-enter short.
entry_conditions: BAMLH0A0HYM2 (FRED daily) widens >= 75 bps over trailing 20 trading sessions
SPY 20-session total return >= -2% (equity has not yet corrected)
SPY 20-session total return <= +10% (not a parabolic momentum environment)
HY OAS level > 300bp at trigger (not from a very tight base where 75bp move is noise)
exit_conditions: 8-week maximum holding period from entry
BAMLH0A0HYM2 retraces 40+ bps from trigger level (credit divergence resolved, thesis invalid)
SPY down 12% from entry: exit 50% of position (partial profit)
SPY down 20% from entry: exit remaining position (full profit target)
Hard stop: SPY up 6% from entry (thesis wrong, cut loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: SPY, SH, IEF, LQD (yfinance)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: BAMLH0A0HYM2 (ICE BofA US HY OAS, FRED, daily from 1997-01-02 - use direct FRED CSV download or fredapi for full history, NOT pandas_datareader which truncates); BAMLC0A0CM (IG OAS, FRED, for HY-IG spread differential crosscheck)

backtest_approach: Algorithmic rolling-window backtest. Load FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 daily series (1997-01-02 onward) and SPY daily returns. For each trading day t: compute OAS_change = OAS[t] - OAS[t-20], SPY_return = SPY[t]/SPY[t-20]-1. Signal = 1 if OAS_change >= 0.75 AND SPY_return >= -0.02 AND SPY_return <= 0.10 AND OAS[t] > 3.0. Enter short SPY at open of t+1; track 5, 10, 20, 30, 40 trading day forward returns. Apply exit rules (8-week, credit-retrace, SPY stop). Compute annualized Sharpe, CAGR, max drawdown on the strategy vs buy-and-hold SPY. Historical signal events expected: ~8-15 distinct episodes (2007-08 GFC approach, 2011 EU debt crisis, 2015 China/commodity, 2018 Q4 Powell pivot, 2020 COVID onset, 2022 rate-hike episode, 2025 tariff episode).
implementation_notes: CRITICAL: Use direct FRED API (fredapi package) or FRED CSV download (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=BAMLH0A0HYM2) for full history from 1997. pandas_datareader FRED reader returns only ~3 years of data for this series. The full series has data from 1997-01-02 and covers all major credit cycles. Note: not all HY widening episodes are true divergence (some are concurrent equity drops); the -2% floor on SPY return is the critical filter. The SPY stop at +6% from entry is aggressive - validate in backtesting whether a wider stop (e.g., +9%) improves Sharpe without sacrificing win rate. counter_signal=true, counters long_SPY. SH (ProShares Short S&P500, inception 2006) is the implementation vehicle for investors who cannot short; include in tickers for forward reference.

name: FINRA Margin Debt 3-Year Peak -> Long IEF / Short SPY Deleveraging Hedge
rule: TRIGGER: FINRA monthly Margin Statistics (published with ~4-6 week lag for prior month) show: (1) YoY growth rate of total margin debit balances hits a new 3-year high, AND (2) absolute margin debt exceeds the prior cycle peak level. Both conditions must be met in the SAME monthly print. ENTRY: On the second business day after FINRA publishes the triggering monthly report, enter long IEF (7-10yr Treasury ETF) and short SPY in equal notional. SIZE: 1x gross leverage per leg (dollar-neutral pair). EXIT: Unwind after 16 weeks (base case) OR when SPY retraces more than 15% from the signal-month close (profit target on the short leg). Hard stop: pair P&L worse than -8% (IEF + SPY short combined).
entry_conditions: FINRA Margin Statistics monthly release shows YoY growth rate of total margin debit balances at new 3-year high
Absolute margin debt (in $ billions) exceeds the prior cycle peak level
SPY is within 5% of its all-time high at trigger date (confirms leverage at euphoric levels, not recovering from crash)
exit_conditions: Hold 16 weeks from entry date (base case)
SPY has declined more than 15% from its close on the signal month (profit target for short leg)
Hard stop: combined pair P&L reaches -8%

data_sources_concrete.prices: SPY, IEF, TLT, QQQ -- all via yfinance
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FINRA Margin Statistics monthly (free download at finra.org/investors); FRED BOGZ1FL663067003Q as quarterly crosscheck

IEF (7-10yr) preferred over TLT (20yr+) for lower duration risk. The 3-year high YoY growth condition fires roughly once per major cycle (historically every 4-7 years). SPY-within-5%-of-ATH condition prevents false positives during recovery rallies. BOGZ1FL663067003Q (quarterly FRED flow of funds) available as a free confirmation series.

name: TrendForce HBM/DRAM Contract Price Rollover -> Short Micron (MU) Margin Compression

Hard stop: MU +15% from short entry price.

MU forward P/E is above 15x at entry (market still anchored to boom thesis)
MU within 20% of its 52-week high (downside room exists before miss is priced)

8 weeks from entry if no earnings falls in that window
Hard stop: MU +15% from short entry (DRAM cycle extended further than expected)

data_sources_concrete.fundamental: TrendForce DRAM/HBM quarterly pricing updates (free summaries at trendforce.com/news); FRED PCU334413334413 (semiconductor PPI monthly proxy); MU earnings dates from yfinance calendar

Short MU carries significant event risk (positive AI demand surprise); hard stop at +15% essential.

name: Quarter-End JPY Cross-Currency Basis Spike → Long FXY
rule: Enter long FXY on the 7th calendar day before each quarter-end date (March 31, June 30, September 30, December 31). If the 7th calendar day falls on a weekend/holiday, enter on the prior trading day. Confirm entry only if DEXJPUS (USD/JPY spot from FRED) is within 5% of its 60-day moving average (i.e., not in extreme BOJ-intervention territory). Exit long FXY on the 2nd trading day of the new quarter (i.e., after the quarter-end date). Position size: 100% of allocated capital. No leverage. Benchmark: hold cash (0%) during out-of-window periods.
entry_conditions: Calendar day is T-7 (or prior trading day if weekend/holiday) before quarter-end (March 31, June 30, September 30, December 31)
DEXJPUS USD/JPY spot rate is within 5% of its own 60-trading-day moving average (filter to avoid BOJ acute intervention episodes)
exit_conditions: Exit on the 2nd trading day of the new quarter (i.e., 2 trading days after the quarter-end date)
Hard stop-loss: exit if FXY falls more than 2% from entry price during the holding window

data_sources_concrete.prices: FXY (yfinance, CurrencyShares Japanese Yen ETF, available 2007-02-13 to present)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: DEXJPUS (FRED, USD/JPY daily spot rate, for BOJ intervention filter)

backtest_approach: Event study: identify all 4 quarter-end dates per year from 2007-02-13 (FXY inception) to present (~76 events). For each event, compute FXY return from T-7 calendar days before quarter-end through T+2 trading days after. Apply the DEXJPUS 60-day MA filter to exclude events during extreme BOJ intervention windows. Compare mean/median event returns vs. SPY returns during same windows. Calculate Sharpe ratio of the strategy as a time series of binary on/off positions. Expected hold time ~9 calendar days per quarter; in-market ~14% of the time.
implementation_notes: FXY tracks USD/JPY inverse: when JPY strengthens (USD/JPY falls), FXY rises. Quarter-ends are the last trading day of March, June, September, December. BOJ intervention filter: exclude any quarter-end where 5-day abs return of FXY exceeded 3% in the 10 days prior to entry (signals active intervention). Cross-currency basis data (DTCC/BIS) is used for signal validation in live trading but is NOT required for the historical backtest — the calendar trigger alone is sufficient. Note the 2022 BOJ intervention period (H2 2022) introduced a noise cluster; the DEXJPUS MA filter should screen out most of these events.

name: FERC Major Transmission Planning Order Compliance Cluster → Long Quanta Services (PWR)
rule: Enter long PWR within 5 trading days of a major FERC transmission planning order compliance filing cluster event — defined as >= 3 major ISO/RTO compliance plan filings within a 60-day window under a single FERC docket. Proxy for historical backtesting: use the dates of FERC Order 890 (2007), Order 1000 (2011-2012 compliance window), and Order 1920 (2024-2025 compliance window) as event dates. Supplement with MISO LRTP Tranche approval announcements (Tranche 1: Dec 2022; Tranche 2: Dec 2023) as additional event dates. Exit after 180 calendar days or when PWR has returned +25% from entry, whichever comes first. Benchmark: long SPY buy-and-hold over the same holding periods.
entry_conditions: Major FERC transmission planning compliance event: FERC issues final rule or ISO/RTO submits compliance plan under a FERC transmission planning docket (Order 890/1000/1920 analogs)
PWR price is above its 50-day moving average at time of entry signal (trend filter)
Entry within 5 trading days of event announcement date
exit_conditions: Exit after 180 calendar days from entry (primary)
Exit if PWR has risen +25% from entry price (profit target)
Exit if PWR falls more than 10% from entry price (stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: PWR (yfinance, Quanta Services, available 1998 to present); NEE (yfinance, benchmark); WEC (yfinance, benchmark); SPY (yfinance, benchmark)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: none — event dates derived from FERC press releases (see known_events); FERC eLibrary for live signal generation

backtest_approach: Event study with 6 known anchor dates: (1) FERC Order 890 final rule Feb 16 2007, (2) FERC Order 1000 final rule July 21 2011, (3) FERC Order 1000 compliance filing cluster (MISO/PJM filings Nov-Dec 2012), (4) MISO LRTP Tranche 1 approval Dec 19 2022, (5) MISO LRTP Tranche 2 approval Dec 14 2023, (6) FERC Order 1920 compliance filing window opens (estimate Nov 2024-Feb 2025). For each date, compute PWR buy-and-hold return over 30/60/90/180-day windows. Compare vs. SPY over same windows and vs. XLI (industrials) for sector-adjusted returns. Small event set (6 dates) so interpret results as a directional signal study, not a high-power statistical test.
implementation_notes: Small event set (n=6) limits statistical power; treat as directional/qualitative confirmation. PWR is the primary target: largest pure-play EPC contractor for electric transmission in the US. NEE and WEC are secondary checks: regulated utilities with large own-transmission rate base, similar causal pathway but with rate-base lag. FERC Order 1920 compliance filings track real-time via FERC eLibrary dockets RM21-17 and RM23-10. The forward-looking thesis (Order 1920 compliance 2024-2026) is likely the strongest version of this trade, but only 1-2 historical analogs exist, so this is a borderline watchlist candidate. The bt_feasibility is 3/5 because the event-study window is very short and the number of events is small.

name: BTC Google Trends Euphoria Peak → Short IBIT (Counter-Signal)
rule: This is a counter-signal to long_BTC. Entry: short IBIT (or use BTC-USD as proxy pre-2024) when weekly Google Trends search volume for keyword "Bitcoin" in the United States crosses above the 80th percentile of the trailing 260-week (5-year) rolling window. Confirm with at least one of: (a) BTC 7-day price return > +20%, or (b) 14-day RSI > 75. Exit: cover short after 28 calendar days OR when Google Trends drops below the 60th percentile of the same rolling window, whichever comes first. Position size: 10% of capital (crypto volatility management). No leverage. Benchmark: buy-and-hold BTC-USD / IBIT over the same periods (to show counter-signal value).
entry_conditions: Weekly Google Trends search interest for keyword Bitcoin (US geo) crosses above 80th percentile of trailing 260-week rolling window (via pytrends library)
At least one confirmation: 7-day BTC price return > +20%, OR 14-day RSI of BTC-USD > 75
exit_conditions: Cover short after 28 calendar days from entry (primary exit)
Cover short if Google Trends index drops below 60th percentile of trailing 260-week window (signal fade)
Stop-loss: cover if IBIT/BTC-USD rises more than 15% from short entry price (counter-trend protection)

data_sources_concrete.prices: IBIT (yfinance, 2024-01-11 to present); BTC-USD (yfinance, 2014-09-17 to present, proxy for pre-IBIT backtesting)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: Google Trends weekly Bitcoin US search volume via pytrends library (free, no API key required)

backtest_approach: Use BTC-USD as the price proxy for the full backtest window (2014-present). Pull weekly Google Trends data for Bitcoin US via pytrends (limit: 5-year window per query; use overlapping 5-year batches to stitch a full series). Normalize each overlapping segment using the intersection period, producing a continuous index. Identify all weeks where the normalized index crosses the 80th percentile rolling threshold and at least one confirmation is met. Compute BTC-USD return over subsequent 28-day windows for each signal. Compare distribution of 28-day returns in signal windows vs. all other periods (t-test). Translate to IBIT for the post-2024 live-trading period. Expected signal frequency: ~3-6 signals per BTC major cycle (4-year halving cycle yields roughly 2 clear euphoria peaks).
implementation_notes: IBIT is the preferred trading vehicle post-2024 (spot Bitcoin ETF, liquid, no custody risk). Pre-2024, use BTC-USD for performance attribution only (not directly shortable without margin crypto account). Counter-signal: this strategy is explicitly counter to the "long_BTC" idea family; broad crypto index target is intentional here per spec. Google Trends data via pytrends has a normalization caveat: each query window is 0-100 scaled; must stitch overlapping windows for a continuous >5-year series. pytrends install: pip install pytrends. Known limitation: Google Trends data has ~3-day publication lag; signal detection is weekly so entry lag is acceptable.

name: TIC Foreign Official Net Treasury Sales -> Short TLT (Duration Headwind)
rule: When US Treasury TIC monthly report (released ~6 weeks after month-end) shows trailing-12-month net purchases of US long-term Treasuries by foreign official institutions (central banks/SWFs) cross below -150B USD (cumulative 12-month outflow), enter short TLT at next-day open. Hold for up to 8 weeks. Exit: (a) 8-week maximum holding period, OR (b) trailing-12-month TIC net purchases recover above -100B USD, OR (c) Fed announces emergency QE/yield curve control (invalidates thesis), OR (d) TLT rises 8% from entry (hard stop, rate compression thesis wrong). This is a counter-signal to prevailing long_TLT thesis: foreign CB selling caps duration rallies even during Fed pivot cycles.
entry_conditions: US Treasury TIC monthly release shows trailing-12-month foreign official net long-term Treasury purchases < -150B USD
Monthly TIC release date serves as signal date (typically 6 weeks after reference month)
DGS10 (FRED) >= 3.5% at signal date (not already deeply inverted environment)
exit_conditions: 8-week maximum holding period from entry date
Subsequent TIC release shows trailing-12-month net purchases recover above -100B USD
Fed announces QE, yield curve control, or emergency bond purchase program
TLT rises 8% from entry (hard stop - thesis invalidated by rate compression)
TLT falls 15% from entry (take profit target reached)

data_sources_concrete.prices: TLT, IEF, TBT, SPY (yfinance)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: US Treasury TIC monthly data: foreign official net purchases of long-term US Treasuries. Primary source: https://ticdata.treasury.gov (Treasury International Capital system, Table 5 - Official Institutions Long-term net purchases). FRED DGS10 (10y Treasury yield) for rate-regime entry filter. FRED DGS30 (30y Treasury yield) for duration signal crosscheck. Known historical net-selling episodes: 2013-2014 (China reducing ~-50B/yr), 2016-2018 (EM FX defense selling ~-100 to -200B/yr), 2022-2023 (broad de-dollarization ~-250 to -400B/yr per TIC Table 5 data)

backtest_approach: Event-study + rolling threshold backtest. Download Treasury TIC Table 5 historical data (available from 2002) from ticdata.treasury.gov. Compute rolling 12-month sum of foreign official net long-term Treasury purchases. Identify months where rolling sum crosses below -150B USD. For each event: compute TLT forward returns at 20, 30, 40 trading days post-release-date. Compare TLT short returns vs long TLT baseline. Regime filter: DGS10 >= 3.5% at signal date. Expected ~4-6 distinct threshold crossings (2016-17 EM outflows, 2022-23 de-dollarization). Benchmark: SPY for risk normalization; include DGS10 change as outcome variable.
implementation_notes: TIC data is NOT on FRED as a ready-made rolling-12m net-change series. Backtester must download Treasury TIC Table 5 (Excel/CSV) from ticdata.treasury.gov and compute the trailing-12-month net purchases sum from monthly flow data. The -150B threshold is approximate; calibrate during backtesting. Important: TIC data has a ~6-week reporting lag (May data released late June/early July). Use the actual TIC RELEASE date as the signal date, not the reference month-end. TBT (ProShares UltraShort 20+yr Treasury, 2x short) is the leveraged alternative. Counter-signal=true, counters long_TLT.

name: NBP Rate Cut + EU Cohesion Fund Disbursement -> Long Poland (EPOL)
rule: When NBP (National Bank of Poland) Monetary Policy Council announces a 25+ bp rate cut AND FRED IR3TIB01PLM156N (Poland 3-month interbank rate) remains >= 2.5% post-cut (positive real rate regime), enter long EPOL (iShares MSCI Poland ETF) at next-day open. Hold for 8 weeks. Exit: (a) 8-week maximum holding period, OR (b) NBP signals explicit pause or hike, OR (c) EUR/PLN rate drops through 4.10 (PLN over-appreciation signal), OR (d) EPOL falls 10% from entry (hard stop). The EU cohesion fund disbursement confirmation (EC payment dashboard) is an optional additional filter: if monthly EC disbursement to Poland > EUR 2B coincides within 30 days, increase position conviction to 1.5x.
entry_conditions: NBP RPP announces rate cut of 25+ bps (from NBP press release at nbp.pl)
FRED IR3TIB01PLM156N (Poland 3-month interbank) >= 2.5% post-cut (positive real rate filter)
EPOL has not already run >8% in the prior 4 weeks (no chase on extended move)
Optional: EC monthly disbursement to Poland > EUR 2B in same or preceding calendar month
exit_conditions: 8-week maximum holding period from NBP announcement date
NBP RPP explicitly signals rate pause or reversal to hike
EUR/PLN spot drops below 4.10 (PLN over-appreciation, carry trade unwind risk)
EPOL falls 10% from entry (hard stop)
EPOL rises 12% from entry (take profit target)

data_sources_concrete.prices: EPOL (yfinance, available 2010-05 onward); EURPLN=X (yfinance EUR/PLN)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FRED IR3TIB01PLM156N (Poland 3-month interbank rate, monthly, 2015-2026); NBP RPP rate decisions (nbp.pl - manual event dates): Cut cycle 2012-2013: Nov 2012 (4.75->4.50%), Jan 2013, Mar 2013, May 2013 (3.00%), Jun 2013 (2.50%); Oct 2014 emergency -50bp; Mar 2015 -25bp; Oct 2019 -25bp; Mar/Apr/May 2020 COVID (3x cuts); Sep 2023 -75bp surprise; Oct 2023 -25bp; CPGRLE01PLM659N (Poland core CPI, FRED monthly, 2015+) for real rate calculation

backtest_approach: Event-study on NBP rate cut announcement dates. Seed events: Nov 2012, Jan 2013, Mar 2013, May 2013, Jun 2013, Oct 2014, Mar 2015, Oct 2019, Mar/Apr/May 2020, Sep 2023, Oct 2023. Filter to events where post-cut rate >= 2.5% (removes ZIRP era 2015-2021). For each filtered event: compute EPOL cumulative returns at 10, 20, 30, 40 trading days. Compare EPOL excess return vs SPY (Poland vs global equity beta). Include EUR/PLN as FX risk crosscheck (EURPLN=X on yfinance). Expected filtered events: ~8-9 (2012-2013 cycle: 5 events, 2023: 2 events, 2019 and Oct 2014 if rates >= 2.5%). Report: hit rate, mean forward return, Sharpe, max drawdown per event.
implementation_notes: EPOL has data from May 2010, covering 2012-2013 NBP cut cycle fully. IR3TIB01PLM156N (Poland 3M interbank) starts 2015 on FRED; for pre-2015 events use Poland reference rate from NBP website directly. EURPLN=X (EUR/PLN) available on yfinance for FX risk monitoring. EU cohesion fund disbursement trigger requires manual EC dashboard verification; treat as optional conviction enhancer, not primary trigger. EPOL is ~30% financials (PKO Bank, Santander Bank Polska, Pekao) + ~15% industrials + ~15% energy (PKN Orlen) - bank-heavy composition amplifies rate-cut benefit. bt_feasibility=3 due to manual NBP event compilation; 2012-2013 and 2023 cycles provide ~7 distinct events total.

name: FDA Drug Safety Communication (DILI/Hepatotoxicity) -> Short Drug Sponsor Equity
rule: TRIGGER: FDA publishes a Drug Safety Communication (DSC) via fda.gov/safety/medwatch RSS feed that explicitly flags drug-induced liver injury (DILI), hepatotoxicity, or a required label change adding a Boxed Warning or REMS related to liver injury for a specific branded drug. ENTRY: Identify the drug sponsor from FDA Drugs@FDA label history or the SEC 8-K filing (item 8.01) published within 4 business days. Short the sponsor equity within 5 trading days of DSC publication date. SIZE: 1x notional. Optional tail hedge: buy 1-month ATM put on the sponsor. EXIT: Cover when FDA issues the confirmed label change with Boxed Warning effective date (stock typically reverses on clarity), or at 8-week maximum hold. Hard stop: sponsor stock +10% from short entry (mechanism failed to transmit).
entry_conditions: FDA Drug Safety Communication published on fda.gov/safety/medwatch RSS for a branded drug citing DILI, hepatotoxicity, or liver injury requiring new Boxed Warning or REMS
The affected drug represents >15% of sponsor revenue or is a key growth asset per most recent 10-K (ensures stock impact is material)
Sponsor market cap is above $5B (ensures sufficient liquidity for short entry)
exit_conditions: FDA confirms label change with Boxed Warning effective date published (regulatory clarity typically triggers stock reversal)
8 weeks from entry date (base case holding period)
Hard stop: sponsor stock +10% from short entry price

data_sources_concrete.prices: Sponsor-specific ticker via yfinance (see known_events); XBI and IBB as sector benchmarks; SPY as market benchmark
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FDA Drug Safety Communications RSS feed (fda.gov/safety/medwatch, free); openFDA FAERS API (api.fda.gov/drug/event, free) for DILI report rate monitoring; SEC EDGAR 8-K item 8.01 for sponsor identification

backtest_approach: Event-study design using historical FDA DSC events with DILI/Boxed Warning escalations. Curated event cohort (sponsors with liquid, still-trading equities): (1) 2018-11-14: Xofigo (radium-223) -- Bayer AG US ADR (BAYRY), FDA safety update; (2) 2020-08-27: Aubagio (teriflunomide) -- Sanofi (SNY) liver injury DSC; (3) 2021-09-09: Xeljanz/Xeljanz XR (tofacitinib) -- Pfizer (PFE) cardiovascular+DILI update; (4) 2021-05-20: Ocaliva (obeticholic acid) -- Intercept Pharmaceuticals (ICPT); note: ICPT acquired 2024 but had clean price data through event; (5) 2022-03-08: Tecfidera/Vumerity -- Biogen (BIIB) liver DSC update. For each event: compute sponsor stock return vs XBI sector return over [0, +40 trading days]. Compute alpha vs XBI (sponsor-specific vs biotech sector drag). Report: mean/median alpha vs XBI, max drawdown, and probability of >10% decline within 40 days. Note: some tickers (ICPT) may need historical yfinance data retrieved before delisting date -- the backtester should set end date to one month before acquisition close to get clean data.
implementation_notes: Key challenge: sponsor ticker is NOT predetermined -- it must be identified from the FDA DSC content and mapped to a public company. The backtester must maintain a sponsor-to-ticker mapping for each known event: 2018-11-14->BAYRY, 2020-08-27->SNY, 2021-05-20->ICPT (use historical data pre-2024), 2021-09-09->PFE, 2022-03-08->BIIB. ICPT (Intercept Pharmaceuticals) was acquired by Alfasigma in 2024 and is now delisted; yfinance returns no data for ICPT even for historical periods. The backtester should exclude this event or attempt to source ICPT historical prices from an alternative provider. Forward deployment requires daily monitoring of the FDA DSC RSS feed. The 15%-of-revenue threshold filters out DSCs on minor pipeline drugs that have immaterial stock impact. XBI is used as sector benchmark to strip out broad biotech beta from the alpha calculation.

name: FTC/DOJ HSR Second Request -> Merger Target Spread Widening Short
rule: TRIGGER: FTC or DOJ publicly announces HSR Second Request issuance for a pending merger. Monitor: ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases (RSS) and justice.gov/atr/news RSS. Public SR announcements per HSR Act Section 7A transparency requirements. ENTRY: Short the acquisition target equity within 5 trading days of SR public announcement. Confirm target from SEC 8-K item 1.01 merger agreement if needed. SHORT SIZE: 1x notional on the target stock. ALTERNATIVE: Buy put spreads (3-month expiry, 90%/75% strikes) to limit upside risk if deal closes. EXIT: Cover when (a) deal is formally abandoned or blocked -- target reverts toward pre-announcement price, (b) regulatory approval despite SR -- target rallies to deal price (take loss), or (c) 4-month maximum hold from SR date. Hard stop: target stock +8% above deal price (signals market pricing deal-certain outcome).
entry_conditions: FTC or DOJ press release explicitly announces HSR Second Request for a named pending acquisition
Target company is publicly traded (identifiable via SEC EDGAR 8-K) and has market cap >$2B
Current merger-arb spread (deal price minus current target price) is <8% at SR announcement -- if spread already >15%, SR is already priced and entry is unattractive
exit_conditions: Deal is formally abandoned or blocked by regulator (target reverts toward pre-announcement price -- profit case)
Regulatory approval issued despite SR -- cover loss at market
4-month maximum hold from SR announcement date
Hard stop: target price reaches deal price + 5% (market pricing deal-certain)

data_sources_concrete.prices: Target-specific ticker via yfinance (see known_events for historical mapping); SPY as market benchmark
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FTC press releases RSS (ftc.gov/feeds/press-releases.xml, free); DOJ ATR news RSS (justice.gov, free); SEC EDGAR 8-K full-text search for merger party identification (efts.sec.gov, free)

backtest_approach: Event-study design using public SR announcement dates with liquid target tickers. Curated event cohort (targets with post-SR price history available on yfinance): (1) 2021-03-09: Nvidia/Arm deal (private target -- EXCLUDE), (2) 2022-02-03: FTC v. Meta/Within VR (private -- EXCLUDE), (3) 2022-03-29: FTC Second Request Kroger/Albertsons (ACI) -- target still public until late 2024 deal; (4) 2022-04-28: Microsoft/Activision Blizzard (ATVI) SR -- note ATVI delisted 2023 after deal closed; (5) 2023-06-12: FTC Second Request for Tapestry/Capri (CPRI) -- CPRI still trades; (6) 2023-08-21: FTC block of Amgen/Horizon Therapeutics (HZNP) -- HZNP delisted after close. Recommended executable events: ACI (SR 2022, deal ultimately blocked Dec 2024 -- full reversal case); CPRI (Capri Holdings, Tapestry deal blocked Oct 2023 -- SR to block within ~6 months). For each event: compute target stock return vs SPY over [0, +80 trading days] from SR date. Compute spread (deal price minus target) at SR date and spread at exit date. Compute P&L for short strategy (long spread widening). Note: many targets delist upon deal close -- event study requires careful date windowing.
implementation_notes: Counter-signal vs long_M&A_target and long_SPY: this trade profits when the consensus merger-arb long is wrong. MAJOR DATA CAVEAT: Most acquisition targets delist after deal closes (ATVI, VMW, SGEN, DISH, etc.), and yfinance returns no data for delisted tickers even for historical periods. The event study is limited to targets that either (a) remained public through the SR window because the deal was blocked (ACI, CPRI -- best candidates), or (b) have valid historical data in yfinance despite eventual delisting (test before backtesting). For forward deployment: the strategy is operationally sound but requires active monitoring of FTC/DOJ RSS and real-time spread calculations. The 8% deal-price hard stop is critical -- if the market reads the SR as noise and pushes target toward deal price, the short thesis is invalidated. bt_feasibility is effectively 3 (not 4 as originally scouted) due to widespread delisting of targets in yfinance.

name: Consumer Stress Rotation: Trade-Down Signal → Long DG / Short CMG Pair
rule: Long DG / Short CMG delta-neutral pair, equal-notional. Entry signal: FRED DRTSCILM (% banks tightening consumer lending standards) rises above zero (net tightening) for 2 consecutive quarterly observations AND JOLTS Quits Rate (JTSQUR) falls below its 12-month moving average. Both conditions must be met. Enter within 3 trading days of the second quarterly DRTSCILM confirmation. Exit after 63 trading days (one quarter) OR when DRTSCILM returns to net-easing territory (< -5%), whichever comes first. Hedge ratio: equal-notional (1x long DG, 1x short CMG). Supplement / replace with foot-traffic ratio if SafeGraph data is available: (DG+DLTR weekly visit YoY / CMG+SBUX weekly visit YoY) > 52-week average + 1 stdev for 2 consecutive weeks.
entry_conditions: FRED DRTSCILM (net % banks tightening consumer lending standards) > 0 for 2 consecutive quarterly readings (net tightening)
FRED JTSQUR (private sector quits rate) < 12-month trailing moving average (labor market cooling confirming consumer stress)
Alternative real-time trigger: SafeGraph/Placer.ai foot-traffic ratio (DG+DLTR YoY / CMG+SBUX YoY) crosses above 52-week mean + 1 stdev for 2 consecutive weeks
exit_conditions: Exit both legs after 63 trading days from entry
Exit if DRTSCILM returns to net-easing territory (< -5%)
Stop-loss: exit if the pair spread (DG return minus CMG return) moves against trade by more than 8% (i.e., CMG rising while DG falls)

data_sources_concrete.prices: DG (yfinance, Dollar General, 2009-present); CMG (yfinance, Chipotle, 2006-present); DLTR (yfinance, Dollar Tree, 1995-present); SBUX (yfinance, Starbucks, 1992-present)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: DRTSCILM (FRED, net % banks tightening consumer lending standards, quarterly); JTSQUR (FRED, private-sector quits rate, monthly)

backtest_approach: Identify all periods 2009-present (DG IPO is the limiting constraint) where DRTSCILM > 0 for 2 consecutive quarters AND JTSQUR < 12-month MA. Main signal periods: 2009-2010 (post-GFC), 2015-2016 (energy sector stress), 2022-2023 (rate hike cycle). For each entry date, compute DG-CMG pair 63-day return vs SPY. Alternative test: use foot-traffic ratio from SafeGraph (available 2018-present via academic access) for post-2018 period to compare signal quality vs macro proxy. Expected signal events: 4-6 episodes over 2009-2025.
implementation_notes: Foot-traffic data (SafeGraph academic API) is the preferred real-time signal but historical data only available 2018+. FRED DRTSCILM serves as the backtestable macro proxy with longer history (2005+). DG IPO was November 2009, limiting pair backtest to 2009-present. Note: DLTR can substitute for DG if needed (DLTR has data back to 1995). The bt_feasibility is 3/5 due to limited event count (foot-traffic signal) or quarterly frequency lag (FRED signal). CMG is a premium fast-casual concept with structurally positive secular growth; the pair trade captures only cyclical stress episodes, not secular direction.

name: USDA NASS Texas Cotton Abandonment Rate Breach 38% → Long CT=F
rule: Long ICE cotton front-month futures (CT=F) when USDA NASS weekly Crop Progress Report shows Texas cotton implied abandonment rate (Texas planted acres minus Texas expected harvested acres, divided by Texas planted acres) exceeds 38% at any point during the July-September growing season. Pull data via USDA Quick Stats API: commodity_desc=COTTON, statisticcat_desc=AREA PLANTED and AREA HARVESTED, state_alpha=TX, year=current. Abandonment rate = 1 - (expected harvested / planted). Hold CT=F long for 42 trading days (approximately 2 months). Early exit: if subsequent NASS report shows abandonment rate falling back below 30% (beneficial rains reversal). Benchmark: buy-and-hold CT=F from start of each growing season (May) for same-length window.
entry_conditions: USDA NASS weekly Crop Progress (Monday release): Texas cotton implied abandonment rate = 1 - (expected harvested acres / planted acres) crosses above 38%
Entry during July-September window only (abandonment signal only meaningful mid-to-late growing season)
Signal must occur during an active crop season (Texas planted acres > 3 million, confirming non-trivial crop year)
exit_conditions: Exit after 42 trading days from entry (primary)
Early exit if subsequent NASS report shows Texas abandonment rate falls back below 30% (beneficial rainfall reversal)
Stop-loss: exit if CT=F falls more than 8% from entry price

data_sources_concrete.prices: CT=F (yfinance, ICE cotton front-month futures, 2000-present)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: USDA NASS Quick Stats API (free, no key required for <50 requests/day): https://quickstats.nass.usda.gov/api — fields: source_desc=SURVEY, sector_desc=CROPS, commodity_desc=COTTON, statisticcat_desc=AREA PLANTED and AREA HARVESTED, state_alpha=TX, freq_desc=ANNUAL and WEEKLY

backtest_approach: Pull Texas cotton planted and harvested acres from USDA NASS Quick Stats API for 2000-present. Compute final-season abandonment rate for each year (final harvested / planted). High-abandonment events: 2011 (>70%, extreme Texas drought), 2022 (~60%, La Nina drought), 2009 (~40%), 2006 (~45%). For each year where abandonment exceeded 38%, determine the approximate calendar date when the growing-season NASS weekly progress report first implied >= 38% abandonment. Use monthly/weekly Crop Progress data (via API weekly reports) for 2010-present. Compute CT=F 42-day return starting from that signal date. Compare vs CT=F 42-day return starting from same calendar date in non-breach years. Expected events: ~5-7 high-abandonment years over 2000-2025.
implementation_notes: USDA NASS Quick Stats API provides historical weekly Crop Progress going back to 2010 (electronic). Pre-2010 data (2000-2009) available via annual final abandonment rate from NASS historical datasets; for those years, use July 15 of the abandonment year as a conservative proxy entry date. CT=F is the front-month continuous contract on yfinance; roll dates may create small gaps — use adjusted close. Texas accounts for ~45% of US cotton production but the abandonment rate is highly variable (0-70%+ in drought years). The 38% threshold was chosen as the 75th percentile of Texas abandonment rate distribution (2000-2023 average ~18%). Correlation check: Texas drought years (PDSI < -3 for TX) should closely align with NASS abandonment signal.

name: AAII + Investors Intelligence Dual-Confirmation Euphoria SPY Short
rule: Every Thursday after AAII survey release: (1) Compute AAII bull-bear spread from the weekly XLS download (aaii.com/files/surveys/sentiment.xls). (2) Read current Investors Intelligence bull% from yardeni.com free chart data. Entry trigger: AAII bull-bear spread >= 30 percentage points (approx top-5th-percentile, empirically ~30pp+ is 90th+ pct since 2010) AND II bull% >= 60% simultaneously. Open short SPY at Friday market open, size = 1 unit. Also open long XLP + XLU as defensive rotation (0.5 units each) as hedge. Exit: EITHER SPY drops 7% from entry OR 8 calendar weeks from entry, whichever first. If no exit triggered, close at week 8 market open. Do NOT enter if VIX > 25 at entry (already in risk-off; signal stale).
entry_conditions: AAII bull-bear spread (bull% minus bear%) >= 30 percentage points on the weekly Thursday release
Investors Intelligence Advisors Sentiment bull% >= 60% on the same week
SPY is within 2% of its 52-week high (confirm euphoria context, not a recovery bounce read)
VIX < 25 at entry (avoid entering into already-elevated volatility regimes)
exit_conditions: SPY has declined 7% or more from entry price (profit target reached)
8 calendar weeks have elapsed since entry (time stop)
AAII bull-bear spread drops back below 15pp OR II bull% drops below 50% (signal reversal)

data_sources_concrete.prices: SPY, XLP, XLU, ^VIX via yfinance daily
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: AAII sentiment: weekly XLS download https://www.aaii.com/files/surveys/sentiment.xls (free, columns: Date, Bullish%, Neutral%, Bearish%); II bull%: Yardeni.com free chart page (weekly, or use St. Louis FRED BULLINVI series if available)

backtest_approach: Event-study: identify all weeks 2000-present where AAII bull-bear >= 30pp AND II bull% >= 60% simultaneously. For each event, record SPY forward return at 2w, 4w, 6w, 8w. Primary P&L: short SPY from Friday open after signal week. Benchmark: buy-and-hold SPY. Also compute long XLP, long XLU forward returns for the defensive rotation leg. Use daily OHLCV from yfinance. Dedup events within 6-week windows (no re-trigger until prior signal resolves). Report Sharpe (annualized), CAGR, max drawdown, hit rate on 8-week horizon.
known_events: 2000-02 (dot-com peak AAII euphoria)
2007-10 (pre-GFC peak sentiment)
2018-01 (Jan 2018 VIX spike precursor)
2021-01 (retail meme euphoria)
implementation_notes: AAII data goes back to 1987 but weekly granularity from 1987; II data free from Yardeni from ~2000. Backtest window limited to 2000+ for dual-confirm. Counter-signal idea (counters: long_SPY) so SPY as primary short target is correct behavior per spec. AAII XLS URL may change; validate download at runtime. Consider log-transforming bull-bear spread before percentile ranking to handle fat tails.

name: S&P 500 Breadth Deterioration (% Above 200-DMA) vs Index ATH Divergence Fade
rule: Weekly, every Friday after close: (1) Pull the SPDR S&P 500 constituent list from the Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' table or ssga.com ETF holdings CSV. (2) Download daily closes for all ~503 tickers via yfinance. (3) Compute pct_above_200dma = count(price > 200-day SMA) / total_constituents. (4) Check: SPY printed a 52-week high within the last 2 weeks AND pct_above_200dma < 50% AND pct_above_200dma has declined for 3+ consecutive weekly readings. Entry: short SPY at Monday open after signal fires, 1 unit. Also long XLV + XLU at 0.5 units each (defensive leg). Exit: pct_above_200dma reverses above 55% on a Friday reading OR 12 weeks elapsed OR SPY drops 8% from entry.
entry_conditions: SPY has printed a new 52-week high within the trailing 2-week window
Percentage of S&P 500 constituents trading above their 200-day SMA < 50%
Breadth reading has declined for 3 or more consecutive weekly readings (sustained deterioration, not one-week noise)
exit_conditions: Breadth (% above 200-DMA) recovers above 55% on any Friday reading (signal invalidated)
SPY has declined 8% or more from entry price (profit target)
12 calendar weeks elapsed from entry (time stop)

data_sources_concrete.prices: SPY, XLV, XLU plus all ~503 S&P 500 constituents via yfinance daily OHLCV
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: none — all computed from price series; constituent list from Wikipedia S&P 500 table (scraped via pandas.read_html) or ssga.com holdings CSV

backtest_approach: Roll a weekly time series of pct_above_200dma from 2005-present (earlier limited by constituent data quality). For each Friday, flag signal = (SPY_52wk_high_in_last_2wks=True) AND (pct < 0.50) AND (pct declining 3+ weeks). On each signal, record SPY short entry at next Monday open and track daily P&L. Compare to long-only SPY benchmark. Dedup within 4-week lockout after signal fires. Use survivorship-bias-aware constituent list (Wikipedia table history or Sharadar-free tier if available). Report Sharpe, CAGR, max drawdown, number of episodes.
known_events: 2015-08 (flash crash: SPY near high, breadth already cracking)
2018-10 (Q4 sell-off: new highs in Sep, breadth diverging since Aug)
2020-02 (COVID pre-sell-off: ATH but narrow leadership)
2023-07 (AI-driven narrow ATH with poor breadth below 200-DMA)
implementation_notes: Survivorship bias is the main risk: using current S&P 500 constituents to reconstruct 2005 breadth overstates historical breadth health. Use point-in-time constituent lists if available (Sharadar free tier, or approximate with Wikipedia historical S&P 500 changes table). Counter-signal idea (counters: long_SPY) so SPY as primary short target is correct per spec. Constituent download (~503 tickers) may be slow; cache price data locally. pct_above_200dma can be cross-checked against StockCharts SPXA200R (public chart, not downloadable) or Barchart SPXA200 for validation.

name: USACE Black Warrior-Tombigbee Waterway Lock Outage — Short HCC (Warrior Met Coal)
rule: When cumulative USACE LPMS-reported downtime on any Black Warrior-Tombigbee Waterway lock (Holt, Bevill, Gainesville, or Bankhead) exceeds 72 hours in a trailing 14-day window: (1) short HCC (Warrior Met Coal) as the primary Alabama barge-dependent met-coal producer, (2) long AMR (Alpha Metallurgical Resources, VA/WV rail-loaded operations) as relative outperformer. Entry on day USACE LPMS data confirms the threshold breach; hold 21 trading days or until LPMS reports restoration to <12 hrs cumulative downtime in trailing 7 days. Size: equal-dollar long AMR / short HCC pair.
entry_conditions: USACE LPMS Black Warrior-Tombigbee lock cumulative downtime > 72 hours in trailing 14-day window (from weekly LPMS download at navigationdatacenter.us)
HCC price within 5% of trailing 20-day high (not already pricing in disruption)
Met-coal market not in crisis (BTU 60-day realized vol < 80%) to avoid entering during commodity market breakdowns
exit_conditions: 21 trading days elapsed since entry
USACE LPMS trailing 7-day cumulative downtime drops below 12 hours (restoration)
HCC moves >15% against position (stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: HCC (Warrior Met Coal), AMR (Alpha Metallurgical Resources), BTU (Peabody Energy), SPY — all via yfinance; historical start: HCC from 2017-04-13, AMR from ~2021
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: USACE Navigation Data Center LPMS monthly/weekly CSV download (https://www.navigationdatacenter.us/lpms/) — Black Warrior-Tombigbee district lock availability tables; no FRED series needed

backtest_approach: Event-study design: identify all USACE LPMS-recorded BWTW lock outage events 2017-2025 where cumulative 14-day downtime exceeded 72 hrs. For each event date, compute HCC and AMR 21-trading-day forward returns. Compare HCC-vs-AMR pair P&L to SPY benchmark. Use daily close prices from yfinance. Primary metric: mean HCC underperformance vs AMR in the 21-day post-event window. Secondary: HCC outright short returns. Note AMR IPO was 2021-07-26, so full pair backtest is limited to 2021 onward; HCC solo-short backtest covers full 2017+ sample.
known_events: 2018-03: Holt Lock mechanical failure (reported in USACE FY2018 performance stats)
2019-07: Low-pool drought delay events on multiple BWTW locks
2022-11: Gainesville Lock maintenance outage
implementation_notes: CEIX (CONSOL Energy) was the original idea ticker but is currently delisted on yfinance. HCC (Warrior Met Coal) is the correct Alabama-barge-dependent met-coal operator; their Warrior Met mines in Tuscaloosa County ship exclusively via BWTW to McDuffie Island Terminal in Mobile. AMR (Alpha Metallurgical Resources) IPO'd July 2021, limiting the paired backtest. For full-sample analysis, use HCC-short only vs SPY benchmark. USACE LPMS data requires manual CSV download and cleaning; flag for backtester to pre-process the lock availability tables. AMR ticker confirmed available from yfinance as of 2026.

name: NHC Atlantic Quiet Spell After Above-Normal Outlook — Short WTI Hurricane Risk-Premium
rule: Counter-signal to existing long-crude catalog entries. Entry conditions: (1) NOAA/CSU seasonal Atlantic hurricane outlook classifies season as 'above-normal' (issued June 1, updated August 1); (2) NHC 5-day advisory track database confirms zero Gulf of Mexico production-threatening tracks (no systems within 200 miles of Gulf production zone) through 6 consecutive weeks from August 1; (3) BSEE daily shut-in production report confirms zero cumulative shut-ins August 1 through September 15; (4) CFTC Disaggregated COT managed-money net long WTI crude >= 200,000 contracts. When all 4 conditions met: short CL=F front-month (or buy SCO ProShares UltraShort Bloomberg Crude Oil ETF for non-futures accounts) and go long CL=F M+3 vs short M+1 calendar spread to capture backwardation compression. Hold 6 weeks or until first named system enters Gulf with production-threatening track, whichever comes first.
entry_conditions: NOAA seasonal Atlantic outlook released June 1 or August 1 classifies season as 'above normal' (named storms forecast above 14 or ACE > 150% of median)
BSEE Gulf of Mexico Daily Shut-In Production Report shows zero cumulative shut-ins from August 1 through current date (minimum 42 consecutive days of zero shut-ins during peak season)
NHC 5-day advisory cone: no named system with track within 200nm of GOM production area for 6 consecutive weeks
CFTC Disaggregated COT most recent weekly report: Managed Money net long WTI crude oil >= 200,000 contracts (confirming crowded positioning)
exit_conditions: 42 calendar days elapsed from entry date (6-week hold expires)
First named tropical system enters Gulf of Mexico with 5-day NHC track passing within 200nm of GOM production area (hurricane put reactivated)
CFTC COT managed money net long drops below 150,000 (crowded positioning already unwound)

data_sources_concrete.prices: CL=F (WTI front-month, yfinance, full history from 2000), SCO (ProShares UltraShort Crude, yfinance, from 2008-11-25), USO (yfinance, from 2006-04-10), SPY (yfinance)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: NOAA/NHC seasonal outlook PDFs (nhc.noaa.gov/seasonal_outlook.html, 2000-present); BSEE Gulf of Mexico shut-in CSV (bsee.gov, daily 2004-present); CFTC Disaggregated COT managed-money WTI net long (cftc.gov weekly, 2006-present); NHC HURDAT2 best-track historical database (2000-present)

backtest_approach: Event-study on annual hurricane seasons 2006-2025 (20 seasons): For each season where NOAA issued above-normal outlook, check if BSEE shows zero Gulf shut-ins Aug 1 to Sep 15 AND CFTC MM net long >= 200k. Count qualifying seasons (~4-8 expected). For each qualifying season entry date, compute CL=F 42-day forward returns and compare to SPY. Also test M1 vs M3 calendar spread compression as secondary signal. Primary metric: mean 42-day CL=F short return in qualifying seasons vs all August 1 periods. Use yfinance CL=F daily closes. Note: calendar spread construction approximates using consecutive CL=F front-month roll; backtester should note CL=F on yfinance is always the active front-month contract.
known_events: 2013: Above-normal NOAA outlook, near-zero Gulf shut-ins, WTI risk premium bled $3-4/bbl late August
2014: Above-normal outlook, quiet Gulf season, WTI underperformed through September
2022: Active season forecast but few Gulf threats; WTI M1-M3 spread compressed through August-September
2023: Above-normal (18 named storms forecast), zero Gulf production shut-ins; WTI sold off in quiet window
implementation_notes: This is an explicit counter-signal to catalog entries countering long_crude. The signal requires cross-referencing 4 data sources; backtester should pre-download BSEE shut-in CSV and CFTC COT weekly data. CL=F yfinance is front-month only — no calendar spread data; use the spread as indicative context only and primary backtest on outright CL=F short. SCO is 2x inverse crude oil ETF and can be used as a proxy for the short. Qualifying event count is approximately 4-8 over the 2006-2025 test window; power may be limited. NOAA seasonal outlooks have been above-normal in majority of recent years (2017-2024), but the zero-shut-in condition is the binding filter. Flag for backtester: wide confidence intervals expected given small N.

name: CBOE Total Put/Call 10-DMA Complacency Signal: Short XLY / Long XLP Pair
rule: This is a counter-signal strategy (counters long_SPY complacency). Download CBOE daily total put/call ratio from cboe.com historical data. Compute rolling 10-day moving average of the total P/C ratio. Entry: when the 10-DMA falls at or below the 10th-percentile of its historical distribution (~0.75 based on 2010-present data) AND VIX < 25 (avoid crisis entries), enter a dollar-neutral pair: short 1 unit XLY, long 1 unit XLP. Hold for 21 trading days (approx 4.5 calendar weeks). Exit: after 21 trading days, or if the 10-DMA P/C ratio reverts above its 30th-percentile (~0.87), or if XLP/XLY spread reaches +8% relative (take profit), whichever comes first. Stop-loss: if pair trade moves -5% against the position, exit immediately.
entry_conditions: CBOE total put/call ratio 10-DMA <= 0.75 (bottom decile, calibrate from 2010-present data)
VIX < 25 at signal date (regime filter to skip into-crisis entries)
Both XLY and XLP have positive 20-day average volume (liquidity check)
exit_conditions: Hold 21 trading days (primary time exit)
10-DMA P/C ratio reverts above 30th percentile (~0.87) — signal dissipated
XLP cumulative return - XLY cumulative return >= +8% (take profit)
Pair trade PnL <= -5% (stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: XLY, XLP, SPY daily OHLCV
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: CBOE total put/call ratio daily history — free bulk download at cboe.com/data/historical-options-data; FRED VIXCLS for VIX level filter

backtest_approach: Event-study backtest: for each date the CBOE total P/C 10-DMA crosses below the 10th-percentile threshold, record as a signal event. Track XLP minus XLY daily return differential starting T+1. Hold up to 21 days. Compute per-signal PnL as: sum of (daily XLP return - daily XLY return) over hold window. Primary metric is alpha vs SPY benchmark on the same dates. Compute Sharpe on the signal-day-triggered returns series. Expected ~12-25 events over a 10-year window. Note: CBOE put/call data requires a one-time download from cboe.com; if not available, proxy with SKEW index or VIX/VVIX divergence as a fallback.
known_events: 2021-01-19 (peak meme complacency)
2020-01-17 (pre-COVID calm)
2017-10-05 (post-Harvey calm)
implementation_notes: Counter-signal strategy — trading XLY/XLP pair is intentional (not a drift toward broad baskets). CBOE total P/C data is free but requires manual download; backtester should check if cboe.com CSV is available in the data folder or proxy with 1/(VIX/VVIX) spread as fallback. The 0.75 threshold and 10th-percentile calibration should be computed in-sample (2010-2018) and validated out-of-sample (2019-present). Dollar-neutral sizing: equal notional in each leg.

name: EIA DUC Drawdown Haynesville/Marcellus Supply Cliff: Long AR (Antero Resources)
rule: Download EIA Drilling Productivity Report (DPR) monthly CSV from eia.gov/petroleum/drilling/. Sum Haynesville + Marcellus DUC (drilled-but-uncompleted) counts each month. Entry: when combined Haynesville + Marcellus DUC count falls to a rolling 24-month low AND is below 400 wells, confirm with EIA-914 showing Appalachian + Gulf Coast gas production declining MoM for 2+ consecutive months. On signal, buy AR (Antero Resources). Size: 100% of position in AR (pure-play Appalachian natgas with ~100% HH price torque). Hold for up to 12 weeks. Exit: close AR position when either (a) 12-week hold expires, (b) DUC count rebounds above 450 wells for 2 consecutive months (supply recovery signal), or (c) AR gains +25% (take profit), or (d) AR loses -12% from entry (stop-loss).
entry_conditions: EIA DPR: Haynesville + Marcellus combined DUC count at 24-month rolling low AND < 400 wells
