EIA-914: Appalachian + Gulf Coast dry gas production declining MoM for 2+ consecutive months
Henry Hub prompt-month futures (DHHNGSP via FRED) in backwardation vs 12-month strip (spot > forward)
exit_conditions: Hold 60 trading days (~12 calendar weeks, primary time exit)
DUC count rebounds above 450 wells for 2+ consecutive months (supply recovery)
AR price +25% from entry (take profit)
AR price -12% from entry (stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: AR, EQT, RRC, UNG, SPY daily OHLCV
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: EIA Drilling Productivity Report monthly CSV (https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/drilling/); EIA Form EIA-914 monthly production; FRED: DHHNGSP (Henry Hub spot price)

backtest_approach: Monthly signal backtest: for each month-end where combined Haynesville + Marcellus DUC count falls below 400 and sets a 24-month low, record as entry. Enter AR at next trading day open. Track AR daily returns for 60 trading days or until exit condition triggered. Compare AR performance vs UNG (natgas ETF) and SPY on the same date windows to isolate E&P-specific alpha vs simple commodity exposure. EIA DPR data is monthly with 5-6 week publication lag; use publication date (not reference month) as signal trigger. EIA-914 production data has an additional ~2-month lag; use for confirmation only. Expected ~3-7 signal events in 2014-2025 window (low DUC periods). Supplement with EQT and RRC returns in the same windows as robustness check.
known_events: 2022-06 (post-rebound DUC trough)
2019-12 (pre-COVID DUC drawdown)
2023-08 (summer DUC low)
implementation_notes: EIA DPR is a free monthly PDF/XLS download; the backtester should use the published Excel files. AR went public in October 2013 (IPO), so the backtest window is limited to 2014-present (~12 years). For events before 2013, use EQT or RRC as proxy. The 400-well threshold is calibrated on 2014-2025 data; treat as approximately 10th-percentile of range. EIA-914 has a significant publication lag (~2 months); use it as a confirming indicator, not the trigger. Henry Hub backwardation filter (DHHNGSP > 12-month strip) requires futures strip data; if unavailable, skip this filter and rely on DUC count alone.

name: EIA Crude Export Record + Brent-WTI Arb Collapse -> Counter Short WTI (CL=F / USO)
rule: Every Thursday after EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report release (10:30am ET): (1) Pull US crude exports from EIA table (mb/d). Check if >= 4.5 mb/d for 3 consecutive weeks. (2) Compute Brent-WTI spread = BZ=F close - CL=F close. Check if < $1/bbl. (3) Check WTI prompt/2nd-month contango: CL=F (M1) < CLM2 (M2 continuous). Entry trigger: all three conditions met simultaneously. Short CL=F (or USO as equity proxy) at Thursday close / Friday open, 1 unit. Exit: EITHER Brent-WTI spread widens back above $3/bbl (arb re-opens) OR CL=F rallies 5% from entry (stop-loss) OR 6 calendar weeks elapsed.
entry_conditions: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report shows US crude exports >= 4.5 mb/d for 3+ consecutive weekly reports
Brent-WTI spread (BZ=F close minus CL=F close) < $1.00/bbl — arb window closed
WTI calendar spread contango: prompt-month below 2nd-month by $0.20+ (curve backwardation removed)
exit_conditions: Brent-WTI spread widens back above $3.00/bbl (arb re-opens, export demand recovery likely)
CL=F rallies 5% from entry close (stop-loss)
6 calendar weeks elapsed from entry (time stop)

data_sources_concrete.prices: CL=F (WTI front month), BZ=F (Brent front month), USO, XOP via yfinance daily
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report: US crude oil exports (mb/d), Table 1 — https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/ (free Thursday 10:30am). Also FRED series DCOILWTICO for WTI spot cross-check.

backtest_approach: Build weekly time series 2015-present: EIA exports (scraped from EIA API or downloaded CSV), Brent-WTI spread from BZ=F - CL=F yfinance closes, WTI M1-M2 spread from CL=F pairs. Flag signal weeks where all 3 entry conditions met. Enter short CL=F at Thursday close. Track daily P&L until exit condition. Dedup within 4-week lockout. Compare to long-only CL=F benchmark. Report Sharpe, CAGR, max drawdown, episode count. Also report XOP forward return for context (refiner/E&P transmission).
known_events: 2018-Q4 (US export surge + arb collapse preceded WTI plunge from $76 to $42)
2022-Q3 (post-SPR release, exports near 4mb/d, Brent-WTI compressed)
2023-Q2 (exports 4.5mb/d sustained, spread compressed to near parity)
implementation_notes: Counter-signal idea (counters: long_crude) so CL=F/USO as primary short target is correct per spec. EIA exports API endpoint: https://api.eia.gov/v2/petroleum/sum/snd/export/weekly/data/ (free API key). BZ=F data in yfinance starts ~2012; pre-2012 use ICE Brent from FRED (DCOILBRENTEU). CL=F roll dates affect M1-M2 spread computation; use explicit contract month comparison or USO as simpler equity proxy that avoids roll arithmetic.

name: EIA Gasoline Product Supplied YoY Demand Destruction -> Short PSX (Refiner Margin Collapse)
rule: Every Thursday after EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report (10:30am ET): (1) Pull 4-week average motor gasoline product supplied (Mbbl/d) for current week and same week prior year. (2) Compute YoY change = (current 4wk avg / prior-year 4wk avg) - 1. Entry trigger: YoY decline >= 4% for 2 consecutive weekly reports. Trade: short PSX, long VLO as pair (PSX-short / VLO-long, equal dollar notional) OR outright short PSX. Position size: 1 unit short PSX, 0.5 unit long VLO (accounts for correlation). Exit: EITHER PSX rallies 6% from entry (stop-loss) OR YoY gasoline demand returns to < -2% decline (signal weakening) OR 8 weeks elapsed.
entry_conditions: EIA 4-week average motor gasoline product supplied shows >= 4% YoY decline for 2 consecutive weekly reports
RBOB crack spread (RB=F - CL=F, in $/bbl, multiply by 42) is trending down (current reading below 4-week average)
exit_conditions: PSX rallies 6% from short-entry price (stop-loss)
EIA 4-week average gasoline demand YoY decline shrinks to less than 2% (demand recovery)
8 calendar weeks elapsed from entry (time stop)

data_sources_concrete.prices: PSX, VLO, RB=F (RBOB front month), CL=F (WTI front month), SPY via yfinance daily
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report: Table 1, 'Motor Gasoline' product supplied (4-week average, Mbbl/d) — https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/ (free Thursday 10:30am). FRED: GASREGCOVW (US regular conventional gasoline retail, weekly, as cross-check).

backtest_approach: Build weekly series 2010-present: EIA gasoline product supplied 4-week avg (from EIA API or weekly XLS), YoY change computed vs same calendar week prior year. Flag signal weeks: YoY < -4% for 2 consecutive weeks. Enter short PSX at Friday open; also track VLO long leg for pair analysis. Track daily P&L until exit condition; dedup within 6-week lockout. Report PSX absolute returns and PSX-VLO pair returns (alpha above sector). Compare PSX to XOP and to gasoline crack spread (RB=F-CL=F) as corroboration.
known_events: 2020-03 (COVID lockdown: gasoline demand -30% YoY, PSX down 60%)
2022-Q2 (demand destruction from $5 gasoline prices, YoY -4% sustained, crack spread compressed)
2023-Q3 (post-summer demand normalization, YoY negative vs 2022 recovery, PSX relative weakness)
implementation_notes: Counter-signal idea (counters: long_crude,long_refiners) so PSX as primary short target is correct per spec. The pair trade (short PSX / long VLO) is cleaner than outright short: VLO has higher distillate/jet exposure that provides partial hedge against crude rallies. Backtester should test both legs. EIA API endpoint for product supplied: https://api.eia.gov/v2/petroleum/cons/psup/weekly/data/ (free key). PSX earnings reports (quarterly) may cause gaps; filter out entries within 5 days of PSX earnings dates. YoY comparison distorted by 2020 COVID baseline year — exclude 2021 data from signal (extreme base effects).

name: SEMI Equipment Book-to-Bill Rollover Below 1.0 — Short KLAC / LRCX
rule: Counter-signal to long-semis catalog entries. Entry: SEMI North America monthly book-to-bill ratio declines below 1.00 for 2 consecutive months after having been above 1.10 (rollover pattern). Enter short equal-weight KLAC and LRCX on the second consecutive sub-1.0 print, targeting highest-operating-leverage WFE names. Hold 6 weeks (30 trading days) or until SEMI B2B recovers above 1.05 for 2 consecutive months. Benchmark vs SOXX and SPY.
entry_conditions: SEMI North America book-to-bill ratio falls below 1.00 in current month AND was below 1.00 in prior month (2 consecutive sub-1.0 prints)
SEMI B2B was above 1.10 at some point in the trailing 6-month window (confirming rollover, not continuation of existing downturn)
KLAC or LRCX within 10% of 52-week high (position not yet fully repriced)
exit_conditions: 30 trading days elapsed from entry
SEMI B2B recovers above 1.05 for 2 consecutive months
KLAC or LRCX declines >25% from entry (profit-take / resize)
SOXX drops >20% from entry with VIX > 30 (macro risk-off, not equipment-specific)

data_sources_concrete.prices: KLAC, LRCX, AMAT, SOXX, SPY — all yfinance, full history from 2005-01-03
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: SEMI North America Equipment Book-to-Bill monthly press release (semi.org/en/products-services/market-data/book-to-bill — free public data, published monthly). Historical B2B data available in SEMI press release archive. FRED IPCONGD (Industrial Production Semiconductors) as corroborating macro series.

backtest_approach: Event-study: Identify all months 2005-2025 where SEMI B2B dropped below 1.0 for 2 consecutive months after a period above 1.10. Key episodes: Oct-Dec 2019, Aug 2022 through Jun 2023, and smaller episodes in 2015-2016 and 2011-2012. For each entry date, compute KLAC and LRCX 30-trading-day forward returns equal-weighted, vs SOXX and SPY benchmarks. SEMI B2B data requires manual digitization from press release archives; flag for backtester to pre-compile monthly series. Primary metric: mean excess return of KLAC+LRCX short vs SOXX over 30 trading days post-signal.
known_events: 2019-09: SEMI B2B hit 0.89 (2 consecutive months below 1.0 after >1.1 in 2018); KLAC fell ~30% in subsequent 6 months
2022-08: SEMI B2B declined below 1.0 through mid-2023; KLAC/LRCX fell 25-35% from peak
2015-11: B2B dropped below 1.0 on PC/mobile inventory correction; LRCX -20% over 3 months
implementation_notes: This is a counter-signal to long_semis catalog entries. KLAC and LRCX chosen over AMAT because they have highest operating leverage to WFE cycle (inspection/etch intensity). SOXX is the appropriate benchmark for a counter-semis signal; SPY included as broader market benchmark. SEMI B2B is a proxy for equipment bookings and requires digitizing from monthly press releases. Historical data available via SEMI website archive back to at least 2000. Note: KLAC ticker changed from KLAC-KLA Instruments pre-2019 merger; yfinance KLAC covers combined entity from 2019 onward; earlier data is KLA-Tencor (KLAC adjusted through the merger).

name: China DRAM/NAND Spot Undercut via BLS PPI Deflation — Short MU Gross Margin Compression
rule: Counter-signal to long-semis catalog entries targeting Micron specifically. Entry: BLS PPI series PCU334413334413 (Semiconductor & Related Devices) prints negative YoY for 2 consecutive months at -3% or worse, signaling broad commodity memory ASP deflation (driven by CXMT/YMTC China DRAM/NAND cost-dumping). Simultaneously, MU stock is within 15% of 12-month high (not pre-discounted). Short MU on confirmation; hold 8 weeks (40 trading days) or until BLS PPI semiconductor series turns positive YoY. Size: short MU, long SOXX as partial hedge to isolate MU-specific memory ASP exposure vs broader semis.
entry_conditions: BLS PPI PCU334413334413 (Semiconductor & Related Devices) YoY change <= -3% for 2 consecutive monthly prints
MU stock price within 15% of its 52-week high (position not yet fully discounting the margin compression)
MU trailing 12-month gross margin > 40% (gives room for downside estimate cuts)
SOXX not already in correction (SOXX within 20% of 52-week high) to isolate MU vs sector drag
exit_conditions: 40 trading days elapsed from entry
BLS PPI PCU334413334413 turns positive YoY (memory ASP cycle turns)
MU stock declines >30% from entry (profit-take / resize)
MU announces positive HBM revenue surprise that more than offsets commodity DRAM/NAND headwinds (earnings call exit)

data_sources_concrete.prices: MU (Micron Technology), SOXX (iShares Semiconductor ETF), SMH (VanEck Semiconductor ETF), SPY — all yfinance from 2005-01-03
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FRED series PCU334413334413 (BLS PPI Semiconductor & Related Devices, monthly, free via FRED API from 2000-present). TrendForce DRAMeXchange DRAM/NAND spot prices as corroborating signal (some free access at dramexchange.com, subscription for full history — use BLS PPI as primary signal for backtest).

backtest_approach: Event-study: Identify all months 2005-2025 where BLS PPI PCU334413334413 YoY was <= -3% for 2 consecutive months. Key episodes: 2008-2009, 2012, 2015-2016, 2019, 2022-2023. For each entry date, compute MU 40-trading-day forward returns vs SOXX and SPY. Primary metric: MU-short 40-day excess return vs SOXX (isolates MU-specific memory ASP exposure). Secondary: MU outright short return. Use FRED PCU334413334413 monthly data and yfinance MU daily prices. Note: TrendForce DRAM spot prices are the leading indicator but BLS PPI (monthly, lagged ~4-6 weeks) is the backtestable proxy. Backtester should pull PCU334413334413 via FRED API.
known_events: 2015-08: BLS PPI semis YoY -8%; MU fell from $30 to $10 (2015-2016 DRAM oversupply)
2019-03: BLS PPI semis YoY -5%; MU fell ~35% from Aug 2018 peak through May 2019
2022-Q3: BLS PPI semis turned negative; MU fell from $85 to $48 by Oct 2022 (2022 memory oversupply)
2023-Q1: CXMT DDR4 market flooding; MU guided FY2023 revenue down >50%; PPI semis -6% YoY
implementation_notes: Counter-signal to long_semis catalog entries, specifically targeting MU as the commodity DRAM/NAND-exposed name (distinct from HBM-focused plays like SK Hynix). BLS PPI PCU334413334413 is a lagging but clean backtestable proxy for what TrendForce DRAM spot prices signal in real-time. CXMT and YMTC are unlisted Chinese companies — no direct yfinance data, but their impact flows through into BLS PPI and MU earnings. The SOXX long hedge reduces systemic semiconductor sector exposure and isolates MU's commodity memory ASP risk. Note: MU has high DRAM/NAND revenue concentration (~60% commodity, ~40% HBM/specialty); HBM strength can partially offset commodity headwinds, which is why the entry condition requires MU near 52-week highs (market not yet pricing the commodity drag).

name: NAND PPI Deflation + OEM Inventory Build -> Short STX / WDC (Storage Hardware)
rule: Monthly, after BLS PPI release (typically mid-month): (1) Pull BLS PPI series PCU334112334112 (Computer Storage Device Manufacturing) YoY change. (2) Check if YoY <= -5% for 2+ consecutive months. (3) Cross-check IDC Quarterly PC Monitor (press release) for PC unit shipments: if PC units YoY <= 0% while NAND production estimates show >10% QoQ growth, inventory days are building. Entry trigger: BLS PPI storage deflation <= -5% YoY for 2+ months AND PC units flat/declining. Short equal-dollar STX and WDC at market open the day after BLS PPI release confirms signal. Exit: EITHER BLS PPI storage deflation turns > -2% YoY (trough forming) OR either stock rallies 8% from entry (stop-loss) OR 8 calendar weeks elapsed.
entry_conditions: BLS PPI PCU334112334112 (Computer Storage Device Manufacturing) YoY change <= -5% for 2+ consecutive monthly readings
IDC press-release PC shipments YoY <= 0% in the most recent quarterly report (demand weak, inventory accumulating)
exit_conditions: BLS PPI storage YoY deflation recovers to > -2% (signal weakening, floor forming)
STX or WDC rallies 8% from entry (stop-loss on either leg)
8 calendar weeks elapsed from entry (time stop)

data_sources_concrete.prices: STX, WDC, SPY via yfinance daily
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: BLS PPI series PCU334112334112 — Computer Storage Device Manufacturing YoY: access via FRED (series PCUAHAHAHAH not available; use BLS API v2 endpoint https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/PCU334112334112 — free registration). IDC Quarterly PC Monitor press release (free headlines at idc.com). FRED IPCONGD (Industrial Production: Computer and Electronic Products) as corroboration.

backtest_approach: Build monthly series 2005-present: BLS PPI PCU334112334112 YoY (from BLS API), IDC PC units YoY (from IDC press releases; approximate with FRED IPCONGD or Census NAICS shipments). Flag signal months where PPI storage YoY <= -5% for 2+ consecutive months AND PC units negative. Enter short equal-dollar STX+WDC at month+1 open. Track daily P&L. Dedup within 2-month lockout. Report pair-level and per-stock Sharpe, CAGR, max drawdown, hit rate. Compare to SMH (semiconductor ETF) as sector benchmark.
known_events: 2015-Q4 (NAND oversupply, PC shipment decline, STX/WDC both -30%+)
2019-Q1 (NAND/HDD price floor after 2018 glut, BLS PPI storage deeply negative)
2023-Q1 (post-COVID inventory glut: PC units -30% YoY, NAND ASPs collapsed, STX/WDC weak)
implementation_notes: BLS PPI series PCU334112334112 requires BLS API key (free at bls.gov); stores monthly. IDC data free only as quarterly press releases — exact shipment numbers available without paywall. Approximate PC demand with FRED series IPCONGD if IDC press releases are not machine-readable. STX is primarily HDD/nearline storage; WDC is HDD + NAND flash hybrid; both affected by NAND ASP collapse. Note: WDC underwent business restructuring / Kioxia merger talks 2023-2024; verify continuity.

name: USDA NASS Corn G/E >= 60% at Pollination -> Short ZC=F Counter-Signal
rule: Each Monday during July pollination window (calendar weeks 27-30, approx July 1 - July 28): (1) Pull USDA NASS weekly Crop Progress report (released Monday ~4pm ET) for Corn Good + Excellent condition %. (2) Check CFTC COT Disaggregated report (released Friday 3:30pm ET for prior Tuesday data): Managed Money Net position in CBOT Corn (ZC). Entry trigger: Corn G/E >= 60% during Weeks 27-30 AND CFTC Managed Money net-long > 150k contracts (confirming speculative weather premium is loaded). Short ZC=F at Tuesday open after Monday Crop Progress release. Position = 1 unit short ZC=F. Exit: EITHER ZC=F falls 5% from entry (profit target) OR Corn G/E drops below 55% (crop stress emerging, signal invalidated) OR day of August WASDE release (event-driven exit).
entry_conditions: USDA NASS Crop Progress: Corn Good + Excellent >= 60% during calendar Weeks 27-30 (July pollination window)
USDA G/E reading is >= 5 percentage points above the 5-year average for that same week
CFTC COT Disaggregated: Managed Money net-long position in CBOT Corn > 150,000 contracts (speculative weather premium in place)
exit_conditions: ZC=F falls 5% from entry price (profit target — weather premium unwind complete)
Corn G/E condition drops below 55% (crop stress emerging, signal invalidated — exit immediately)
August WASDE release date (hard event-driven exit regardless of P&L)

data_sources_concrete.prices: ZC=F (CBOT corn front-month), CORN (Teucrium Corn ETF as equity proxy), SPY via yfinance daily
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: USDA NASS Crop Progress weekly: https://www.nass.usda.gov/Publications/National_Crop_Progress/ (free, Monday 4pm ET release; PDF + XLS). CFTC COT Disaggregated Futures-Only: https://www.cftc.gov/MarketReports/CommitmentsofTraders/index.htm (free, Friday 3:30pm ET). USDA WASDE monthly: https://www.usda.gov/oce/commodity/wasde/ (event-driven exit date).

backtest_approach: Annual event study 2000-present: for each July, identify if Corn G/E >= 60% sustained across Weeks 27-30. Confirm CFTC COT managed-money net-long > 150k contracts at entry. Enter short ZC=F Tuesday after Crop Progress release confirming G/E >= 60%. Record ZC=F forward returns at 2w, 4w, 6w and at August WASDE date. Dedup: only 1 signal per July window per year. Compare short-ZC return to long-ZC buy-and-hold over same window. Report hit rate (% of July-G/E-high episodes where ZC falls), average return, Sharpe.
known_events: 2004 (Corn G/E ~73%, ZC fell into WASDE)
2014 (Corn G/E ~75% by Week 29 — one of the best crop ratings ever; ZC front-month fell sharply)
2016 (Corn G/E ~76% peak; ZC sold off through July-Aug)
2023 (Corn G/E recovered to 57% post-drought; marginal signal but useful as near-miss)
implementation_notes: Counter-signal idea (counters: long_corn,long_ZC) so ZC=F as primary short target is correct per spec. USDA Crop Progress XLS downloads at nass.usda.gov free. CFTC COT data free at cftc.gov in bulk CSV format (annual archives). ZC=F roll dates: corn futures roll quarterly (Mar/May/Jul/Sep/Dec); use front-month continuously rolled. CORN ETF (Teucrium) available since 2010 as equity-accessible proxy; ZC=F directly tradable for futures accounts. Signal only fires ~3-5 years per decade (requires exceptional crop condition AND speculative loading), so episode count will be modest (~10-15 events 2000-present).

name: USDA FAS Corn Export Commitment Pace >= 90% by Week 35 Signals WASDE Upward Revision: Long ZC=F
rule: Download USDA FAS Weekly Export Sales reports (ams.usda.gov/market-news/weekly-export-sales) each Thursday. Track cumulative marketing-year corn export sales (inspected + outstanding) as a percentage of the current USDA annual export projection from the most recent WASDE. Entry: when cumulative corn export commitment pace reaches >= 90% of the USDA annual export projection by Week 35 of the Sep-Aug marketing year (approximately early June), enter long ZC=F (CBOT front-month corn futures) at the next Friday open. Hold until day before the subsequent WASDE publication date (~12th of the month). Exit: close at the close of the trading day immediately preceding the WASDE release, or if ZC=F gains +4% (take profit), or if ZC=F loses -2.5% (stop-loss), whichever comes first. For equity alternative, use CORN ETF or ADM as proxy if futures unavailable.
entry_conditions: USDA FAS weekly export sales: cumulative marketing-year corn sales >= 90% of current USDA annual projection
Signal date is at or before Week 35 of the Sep-Aug marketing year (approximately early June)
No active WASDE release in the next 5 trading days (avoid release-day noise)
ZC=F 10-day average daily volume > 50,000 contracts (liquidity check)
exit_conditions: Exit at close of trading day before next WASDE publication date (~12th of month)
ZC=F cumulative gain >= +4% from entry (take profit)
ZC=F cumulative loss >= -2.5% from entry (stop-loss)
Weekly export sales pace reverses (drops below 85% of projection)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: ZC=F (CBOT corn front-month), ADM (archer-daniels-midland), SPY daily OHLCV
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: USDA FAS Weekly Export Sales Report (free, Thursday releases): https://apps.fas.usda.gov/gats/ExpressQuery1.aspx or ams.usda.gov/market-news/weekly-export-sales. USDA WASDE monthly corn supply/use table: https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/ for annual export projection. WASDE release calendar: https://www.usda.gov/oce/commodity/wasde/

backtest_approach: Event-study backtest on annual frequency: for each Sep-Aug marketing year from 2004 to present, check whether cumulative corn export sales reached >= 90% of USDA projection by Week 35. If yes, enter ZC=F at the Friday open after Week 35 report. Hold through the day before the following WASDE release (~2-3 weeks). Compute entry-to-exit return on ZC=F. Compare: (a) years when pace hit 90% by Week 35 vs. (b) years when it did not to measure the differential. Expected ~5-10 signal years in a 20-year backtest window. Also compute average ZC=F return in the ~3-week pre-WASDE window stratified by whether WASDE ultimately raised exports (to confirm the causal mechanism). Note: USDA FAS historical export sales data is publicly available in bulk download format from apps.fas.usda.gov.
known_events: 2012-06 (drought year, exports exceeded projection)
2021-06 (China buying surge)
2020-06 (COVID year strong pace)
implementation_notes: ZC=F is rolling front-month; backtester should handle contract rolls by using continuous adjusted price series. ADM equity is the best listed proxy if futures data unavailable. USDA WASDE is published monthly on a pre-announced schedule; calendar is available 12 months in advance. The 90% threshold and Week 35 cutoff are based on the idea thesis — the backtester should calibrate the optimal threshold in-sample. Marketing year for corn is September-August (Week 1 = first week of September). This is a pre-announcement drift strategy; enter before WASDE and exit on/before release.

name: USDA WASDE Soy Oil Stocks-to-Use <5% + EPA High RFS BBD Volume: Crush Margin Surge Long BG
rule: Monthly: after each WASDE release, check USDA global soybean oil ending stocks-to-use (STU). Separately check the EPA Renewable Fuel Standard final rule for current year biomass-based diesel (BBD) volume standard. Entry trigger: WASDE global soybean oil STU < 5% AND EPA BBD volume standard >= 3.0 billion gallons for current year AND CME soybean crush spread (ZL=F + ZM=F - ZS=F, using standard 11:11:1 board crush ratio proxy) is in the top quartile of its rolling 2-year distribution. Enter long BG (Bunge Ltd) at the next trading day open after all three conditions are met. Hold up to 60 trading days (12 calendar weeks). Exit: take profit at +20% BG gain, stop-loss at -10% BG loss, or time exit at 60 days. Also exit if WASDE global soybean oil STU reverts above 6% (tight conditions resolve).
entry_conditions: USDA WASDE global soybean oil ending stocks-to-use < 5% in most recent monthly release
EPA RFS final rule for current calendar year: biomass-based diesel (BBD) volume >= 3.0 billion gallons
CME soybean crush spread (11:11:1 proxy: ZL=F*11/100 + ZM=F/100 - ZS=F/100) in top quartile of rolling 104-week distribution
exit_conditions: Hold 60 trading days (~12 calendar weeks, primary time exit)
BG stock price gains +20% from entry (take profit)
BG stock price loses -10% from entry (stop-loss)
WASDE global soybean oil STU reverts to >= 6% (supply tightness resolves)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: BG, ADM, ZL=F, ZM=F, ZS=F, SPY daily OHLCV
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: USDA WASDE monthly soybean oil supply/use table: https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/app/index.html (PSD Online, free). EPA RFS annual volume standards (final rules): https://www.epa.gov/renewable-fuel-standard-program/regulations-and-volume-standards-under-rfs-program (annual final rule, published each November). Note: EPA BBD volumes are set for multi-year periods; the 3.0 billion gallon level has been in effect since the 2022 final rule cycle (2023+ program years).

backtest_approach: Monthly conditional event study: for each WASDE month from 2008 to present, check global soybean oil STU from PSD Online. For years where STU < 5% and EPA BBD >= 3.0B gal (applicable for 2023+ program years; for earlier years use BBD >= 2.0B gal as a lower threshold), enter BG at month-end close. Track BG returns vs ADM and SPY over 60-day hold window. Also track ZL=F (soy oil futures) returns in same windows to isolate equity-vs-commodity alpha. Note: the strict >= 3.0B BBD threshold limits to 2023+ data (only 2-3 years), so the backtester should run a broader version with STU < 6% + BBD >= 2.0B to get adequate sample size. Supplement with BG earnings revisions in tight-margin years to validate the mechanism. bt_feasibility is 3 due to short sample with both conditions simultaneously satisfied.
known_events: 2022-08 (post-IRA soybean oil demand spike)
2023-03 (WASDE tightening cycle)
2021-06 (early BBD ramp + tight STU)
implementation_notes: EPA RFS BBD volumes escalated: 2021=2.1B gal, 2022=2.76B gal, 2023=2.82B gal, 2024=3.35B gal (from final rules). The strict 3.0B gal threshold only applies post-2023. For a usable backtest (>5 events), use STU < 6% with EPA BBD in top tercile of the year's announced volume as the trigger. BG was taken private briefly in 2023 during Viterra merger discussions; verify continuous price data before 2024. ADM is a reasonable second-ticker parallel trade. The 11:11:1 crush ratio uses 11 pounds of oil + 11 pounds of meal from 1 bushel of soybeans — the standard CME product spec. Adjust units: ZL=F trades in cents/lb, ZM=F in $/short ton, ZS=F in cents/bushel.

name: MSTR mNAV Premium >3x Extreme Threshold — Short MSTR (Counter-Signal to Long BTC)
rule: Counter-signal to long-BTC catalog entries. Compute MSTR mNAV = MSTR market cap / (BTC holdings * BTC spot price). When mNAV > 3.0 for 5+ consecutive trading days, enter short MSTR. Cover at mNAV < 2.0 OR when BTC-USD 10-day return drops below -15% (premium already collapsed) OR 30 trading days elapsed, whichever comes first. MSTR BTC holdings count from most recent MSTR 8-K or quarterly filing (update when MSTR files new 8-K). Primary trade: short MSTR equity (most liquid, clean execution). Sizing: position sized at 0.5x normal as MSTR has extremely high idiosyncratic vol.
entry_conditions: MSTR mNAV (market_cap / (btc_holdings_count * BTC_spot)) > 3.0 for 5 consecutive trading days
BTC-USD trailing 30-day return > +20% (confirming the premium is driven by momentum, not fundamental re-rating)
MSTR 20-day realized volatility > 60% annualized (premium elevated, not just stable high valuation)
exit_conditions: MSTR mNAV drops below 2.0 (premium compression target reached)
BTC-USD declines >15% from entry date (catalyst for mNAV compression already unfolding)
30 trading days elapsed from entry
MSTR announces major new BTC purchase reducing the outstanding share float (positive reflexivity event)

data_sources_concrete.prices: MSTR (MicroStrategy) yfinance from 2018-01-02; BTC-USD yfinance from 2014-09-17; IBIT (iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF) yfinance from 2024-01-11; SPY benchmark
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: MSTR BTC holdings count: saylor.org/bitcoin (free public tracker) or MSTR 8-K filings on SEC EDGAR (RSS feed for real-time updates). Historical BTC holdings by quarter available from MSTR investor relations page. No FRED series needed.

backtest_approach: Compute daily MSTR mNAV from August 2020 (when MSTR began BTC purchases) through 2025, using yfinance MSTR prices and BTC-USD prices, combined with quarterly BTC holdings count from MSTR 8-K filings. Identify all 5-consecutive-day windows where mNAV > 3.0. Key episodes: Nov-Dec 2021 (mNAV ~5x peak), Nov 2024 (mNAV ~3.5x), Jan 2025 (mNAV ~3.2x). For each entry date, compute MSTR 30-trading-day forward return and compare to BTC-USD return (to isolate the premium compression alpha vs raw BTC direction). Primary metric: MSTR short excess return vs BTC-USD over 30 days. Note: mNAV data requires combining price data with holdings from SEC filings — backtester must pre-compile quarterly BTC holdings CSV.
known_events: 2021-11-09: MSTR mNAV peaked ~4.5x as BTC approached $68K; MSTR fell 70% over next 6 months while BTC fell 75%
2024-11-20: MSTR mNAV hit ~3.5x; MSTR fell ~40% over following 6 weeks while BTC was flat-to-down 15%
2025-01-15: mNAV ~3.2x; MSTR underperformed BTC by 25 percentage points over following 30 days
implementation_notes: MSTR BTC holdings requires manual data compilation from 8-K filings; key holding counts: 21,454 BTC (Aug 2020), 70,470 (Dec 2020), 105,085 (Jun 2021), 129,218 (Sep 2021), 130,000 (Dec 2021), 152,333 (Mar 2022), 158,245 (Nov 2022), 189,150 (Jun 2023), 244,800 (Dec 2024). Backtester should build a time-series of holdings by quarter and linearly interpolate between 8-K dates for daily mNAV computation. IBIT is only from Jan 2024 so use MSTR as primary backtest vehicle. This signal is distinct from PL637 (CME futures basis compression) — that fires on carry collapse; this fires on mNAV premium itself.

name: Crypto Fear & Greed Sustained Extreme Greed (>=85 for 5d) — Short IBIT
rule: Counter-signal to long-BTC catalog entries. Entry: Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads >= 85 (Extreme Greed) for 5 or more consecutive trading days. Enter short IBIT (or short BTC-USD equivalent for backtest). Hold 21 calendar days or until Fear & Greed Index drops below 60 (neutral territory), whichever comes first. Exit early if BTC-USD drops >15% from entry (position already profitable, take profits). Sizing: 1x standard position due to high BTC volatility. Primary trade vehicle: short IBIT (most liquid listed BTC short vehicle for equities accounts).
entry_conditions: Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index >= 85 for 5 consecutive calendar days (free daily JSON API at api.alternative.me/fng/)
BTC-USD trailing 30-day return >= +20% (confirming the greed is momentum-driven)
IBIT (or BTC-USD) within 5% of 30-day high (not already correcting)
exit_conditions: 21 calendar days elapsed from entry
Alternative.me Fear & Greed Index drops below 60 for 2 consecutive days
BTC-USD declines > 15% from entry date (aggressive profit-take trigger)
VIX spikes above 35 (macro risk-off event; signal is sentiment-specific, not macro crash)

data_sources_concrete.prices: IBIT (iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF) yfinance from 2024-01-11; BTC-USD yfinance from 2014-09-17 (use BTC-USD for full-history backtest); SPY as benchmark
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index: free daily JSON API (api.alternative.me/fng/?limit=2000&format=json) and historical CSV download. Full history from 2018-02-01. No FRED series needed.

backtest_approach: Download full Alternative.me Fear & Greed Index history (2018-2025) from free API or CSV. Identify all instances where index reads >= 85 for 5+ consecutive days. Key episodes: Dec 2017, Dec 2020, Feb 2021, Nov 2021, Nov 2024, Jan 2025. For each entry date, compute BTC-USD 21-calendar-day forward return (use BTC-USD for full history, IBIT for 2024+ validation). Primary metric: mean 21-day BTC-USD return following signal vs all 21-day periods as benchmark. Compare to H01 (perp funding), H06 (MVRV), and other BTC counter-signals in catalog to check for correlation. IBIT data from Jan 2024 can be used for out-of-sample validation of 2024-2025 events.
known_events: 2021-11-08: Fear & Greed hit 84+ for 6 days; BTC peaked at $68K and fell 40% over next 6 weeks
2024-11-22: Fear & Greed hit 88 for 5+ consecutive days; BTC fell 15% over following 3 weeks
2021-02-20: Fear & Greed sustained >=85 for 7 days; BTC corrected 20% within 3 weeks
2025-01-18: Fear & Greed hit 85 for 5 days; BTC fell 12% over following 14 days
implementation_notes: bt_feasibility=5 because both data sources (BTC-USD via yfinance, Fear & Greed via free API) are directly machine-readable with no paywall. IBIT only from Jan 2024 — use BTC-USD for full backtest; validate with IBIT for 2024+ out-of-sample. Approximately 8-12 qualifying events in the 2018-2025 window. Distinct from H06 (MVRV z-score) and H01 (perpetual funding rate) — this is a multi-input sentiment composite vs single on-chain or derivatives metrics. Backtester should call api.alternative.me/fng/?limit=2000&format=json or download CSV from Alternative.me to get full history.

name: FDA REMS Termination → Prescriber Access Broadens → Sponsor Equity Long
rule: When FDA formally terminates or materially simplifies a REMS program for a single-sponsor drug (publication in FDA's REMS@FDA database and/or Federal Register), go long the sponsoring company's equity within 3 trading days of the termination notice. Hold for 60 calendar days or until a 25% adverse move (stop loss). Size at equal weight per event. Exclude events where: (a) the sponsor has market cap <$500M, (b) the drug accounts for <10% of sponsor revenues (immaterial), or (c) the company was acquired/merged within the backtest period. Benchmark: long XBI for the same window.
entry_conditions: FDA REMS@FDA database shows termination or ETASU-removal modification published for a specific drug
Sponsor equity is publicly traded on US exchange with market cap ≥$500M
Drug at issue accounts for ≥10% of sponsor's reported revenue (material)
Entry within 3 trading days of FDA publication date
exit_conditions: 60 calendar days have elapsed since entry
Adverse price move of 25% or more from entry (stop loss)
Sponsor announces reacquisition / merger event (hard exit)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: ALKS, BIIB, JAZZ, BMY, SUPN, ACAD, CPRX, XBI, SPY
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FDA REMS@FDA database termination history (manual date compilation): https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/rems/index.cfm; Federal Register REMS notices: https://www.federalregister.gov/search?conditions[term]=REMS+termination

backtest_approach: Event-study PnL. Curated list of FDA REMS termination dates 2010-2025 mapped to sponsor tickers (approximately 15-25 events in total). For each event: compute excess return (sponsor return minus XBI return) over the 60-day holding period starting T+1. Pool all events into a single equal-weighted portfolio. Compute arithmetic mean excess return, t-stat (one-sample vs zero), and Sharpe of event returns. Report per-event attribution to flag MRK/BIIB outliers. Also report median return to check for skew. Known seed events: Vivitrol/ALKS ~May 2011; Tysabri/BIIB Sept 2017; Xyrem/JAZZ REMS simplification 2018; Abstral/Galena 2019; opioid REMS consolidation 2022.
implementation_notes: REMS terminations are rare (roughly 5-10 material events per 5-year window). Backtester should compile the full FDA REMS terminated-programs list from: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/rems/index.cfm?event=IndvReports.page&REMS=Terminated and cross-reference sponsor revenue impact before including each event. bt_feasibility=3: event count is low and compilation is manual, but FDA data is free. If event count is below 10 after filtering, report the strategy as 'insufficient sample' and fall back to a 10-day excess return window for more granular analysis. Specific companies (ALKS, BIIB, JAZZ) are primary targets — not XBI/XLV baskets — because each REMS termination is drug- and sponsor-specific.

name: FDA FAERS PRR Signal-Cluster → Post-Market Safety Review → Drug Sponsor Short
rule: Counter-signal to crowded long single biotech/pharma. When FDA's quarterly FAERS data release shows a PRR ≥ 2 with n ≥ 3 adverse event reports AND Chi-squared ≥ 4 for a serious drug-event pair for a specific publicly-traded sponsor (US exchange, market cap ≥$1B), short the sponsor equity within 5 trading days of FAERS data release. Cover at 90 calendar days or upon FDA Drug Safety Communication / label-change event (take profit), whichever comes first. Size at equal-weight per event; stop loss at +15% adverse move from entry. Exclude: (a) generic manufacturers (mechanism is brand-specific), (b) drug accounts for <15% sponsor revenues.
entry_conditions: FDA FAERS quarterly data release (published on FDA website) shows PRR ≥ 2, n ≥ 3, Chi-sq ≥ 4 for a specific drug-event pair
Drug is a brand-name product of a publicly-traded sponsor with market cap ≥ $1B
Drug at issue accounts for ≥ 15% of sponsor's reported revenues (material risk)
No FDA Drug Safety Communication for this drug-event pair has already been issued (avoid post-event short)
Entry within 5 trading days of FAERS data release date
exit_conditions: 90 calendar days elapsed since entry (time stop)
FDA Drug Safety Communication or label change event published (take profit; close at next open)
Adverse (upward) price move of 15% from entry (stop loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: MRK, GSK, JNJ, AZN, BMY, PFE, ABBV, ACAD, SRPT, IBB, SPY
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FDA FAERS quarterly data files (free CSV download, 2004-present): https://fis.fda.gov/extensions/FPD-QDE-FAERS/FPD-QDE-FAERS.html; openFDA FAERS API: https://open.fda.gov/apis/drug/event/; FDA Drug Safety Communications: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/drug-safety-communications

backtest_approach: Event-study PnL. Build anchor event set from known major FAERS-signal-to-label-change episodes (2004-2024): Vioxx/MRK 2004-09-30, Avandia/GSK 2007-05-21, Onglyza/AZN 2016-04-26, Zantac/NDMA signal ~2019-04-01 (for Pfizer's ranitidine brands), Invokana/JNJ amputation warning 2016-05-16, Abilify/BMY compulsive behavior warning 2016-05-03. For each event: FAERS quarterly data availability date (T0) → short entry T0+1, compute sponsor return vs IBB over 90-day window. Pool events; compute equal-weight mean excess return, t-stat, and Sharpe. Note: the full quantitative pipeline (parse FAERS CSV, compute PRR per drug-event pair, flag threshold crossings) is the production trigger; for backtesting purposes, the anchor event set is a proxy. The bt_feasibility=4 reflects that FAERS data is free but PRR computation requires CSV parsing.
implementation_notes: This is a counter-signal: targets sponsors with crowded long consensus positions where FAERS safety data suggests material downside from regulatory action. The PRR calculation requires downloading FAERS quarterly CSV files and parsing DRUG/REAC tables — backtester should implement this as a data pipeline step or use the curated anchor events above as a proxy. Market cap filter (≥$1B) excludes small-cap biotech where adverse event risk is well-known to market. Primary short targets are large-cap pharma (MRK, GSK, JNJ, AZN, BMY, PFE, ABBV) where FAERS signal represents true information asymmetry — not XBI/IBB baskets. FAERS data has a known 90-day reporting lag; entry timing is FAERS release date, not the adverse event date. bt_feasibility=4 from scout.

name: BTC Dominance Rapid Spike >62% (Altcoin Capitulation) Counter-Signal: Short COIN
rule: This is a counter-signal strategy (counters long_BTC). Track BTC dominance daily (BTC market cap / total crypto market cap) from CoinGecko or CoinMarketCap free API. Entry: when BTC dominance rises >= 5 percentage points in any rolling 10-day window AND crosses above 62% for the first time in at least 60 days, enter short COIN (Coinbase Global). Entry at the next trading day open after the dominance signal triggers. Hold up to 45 trading days (~9 calendar weeks). Exit: cover short when BTC dominance reverts below 58% (altcoin recovery signal), or COIN drops -20% from entry (take profit on short), or COIN rises +12% against the short (stop-loss), or 45 trading days have elapsed, whichever comes first. Do not enter if COIN earnings are within 14 days.
entry_conditions: BTC dominance rises >= 5 percentage points in rolling 10-day window AND crosses above 62%
BTC dominance was below 62% for at least 60 consecutive prior days
COIN 20-day average daily volume > 5M shares
COIN earnings date is NOT within the next 14 trading days
exit_conditions: Hold 45 trading days (~9 weeks, primary time exit)
BTC dominance reverts to < 58% (altcoin recovery)
COIN short profits reach +20% from entry (take profit)
COIN short losses reach +12% vs entry (stop-loss, cover short)
COIN quarterly earnings release within 2 days

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: COIN, BTC-USD, IBIT, SPY daily OHLCV
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: BTC dominance daily: CoinGecko Global API (free): https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/global (returns BTC dominance %). Historical dominance: CoinMarketCap global chart CSV export (free). COIN transaction revenue by asset class: Coinbase quarterly earnings supplements (SEC EDGAR CIK 0001682852, 10-Q/10-K Exhibit 99.1).

backtest_approach: Event-study backtest: compile daily BTC dominance history from CoinGecko/CoinMarketCap (available 2013-present free). Identify all dates where dominance spikes >= 5pp in 10 days AND crosses above 62% from below (after 60+ day sub-62% regime). For each event, track COIN returns (only from COIN IPO: April 14, 2021 forward). Compare COIN returns in the 45-day post-signal window vs BTC-USD and SPY benchmark. Expected: 3-6 events in the 2021-2025 COIN-data window. bt_feasibility=3 due to limited COIN history (~5 signal events max).
known_events: 2021-05-19 (crypto crash, BTC dominance spike to 62%)
2022-06-13 (LUNA/3AC crisis, BTC dominance spike)
2023-03-10 (SVB/Silvergate banking crisis, BTC dominance above 62%)
2025-01 (post-election altcoin correction)
implementation_notes: Counter-signal strategy -- COIN short is intentional (counters long_BTC complacency). COIN IPO was April 14, 2021; backtest window is only ~4-5 years. BTC dominance: CoinGecko global.bitcoin.market_cap_percentage (JSON API, free). The short setup: assume borrow cost 2-4% annualized in backtesting. bt_feasibility is 3 due to limited COIN history (2021-present only).

name: FDA PDUFA No-AdComm Pre-Approval Drift: Long Sponsor 8 Weeks Before Action Date
rule: Compile FDA PDUFA action dates and verify no Advisory Committee meeting was scheduled. Entry: 40 trading days (8 calendar weeks) before the PDUFA action date, enter long the sponsor equity if: (1) no AdComm has been scheduled, (2) sponsor market cap > $1B, (3) sponsor 20-day ADV > 500K shares. Exit: 2 trading days before the PDUFA action date. Stop-loss: if sponsor loses -15% from entry, exit immediately. Size: max 5% of portfolio per event.
entry_conditions: FDA PDUFA action date is 40 trading days in the future
No Advisory Committee meeting scheduled in Federal Register for this NDA/BLA
Sponsor market cap > $1B at entry date
Sponsor 20-day average daily volume > 500K shares
Sponsor stock has not already rallied >20% in prior 20 days
exit_conditions: Exit at close T-2 trading days before PDUFA action date (primary time exit)
Sponsor stock loses -15% from entry (stop-loss)
AdComm unexpectedly scheduled -- exit within 1 day of Federal Register notice
FDA issues complete response letter or refuses to file before action date

data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FDA PDUFA calendar: https://www.fda.gov/patients/drug-development-process/step-4-fda-drug-review. Federal Register AdComm notices: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/search.
