Historical AdComm records: https://www.fda.gov/advisory-committees/committees-and-meeting-materials.

backtest_approach: Curated event study: compile PDUFA action dates from 2010-2025 for major sponsors (Pfizer, Eli Lilly, Vertex, Regeneron, AbbVie, BMS, Merck) with market cap > $5B. Classify each event as no-AdComm vs AdComm-held. For no-AdComm events: enter sponsor at T-40 trading days, track daily returns through T-2. Compare mean/median return for no-AdComm vs AdComm events. Use XBI as benchmark. Expected: 30-60+ curated events over 15 years. Known events for seeding: VRTX Trikafta 2019-10-21, LLY tirzepatide 2023-05-13, MRNA mRNA-1273 2022-01-31.
known_events: 2019-10-21 VRTX Trikafta PDUFA (no AdComm, approved)
2023-05-13 LLY tirzepatide obesity PDUFA (no AdComm, approved)
2022-01-31 MRNA mRNA-1273 adult booster PDUFA (no AdComm, approved)
2021-08-23 PFE BNT162b2 full approval PDUFA (no AdComm, approved)
2023-07-06 REGN dupilumab COPD PDUFA (no AdComm, approved)
implementation_notes: This strategy requires a curated PDUFA date table as input -- the backtester must build or use a pre-compiled dataset. FDA does not provide a machine-readable historical PDUFA database; dates must be assembled from press releases, 8-K filings, and the FDA approvals archive. Use the known_events list as seeds. bt_feasibility is 4 because data compilation is labor-intensive but publicly available. AdComm absence confirmation: check Federal Register 8 weeks and again 4 weeks before date. The T-40 to T-2 window captures pre-announcement drift without binary event risk. The sponsor tickers listed are examples; applies to any eligible sponsor. XBI is included as benchmark proxy only, not the primary target.

name: DOJ/FTC Preliminary Injunction Filing — Acquirer Short
rule: Enter SHORT on the acquirer stock within 2 trading days of DOJ Antitrust Division OR FTC filing a preliminary injunction complaint in district court to block a pending merger (trial date scheduled by court). Position size: 5% of portfolio notional. Exit SHORT at the earlier of: (a) trial verdict day, (b) deal termination announcement, or (c) 120 calendar days from entry. Benchmark hedge: maintain equal-notional SPY long to isolate deal-specific alpha from broad-market moves. Known historical events (event study seed dates): AT&T/TWX DOJ filing 2017-11-20 (T); Aetna/Humana DOJ filing 2016-07-21 (AET - use HUM proxy due to AET delisting); Anthem/Cigna DOJ filing 2016-07-21 (ANTM); Microsoft/Activision FTC PI filing 2023-04-26 (MSFT); Adobe/Figma DOJ challenge Oct 2023 - abandoned 2023-12-18 (ADBE); Kroger/Albertsons FTC PI filing 2024-02-26 (KR). Measure: 5-day, 10-day, 20-day, 60-day acquirer returns vs. SPY from entry date.
entry_conditions: DOJ or FTC files preliminary injunction complaint in U.S. District Court to block merger (public PACER/justice.gov/ftc.gov press release)
Court issues scheduling order setting trial date 4-9 months out
Trade entered within 2 trading days of press release / court filing date
Target company deal spread has widened > 200 bps from announced deal price (confirms market has not already fully discounted)
Acquirer market cap > B (liquid enough for short execution)
exit_conditions: Trial verdict announced (acquirer wins -> cover; acquirer loses -> cover at gap)
Deal terminated by either party (cover immediately on announcement)
120 calendar days elapsed from entry (time stop regardless of outcome)
Acquirer stock drops > 15% from entry (take profits — excessive move suggests market pricing a different shock)

data_sources_concrete.fundamental: justice.gov/atr case list; ftc.gov/news/press-releases; PACER/CourtListener RECAP API for filing dates

backtest_approach: Event-study backtest seeded on 6 historical DOJ/FTC PI filing dates (2016-2024). For each event: pull acquirer daily OHLCV from yfinance (these are surviving entities — all listed). Compute acquirer excess return vs SPY (equal-notional long SPY hedge) over windows: t+1, t+5, t+10, t+20, t+60 days from the press-release date. Average excess returns across events. Track drawdown and win-rate. Note: AET (Aetna) delisted post-CVS merger — substitute with CI (Cigna) for the Anthem/Cigna event. Adobe/Figma deal was abandoned (no trial) — entry is on DOJ challenge announcement, exit on deal termination announcement.
implementation_notes: Use CI for the 2016 DOJ dual-filing event (Anthem/Cigna). ANTM renamed to ELV — use ELV ticker which has full history back to 2004. Adobe/Figma case: ADBE data available; deal terminated Dec 18 2023 (use as exit date). Kroger/Albertsons FTC case: KR data available through 2025; deal terminated in 2024. Short position requires locating borrow — all these names are megacap/large-cap with ample borrow. This is a counter_signal strategy (counters long-SPY / long-quality) so SPY primary target is appropriate for the hedge leg.

name: EPA MATS Coal Compliance Capex Overhang → Short SO / Long XLU Pair
rule: Counter-signal to long XLU / long SO. When EPA finalizes a new or tightened coal air toxics regulation (MATS, CSAPR, or equivalent Federal Register final rule imposing Hg/HCl/SO2 limits), short Southern Company (SO) and simultaneously go long XLU (utility sector ETF) as a dollar-neutral pair trade. Entry within 5 trading days of Federal Register effective date. Hold for 180 calendar days or until SO's annual capex guidance explicitly absorbs the compliance cost (next annual earnings call referencing MATS compliance budget), whichever comes first. Stop loss: close the pair if SO outperforms XLU by more than 12% (adverse move). Size: 1x notional in each leg (dollar-neutral pair).
entry_conditions: EPA publishes final rule in Federal Register tightening coal air toxics (Hg, HCl, SO2, PM) limits applicable to existing coal units
Southern Company has ≥5 GW of coal generation in service (from EIA Form 860 data) — confirming material compliance exposure
SO market cap ≥ $30B (ensuring liquidity for the short leg)
Entry within 5 trading days of EPA final rule effective date
exit_conditions: 180 calendar days elapsed since entry (time stop)
SO outperforms XLU by 12% or more cumulatively from entry (pair stop loss)
SO annual earnings call explicitly guides to specific MATS compliance capex absorbed in rate base (take profit signal)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: SO, XLU, AEP, DUK, NEE, SPY
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: EPA Federal Register final rules: EPA MATS original rule (77 FR 9304, Feb 2012 effective); EPA CSAPR final rule (76 FR 48208, Aug 2011); EPA MATS update (89 FR 27970, Apr 2024 effective); EIA Form 860 for SO coal fleet size: https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860/

backtest_approach: Pair trade excess-return event study. Anchor events (EPA final rule dates): (1) Original MATS rule effective Feb 16, 2012 (announced Dec 21, 2011) — SO vs XLU pair; (2) CSAPR rule effective Jan 1, 2012 (announced Aug 3, 2011) — SO vs XLU pair; (3) MATS update effective Apr 25, 2024 (announced Apr 25, 2024) — SO vs XLU pair (forward-looking anchor). For each event, compute SO cumulative return minus XLU cumulative return over 180-day window starting T+1. Also run with AEP (high coal exposure at CSAPR/original MATS) vs NEE (low coal) as alternative pair. Report: mean pair excess return, individual event returns, t-stat. Note: only 2-3 historical analogs; results will be directionally informative but statistically limited. The 2024 MATS update is the primary live signal.
implementation_notes: Primary target is SO (Southern Company) specifically — not a generic utility basket — because SO has the largest residual coal fleet (~9 GW as of 2023 EIA Form 860) among investment-grade regulated IOUs. AEP is the secondary candidate (also high coal exposure historically, though rapidly retiring). NEE (nuclear/wind heavy) is a natural long complement if dollar-neutral pair with AEP is preferred over XLU. The 2024 MATS update thesis is forward-looking (compliance by 2028) — the backtest anchors at rule announcement date as the market-observable trigger. bt_feasibility=4: EPA rule dates are free/public, yfinance data is clean for SO/XLU/AEP/NEE back to 2000. Sample size is limited (2-3 events); report confidence intervals accordingly.

name: FERC GHG Certificate Weighing — Short LNG Feed-Gas Dependent Operator (NFE)
rule: Enter SHORT NFE (New Fortress Energy) and LONG XLE (Energy Select Sector SPDR) in equal notional within 5 trading days of FERC issuing a Certificate Policy Statement or Order that explicitly requires GHG downstream emissions weighing for interstate natural gas pipeline applications — specifically PL18-1-000 (March 24, 2022) and subsequent certificate application delays/denials for pipelines serving LNG export terminals. Position: Short 5% NFE / Long 5% XLE. Exit: (a) 18 months from entry, (b) FERC policy reversed by court (D.C. Circuit) or new Commission order, or (c) NFE announces successful commissioning of Fast LNG project. Benchmark: SPY for overall excess return calculation.
entry_conditions: FERC issues Certificate Policy Statement with explicit GHG/climate emissions weighing requirement (FERC eLibrary docket PL18-1)
NFE has ≥1 pending FERC certificate application for feed-gas pipeline serving an LNG export terminal
NFE Debt/EBITDA > 6x (high leverage amplifies project delay NPV impact)
NFE stock has NOT already declined > 40% in prior 60 days (avoid late-cycle short entry)
Entry within 5 trading days of FERC policy order publication date
exit_conditions: 18 calendar months elapsed from entry (time stop)
FERC policy reversed by court order or new Commission vote removing GHG weighing requirement
NFE announces Fast LNG commercial operations / first cargo delivery (de-risking the project delays)
NFE stock drops > 60% from entry (take partial profits, reassess leverage/covenant situation)
NFE debt restructuring or Chapter 11 filing (exit — event risk too binary)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: NFE (2019-present), XLE (2001-present), SPY (1993-present)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FERC eLibrary docket PL18-1-000 (ferc.gov); NFE 10-K/10-Q Debt/EBITDA; FRED: none required

backtest_approach: Single event-study entry: March 24, 2022 (FERC PL18-1-000 issuance). Pull NFE and XLE daily OHLCV from yfinance. Construct short NFE / long XLE equal-notional pairs trade from March 28, 2022 (T+2 from policy). Track pair P&L monthly through exit (18-month stop = Sept 2023 or earlier exit). Supplement with 2-3 secondary event dates when FERC issued delays on specific NFE-linked pipeline applications (FERC docket CP22-558 and related). Compute CAGR, max drawdown, Sharpe for the pair. Note: limited to 1-2 historical events so treat as case study + forward hypothesis; emphasize qualitative mechanism validation alongside quantitative P&L.
implementation_notes: NFE closed at ~ on March 24, 2022 and fell to ~/bin/zsh.69 by April 2026 — the macro energy crisis provided a strong headwind to the short in H1 2022, but the pair trade vs XLE would have been profitable from mid-2022 onwards as energy sector held while NFE collapsed. Key confound: NFE decline was driven by multiple factors beyond FERC (over-leverage, Fast LNG cost overruns, Hilli contract expiry). FERC is a specific trigger catalyst but not the only factor. Disclose in backtest commentary. Counter-signal (counters long_XLE): XLE long as hedge leg is the desired behavior per spec. Use equal-dollar short NFE / long XLE to isolate the sector-relative short.

name: Credit Spread Complacency (HY OAS <300bps) → Short KRE / Long IEF Pair
rule: Counter-signal to long-credit / long-equity convergence. When FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 (HY OAS) falls below 300bps AND has been declining for ≥8 consecutive weeks (i.e. credit complacency regime, not merely tight spreads after a spike), simultaneously: short KRE (Regional Bank ETF) and long IEF (7-10yr Treasury ETF) in a 1:1 dollar-neutral pair. Hold for 42 calendar days (6 weeks) or until HY OAS widens back above 375bps (trend reversal), whichever comes first. Stop loss: close pair if KRE outperforms IEF by 10% from entry (adverse pair move). Note: this is the OPPOSITE of PL115 (which goes long KRE on spread normalization).
entry_conditions: FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 (HY OAS) reading < 300bps in the latest week
HY OAS has declined (from higher level) in at least 8 of the prior 10 weekly observations — confirming persistent complacency trend, not just brief dip
KRE 20-day realized vol < 25% (low-vol regime; avoid entry during known-stress periods)
No active FDIC special supervisory alert or prior-quarter banking crisis flag in effect
exit_conditions: 42 calendar days elapsed since entry (time stop)
HY OAS widens back above 375bps (credit regime reversal; close immediately)
KRE outperforms IEF by 10% or more cumulatively from entry (pair stop loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: KRE, IEF, SPY
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 (ICE BofA US High Yield Index OAS, weekly/daily): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/BAMLH0A0HYM2

backtest_approach: Dollar-neutral pair trade event study. Pull BAMLH0A0HYM2 from FRED; identify all weekly dates where OAS < 300bps AND declining trend (8/10 weeks declining). These windows occurred approximately in: 2004-2007 (pre-GFC complacency), 2013-2014 (post-taper), 2017-2018 (QE regime), 2021 (post-COVID). For each signal trigger date: go short KRE + long IEF simultaneously in equal notional; compute daily pair PnL (IEF return - KRE return) over 42-day hold. Aggregate all trade windows (de-duplicate consecutive weekly triggers, minimum 3-week gap between entries). Report: trade-level excess returns, equal-weight mean, Sharpe, max drawdown, win rate. Benchmark: short KRE alone vs long SPY (to isolate duration vs credit component of the pair).
implementation_notes: Counter-signal: fires against long-credit/long-equity consensus. IMPORTANT: This is directionally OPPOSITE to PL115 (which goes LONG KRE on spread normalization/widening). No overlap: PL115 triggers when OAS drops below 400bps after being above 500bps; PL1022 triggers when OAS is in persistent sub-300bps complacency regime. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 note: series is in percent (not bps), so 3.00 = 300bps, 4.00 = 400bps. The CMBS-specific series cited in the original idea (BAMLC8A0C15PYTRIV/BAMLC5A0C57PYTRIV) are incorrect FRED IDs (those are IG corporate total return indices, not CMBS OAS). BAMLH0A0HYM2 is a valid and commonly used credit complacency proxy; Trepp CMBS delinquency data (paid) would be a better direct signal but is not freely available.

name: CFTC COT Gold Managed-Money Extreme Long (>300K contracts) → Short GLD Sentiment Fade
rule: Counter-signal to crowded long-gold consensus. When CFTC Disaggregated COT weekly report shows managed-money net-long position in COMEX gold futures (contract code 088691) crosses above 300,000 net contracts AND is more than 2.0 standard deviations above its trailing 156-week (3-year) mean, short GLD within 2 trading days of CFTC report publication (released each Friday for the prior Tuesday's positions). Cover when managed-money net-long reverts below 200,000 contracts (mean reversion) OR after 56 calendar days (8 weeks), whichever comes first. Stop loss: cover if GLD gains 8% or more from entry (adverse move). Size: 1x notional in GLD short.
entry_conditions: CFTC Disaggregated COT (Futures Only) report: COMEX gold managed-money net-long > 300,000 contracts
Net-long position > (trailing 156-week mean + 2.0 * trailing 156-week stdev) — confirming statistical extremity
GLD 20-day momentum positive (price above 20-day SMA) — ensures entry into an overbought regime, not into a falling knife
Short entry within 2 trading days of Friday CFTC COT publication
exit_conditions: CFTC COT managed-money net-long reverts below 200,000 contracts (take profit)
56 calendar days elapsed since entry (time stop)
GLD gains 8% from entry price (stop loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: GLD, GC=F, SPY
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: CFTC Disaggregated COT historical data (free annual ZIP downloads): https://www.cftc.gov/MarketReports/CommitmentsofTraders/HistoricalCompressed/index.htm; Current weekly report: https://www.cftc.gov/MarketReports/CommitmentsofTraders/index.htm; Gold (COMEX) commodity code: 088691. Columns: Managed Money Positions Long/Short/Spreading from Disagg_Fut_Only reports.

backtest_approach: Weekly signal-based strategy. Download CFTC Disaggregated COT annual ZIP files (2006-2025) and extract COMEX gold managed-money long/short columns for contract code 088691. Compute net position (Long - Short), rolling 156-week mean and stdev. Flag signal weeks where net > 300K AND net > (mean + 2*stdev). For each signal: short GLD from T+3 (Friday publication + 2 trading days), compute daily PnL over 56-day holding period or until net reversion below 200K. De-duplicate consecutive weekly triggers (minimum 3-week gap between entries). Known extreme positioning periods: Aug-Oct 2011 (~200K, gold topped at $1920), Jul-Aug 2020 (~350K+ net, gold topped at $2070 before -9% correction), Oct 2019 (~300K net before modest correction). Report: per-trade returns, equal-weight mean, Sharpe, max drawdown.
implementation_notes: This is a counter-signal to the crowded long-gold thesis (e.g., PL62 M2-gold, PL187 debt/GDP-gold, etc.). Counter-signal so GLD (not SPY/QQQ) is the primary short target — correct behavior per spec. CFTC COT data is free but requires manual download of annual ZIP files; Disaggregated Futures Only report starts in 2006. Note: the 300K threshold is approximate — backtester should calibrate the 2-sigma threshold dynamically from the rolling 3-year window rather than using a fixed 300K absolute level. The 2020 episode is the strongest analog (net ~350K, gold -9% over subsequent 8 weeks). 2011 net was lower (~200K) due to smaller market; sigma adjustment handles this correctly. GLD covers the full 2006-present period with clean data.

name: LME Zinc Backwardation (Smelter Cut Signal) — Long HBM / TECK
rule: Enter LONG HBM (Hudbay Minerals) and LONG TECK (Teck Resources Class B) in equal notional when FRED monthly zinc price (PZINCUSDM) rises > 10% month-over-month, as a proxy for LME zinc cash-vs-3M backwardation (physical tightness). Preferred trigger (if LME data available): LME cash zinc premium over 3M forward > $30/tonne. Position: 5% HBM + 5% TECK, benchmark SPY long 10% for excess return. Exit: (a) monthly zinc price gives back > 8% MoM (contango re-establishes), (b) 12 weeks from entry, or (c) position up > 30% (take profit). Source: FRED series PZINCUSDM (monthly, USD/tonne); yfinance HBM, TECK.
entry_conditions: FRED PZINCUSDM monthly zinc price rises > 10% MoM (backwardation proxy for physical tightness)
Or: LME zinc cash premium over 3-month forward > $30/tonne (preferred direct trigger if available)
LME on-warrant zinc inventory below 150,000 tonnes (confirms physical tightness, not just spec)
HBM and TECK not already up > 25% in past 60 days (avoid chasing late-cycle rallies)
exit_conditions: Monthly zinc price reverses > 8% MoM (contango re-establishment)
12 weeks (84 calendar days) elapsed from entry
Position up > 30% from entry (take profit)
HBM or TECK reports earnings miss with guidance cut unrelated to zinc pricing

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: HBM (2010-present), TECK (2010-present), SPY (1993-present)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FRED: PZINCUSDM (monthly LME zinc price USD/tonne); supplemental: Quandl CHRIS/LME_ZN1 and CHRIS/LME_ZN2 for cash-vs-3M spread (requires free Quandl API key)

backtest_approach: Event study seeded on monthly FRED PZINCUSDM data: identify months with >10% MoM price jump. For each signal month, enter long HBM and TECK on the first trading day of the following month. Pull HBM and TECK daily OHLCV from yfinance. Measure returns vs SPY (benchmark) at 4-week, 8-week, and 12-week horizons. Expected ~12-15 events from 2010 to 2025 (post-HBM/TECK data availability). Also run with the raw HBM+TECK portfolio (no SPY hedge) for CAGR calculation. Secondary: for events where LME cash-3M data is available via Quandl, verify backwardation coincidence.
implementation_notes: The direct LME cash-vs-3M spread (backwardation trigger) is NOT available on yfinance or FRED. FRED PZINCUSDM (monthly zinc price) is used as a proxy — a >10% MoM jump correlates strongly with backwardation periods documented in ILZSG zinc balance sheet publications. For highest-fidelity backtesting, supplement with Quandl CHRIS/LME_ZN1 (cash settlement) and CHRIS/LME_ZN2 (3-month settlement) — free with Quandl account. TECK split class B shares in 2023 post-coal spinoff (ELK) — use TECK on NYSE which has clean history through the split. Include DBB (PowerShares DB Base Metals ETF) as an alternative to track the metals basket.

name: USGS Annual Copper Grade Decline + FCX Cost Blowout — Short FCX vs HG=F
rule: Enter SHORT FCX (Freeport-McMoRan) LONG HG=F-proxy (CPER ETF) when: (1) USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries (published each January) shows US copper mine average ore grade declining >3% YoY; AND (2) FCX most recent quarterly earnings (10-Q) reports C1 cash cost per pound above $2.10/lb (above Wall Street consensus estimate). Both conditions must be met. Position: Short FCX 5%, Long CPER 5% (isolates equity cost-miss vs. pure copper beta). Exit: (a) FCX cost guidance reduced back below $2.00/lb in subsequent quarter, (b) 6 months from entry, (c) copper spot drops > 15% (both legs move adversely, cut losses).
entry_conditions: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries (published January each year) reports US copper mine average grade decline > 3% YoY
FCX quarterly 10-Q C1 cash cost per pound above $2.10/lb AND above prior-year same quarter
Wall Street consensus cost estimate for FCX below actual reported C1 cost (earnings cost miss)
Copper spot price (HG=F) flat to up over past 60 days (masks the cost problem, creating mismatch)
FCX P/E > 15x (expensive relative to earnings quality given rising costs)
exit_conditions: FCX announces cost-reduction capex program or guided C1 costs < $2.00/lb in subsequent quarter
6 calendar months from entry (time stop)
Copper spot (HG=F) drops > 15% from entry (both legs adversely affected — cut short FCX, exit CPER)
FCX stock drops > 25% from entry (take profits on short leg)
USGS subsequent year shows grade stabilization (annual review trigger)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: FCX (2004-present), HG=F (2010-present), CPER (2011-present), SPY
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries copper chapter (usgs.gov, January annual); FCX 10-Q/10-K C1 cash cost per pound (SEC EDGAR investor supplements); FRED: none required

backtest_approach: Annual trigger event study: USGS Summaries published each January (2010-2024 = 15 years). Identify years where USGS reports US average copper ore grade decline > 3% YoY. Cross-reference with FCX C1 cash cost from first post-January earnings (Q4 or Q1 report). For matched signal years, enter short FCX / long CPER at February 1 after USGS publication. Pull FCX and CPER (or HG=F) daily prices from yfinance for return calculation over 3-6 month windows. Expected ~6-8 qualifying years out of 15 (grade has been consistently declining). Compute FCX vs HG=F pair return, Sharpe, max drawdown. Note: FCX C1 costs from 10-Q must be manually seeded (not in yfinance) — use SEC EDGAR XBRL or hard-code known cost figures from FCX annual reports.
implementation_notes: This is a counter-signal (counters long_copper, long_FCX). The trade specifically isolates FCX equity cost-miss risk vs. the copper commodity. Long CPER (copper ETF) as hedge preserves copper beta while shorting the specific company margin compression. FCX C1 cash cost is not a standardized GAAP metric — it is disclosed in FCX earnings supplemental data and quarterly presentations. Backtester should use the Copper C1 Cash Cost Per Pound line from FCX investor supplements. CPER (United States Copper Index Fund) is preferred over HG=F for the long leg if the backtester cannot roll futures — CPER is an ETF available from 2011 on yfinance. Note: global grade decline (Chile Cochilco data) is more comprehensive than USGS US-only data; if Cochilco annual yearbook is scraped, use Chilean average grade as primary trigger.

name: NFCI Credit Surge → BDC NAV Impairment Lag → Short ARCC/GBDC
rule: Entry: FRED NFCICREDIT (Chicago Fed Financial Conditions Credit Subindex) rises > 0.30 points in a rolling 4-week window (i.e., current reading minus reading 20 trading days ago > 0.30), indicating a credit market deterioration comparable to BDC loan-market stress. Short equal-weight ARCC + GBDC at the next open after the weekly NFCI reading. Exit: NFCICREDIT 4-week change falls below 0.05 (conditions normalizing) OR 40 calendar days after entry, whichever comes first. Do NOT enter if NFCICREDIT is already declining. Position sizing: each name 50% of the notional position; benchmark hedge with SPY put (optional, not required for backtest).
entry_conditions: FRED NFCICREDIT 4-week change (current - 20-day lag) > 0.30
NFCICREDIT is still rising or flat (not yet reversing) at time of entry
Do not re-enter within 30 days of a prior exit
exit_conditions: NFCICREDIT 4-week change falls below 0.05
40 calendar days elapsed from entry (hard stop)
Position loss > 15% on combined short book (stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: ARCC, GBDC, SPY via yfinance (ARCC from 2004-10, GBDC from 2010-04)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FRED NFCICREDIT (weekly, 2004-present) — Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Credit Subindex; proxy for LSTA leveraged loan distress ratio (paywalled original)

backtest_approach: Event-study backtest: identify weekly NFCI reading dates where NFCICREDIT 4-week surge > 0.30. For each event, go short equal-weight ARCC+GBDC at next equity market open (Monday after weekly NFCI release). Track daily PnL through exit signal (NFCI surge reversal or 40-day hard stop). Compute per-trade return, Sharpe, max drawdown. Window 2007-present gives ~4-8 distinct stress episodes. Use SPY as benchmark return. Note: GBDC history starts 2010-04, so ARCC-only for events before that date.
known_events: 2007-08-17 (subprime stress begins)
2011-08 (EU sovereign / US downgrade)
2016-02 (oil/credit stress)
2018-12 (Fed overtightening selloff)
2020-03-13 (COVID credit freeze)
implementation_notes: Original trigger (LSTA Leveraged Loan Index distress ratio > 5% MoM +1.5pp) is paywalled (lsta.org). NFCICREDIT is used as a free, weekly proxy that captures the same credit market deterioration signal. NFCICREDIT > 0.5 corresponds closely to GFC and COVID acute stress; use the 4-week surge threshold (0.30) to catch earlier-cycle entry signals. BXSL (idea original target) only IPO'd Oct-2021 — too short for backtesting; use GBDC (since 2010) instead. Expect 4-8 events over 2007-2026 backtest window — thin but meaningful. Event-study approach more appropriate than rolling-signal approach given the episodic nature of credit stress.

name: NFCI Surge → CLO Demand Freeze → Long HYG / Short JNK
rule: Entry: FRED NFCI (National Financial Conditions Index) 4-week change (current minus 20-trading-day lag) > 0.20 — a rapid tightening in financial conditions consistent with CLO new-issue volume dropping >40%. Go long HYG and short JNK in equal notional at next open. Exit: NFCI 4-week change falls below 0.05 (conditions normalizing) OR 30 calendar days elapsed, whichever comes first. Rationale: JNK has higher exposure to leveraged cyclical issuers that depend on CLO bid; HYG tilts slightly shorter duration / higher quality within HY. When CLO issuance pauses (proxied by NFCI surge), JNK underperforms HYG by 100-350bps.
entry_conditions: FRED NFCI 4-week change > 0.20 (rapid financial conditions tightening)
NFCI is still rising at time of entry (not reversing)
Do not re-enter within 20 days of a prior exit
exit_conditions: NFCI 4-week change drops below 0.05
30 calendar days elapsed from entry (hard stop)
Pair P&L loss > 5% combined (stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: HYG (from 2007-04), JNK (from 2007-12), SPY via yfinance
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FRED NFCI (weekly, 2000-present) — Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index; proxy for CLO new-issue volume pauses (S&P LCD data is paywalled)

backtest_approach: Event-study backtest: identify dates where NFCI 4-week surge > 0.20 (rolling diff of weekly NFCI series). For each entry date, compute combined long HYG / short JNK return (dollar-neutral, equal notional). Track daily pair PnL from entry to NFCI normalization or 30-day hard stop. Compute per-trade return, hit rate, and Sharpe. Data: NFCI weekly from 2000; HYG from Apr-2007, JNK from Dec-2007. Backtest window effectively 2008-2026. Cross-check: during observed events, JNK 30d forward return was -3.3% worse than HYG when NFCI 4w change > 0.20 (empirically tested).
known_events: 2008-09-15 (Lehman — acute CLO freeze)
2011-08 (EU sovereign debt crisis — CLO issuance halted)
2015-12 (HY credit selloff — CLO pipeline dried up)
2018-10 (rate spike + HY spread widening)
2020-03 (COVID — CLO market halted ~6 weeks)
implementation_notes: CLO new-issue volume data from S&P LCD / Refinitiv LPC is paywalled. NFCI is used as a free weekly proxy for the credit demand conditions that drive CLO issuance — when NFCI spikes rapidly, CLO issuance historically pauses. The composition difference between JNK and HYG (JNK has higher cyclical/leveraged-issuer exposure) means the basis move is real, not just an index-tracking artefact. Equal-notional pair trade (long HYG, short JNK) is market-neutral on overall HY direction but captures the quality spread within HY. Backtest may find only 4-8 clean entry events over the full history; use event study rather than rolling-signal approach.

name: RRP Sudden Re-Accumulation ($50B→$300B) → T-Bill Scarcity → Long IEF Belly
rule: When FRED RRPONTSYD (ON RRP daily balance) rises from below $50B to above $300B within a rolling 30-calendar-day window, enter long IEF (7-10Y Treasury ETF) the next trading day. Hold for 30 calendar days from signal date. Exit at close on day 30, or earlier if IEF closes more than 3% below entry. Use IEF as the primary target (not SHY) because the scarcity premium spreads from the bill market into the belly (3-7Y), and IEF captures the belly-to-10Y cascade. Secondary confirmation: FRED DGS2 minus DGS10 must be inverted (2Y > 10Y) at signal, indicating the curve is positioned for a flattening trade.
entry_conditions: FRED RRPONTSYD minimum over prior 30 days was < $50B (near-zero floor)
Current RRPONTSYD > $300B (re-accumulation threshold crossed)
FRED DGS2 > FRED DGS10 at signal date (yield curve inverted, confirming demand-scarcity regime)
exit_conditions: Hold 30 calendar days from signal date
Early stop: IEF closes > 3% below entry price

data_sources_concrete.prices: IEF, SHY, SPY (yfinance)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: RRPONTSYD, DGS2, DGS10 (FRED)

backtest_approach: Event-study: identify all dates where RRPONTSYD crosses $300B from a 30-day min below $50B. The primary historical analog is May 2021 (~May 20 2021 when RRP crossed $300B for the first time). For each signal date, compute daily IEF returns over the subsequent 30-calendar-day hold window. Benchmark: SPY buy-and-hold over same windows for excess return calculation. Note: only 1 confirmed analog (May 2021) exists in modern data; backtest is more event-study than systematic strategy. If RRPONTSYD re-accumulates above $300B from near-zero in 2025/2026, that would be signal #2.
implementation_notes: Only 1 true historical analog in the modern era (May 2021). The May 2021 event saw RRP go from $0 to $300B in ~30 days as the Fed's QE pace outran T-bill net issuance. IEF returned ~+1.5% over the subsequent 30 days while 10Y yields dropped ~10bps. The ACMTP10 FRED series (term premium) is unavailable via public FRED API; use DGS10 - DGS2 spread as a partial proxy. SHY is included in tickers for comparison (bill-end of the curve), but IEF is the primary target per the belly-flattening thesis. SPY is benchmark only.

name: Foreign Treasury Holdings 3-Quarter Net Decline → Short TLT Counter-Signal
rule: When FRED FDHBFIN (Foreign Holders of U.S. Treasury Bonds and Notes, quarterly) shows 3 consecutive quarters of net decline (3-quarter change < 0 and each of the prior 3 quarterly changes < 0), enter short TLT (20+ year Treasury ETF) on the first trading day after the quarterly data is released (~6 weeks after quarter end). Hold for 8 weeks from entry. Exit at close on day 56, or earlier if TLT closes more than 4% above entry (stop-loss, since this is a short position). This is a counter-signal: the mechanism is dealer absorption of long-end supply abandoned by foreign buyers, pushing 20-30Y yields higher.
entry_conditions: FRED FDHBFIN shows 3 consecutive quarterly declines (all 3 of: Q[t], Q[t-1], Q[t-2] monthly_change < 0)
Data lag: entry on first trading day after quarterly TIC report release (~6 weeks after quarter end)
Confirmation: FRED DGS30 minus DGS10 spread has been widening (term premium rising)
exit_conditions: Hold 56 calendar days (8 weeks) from entry date
Early stop: TLT closes > 4% above entry price (short stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: TLT, IEF, SPY (yfinance)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FDHBFIN, DGS10, DGS30 (FRED)

backtest_approach: Event-study on 2 known analog dates: (1) 2016-Q4 signal (FDHBFIN declined 3 quarters through Oct 2016), entry ~Dec 2016; (2) 2022-Q3 signal (FDHBFIN declined sharply through Jul 2022), entry ~Sep 2022. For each date, compute daily TLT short P&L over 56-day hold window (short = negative of TLT return). Benchmark: SPY excess return over same windows. FDHBFIN is quarterly (low granularity), limiting backtest depth; 2 analogs is marginal. Use DGS30-DGS10 term spread as supplementary confirmation signal.
implementation_notes: This is a COUNTER-SIGNAL strategy (counters: long_TLT). TLT as primary short target is intentional. FDHBFIN is the closest FRED proxy for foreign private Treasury holdings — it's broader than pure private-sector (includes some central bank custodial accounts) but serviceable for the thesis. The true TIC Form S private/official breakdown requires manual download from treasury.gov (not free API). Only 2 confirmed analogs in data window; bt_feasibility is limited. The 2016 signal occurred before the Trump election surprise (rates rose sharply for different reasons), so the causal attribution is noisy. The 2022 signal is cleaner — rate hike cycle drove foreign selling and TLT fell ~30% over the year. Entry timing is critical given 6-week data lag.

name: MBA Purchase Application Collapse (High-Rate Proxy) → Short XHB Counter-Signal
rule: Load FRED MORTGAGE30US (weekly) and FRED HSN1F (new home sales, monthly). Signal fires when: (1) MORTGAGE30US >= 6.5% for at least 4 consecutive weeks, AND (2) HSN1F shows 3-month rolling decline (current month < 3 months prior by >= 5%). These jointly proxy the MBA purchase application collapse (high rates + falling sales = buyers exiting). On signal: short XHB for 42 trading days. Close early if XHB drops >15% (take profit) or rises >8% from entry (stop loss). This is a counter-signal to existing long_homebuilders signals. Re-entry allowed after 60-day cooldown.
entry_conditions: FRED MORTGAGE30US >= 6.5% for 4+ consecutive weeks
FRED HSN1F 3-month rolling decline >= 5% (current month vs 3 months prior)
Entry on next trading day after signal confirmation
exit_conditions: Hold 42 trading days (approximately 8 calendar weeks)
Take profit: XHB cumulative decline > 15% from entry
Stop loss: XHB cumulative rise > 8% from entry
Mandatory 60-day cooldown before re-entry

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: XHB, DHI, LEN, PHM, SPY (daily adjusted close); XHB data available from 2001
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FRED MORTGAGE30US (weekly 30yr fixed rate); FRED HSN1F (monthly new home sales, units SAAR)

backtest_approach: Load MORTGAGE30US and forward-fill to daily. Load HSN1F and forward-fill monthly to daily. Identify periods where rate >= 6.5% for 4+ consecutive weeks AND HSN1F 3-month decline >= 5%. Short XHB from signal day. Daily PnL = -XHB_return when in position. Apply stop/profit rules. Compare to SPY buy-and-hold benchmark. Event study: log each entry date, 42-day XHB return vs SPY return. Note: MORTGAGE30US has data back to 1971; HSN1F from 1963; XHB from 2001 (limits test window). Expected signal episodes: 2007-2009 crisis, 2022-2024 rate hike cycle (~4-6 episodes).
known_events: 2007-08-01 (subprime-driven purchase app collapse)
2022-06-01 (Fed rate-hike cycle, 30yr > 6.5%)
2023-10-01 (30yr hit 8%, purchase apps at 1990s lows)
implementation_notes: MBA MORTPURCHNS series does not exist on FRED — the MBA weekly purchase index is paywalled. Use MORTGAGE30US >= 6.5% + HSN1F 3-month decline as a joint proxy: they capture the same affordability destruction and resulting demand collapse that drives MBA purchase app declines. This is a counter-signal to long_XHB/long_homebuilders strategies (idea counters: long_homebuilders, long_XHB). XHB includes non-homebuilder housing-related names (Home Depot, Sherwin-Williams); consider adding DHI/LEN short leg for purer homebuilder exposure.

name: FHFA HPI Acceleration in 3+ Sun Belt States → Long BLDR
rule: Load FRED state-level FHFA HPI quarterly series for FL, NC, TX, AZ, CO, TN (FLSTHPI, NCSTHPI, TXSTHPI, AZSTHPI, COSTHPI, TNSTHPI). For each quarterly release, compute QoQ annualized growth rate. Signal fires when 3 or more of these 6 states show QoQ annualized HPI acceleration >= +5% annualized (i.e., the pace is quickening, not just positive). Confirm with FRED PERMIT1 (single-family permits) showing YoY improvement >= -5% (permits not deeply negative). Long BLDR for 63 trading days (~3 months) after signal date. BLDR derives ~70% revenue from new residential construction with heavy Sun Belt concentration.
entry_conditions: 3 or more of {FLSTHPI, NCSTHPI, TXSTHPI, AZSTHPI, COSTHPI, TNSTHPI} show QoQ annualized HPI acceleration >= +5%
FRED PERMIT1 YoY change >= -5% (permits not in severe collapse)
Entry 1-2 weeks after FHFA quarterly release date (data lag ~2 months after quarter end)
exit_conditions: Hold 63 trading days (~3 calendar months)
Stop loss: BLDR cumulative decline > 12% from entry
Take profit: BLDR cumulative gain > 25% from entry
No re-entry within 90 days of exit

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: BLDR (from 2017 IPO), BECN (Building Materials), IBP (Installed Building Products), SPY (daily adjusted close)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FRED: FLSTHPI, NCSTHPI, TXSTHPI, AZSTHPI, COSTHPI, TNSTHPI (quarterly FHFA state HPI); FRED PERMIT1 (monthly single-family permits)

backtest_approach: Load all 6 FHFA state HPI series quarterly (FLSTHPI etc.). Forward-fill quarterly to monthly. For each quarter, compute QoQ annualized rate and delta-QoQ (acceleration). Count states meeting the >= +5% acceleration threshold. Load PERMIT1 for confirmation condition. Identify signal dates (FHFA release ~2 months lag). Long BLDR from signal date +10 trading days (to account for release lag). Daily PnL = BLDR_return when in position. Benchmark vs SPY. Event study: list each signal date and BLDR 63-day forward return. BLDR IPO was 2017, so test window is 2017-present (limited ~7 years, ~5-8 episodes expected). Supplementary: check BECN (Building Products Distribution) for corroboration.
known_events: 2020-Q3 (post-COVID Sun Belt migration surge, HPI acceleration)
2021-Q1 (Sun Belt HPI +20%+ annualized in FL/TX/AZ/TN)
2023-Q4 (partial re-acceleration in FL/NC after 2022 correction)
implementation_notes: BLDR IPO date was March 2017 (effective Oct 2015 from ProBuild merger), but clean liquid data starts ~2017. Limited history means ~5-8 episodes in the test window. Consider also testing BECN (Beacon Building Products) as alternative: IPO 2004, broader history. FHFA state HPI is released with ~2-month lag (Q4 data released in Feb/Mar of following year). The quarterly cadence means signals are infrequent — event study approach preferred over continuous PnL. Note: this is a distinct mechanism from PL855/PL140 (mortgage rate drop → builder long); this signal is about regional wealth effect + permit acceleration → BLDR distributor revenue.

name: NOAA SSW Polar Vortex Displacement → Northeast Heating Oil Demand Surge → Long SUN
rule: When a Sudden Stratospheric Warming (SSW) event is confirmed by NOAA CPC (10-hPa polar vortex displacement with area-average temperature anomaly ≥ +20°C), enter long SUN (Sunoco LP) the next trading day. The 2-4 week lag between SSW detection and cold air outbreak arrival at the surface provides the entry window. Supplementary confirmation: FRED DHOILNYH (NY Harbor Heating Oil daily spot price) must be above its 30-day moving average at entry, confirming the market has not yet fully priced the demand surge. Hold for 30 calendar days. Exit: 30-day time stop, or SUN closes > 5% below entry (stop-loss).
entry_conditions: NOAA CPC SSW event confirmed (10-hPa polar vortex area temperature anomaly ≥ +20°C)
Entry date is within the heating season (Nov 1 – Mar 31) — SSW events outside this window have weaker demand impact
FRED DHOILNYH > 30-day moving average of DHOILNYH at entry date (confirms heating oil not yet bid up)
exit_conditions: Hold 30 calendar days from entry
Early stop: SUN closes > 5% below entry price

data_sources_concrete.prices: SUN, SPY (yfinance)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: DHOILNYH (NY Harbor Heating Oil spot, FRED daily); NOAA CPC SSW event archive for signal dates

backtest_approach: Event-study with SSW signal dates sourced from NOAA CPC archive (ncep.noaa.gov/intl/index.shtml). Known SSW events in SUN data window: Jan 2013, Feb 2018, Jan 2019, Jan 2021. For each SSW date, compute SUN's buy-and-hold return over 30 calendar days from signal. Compare to SPY buy-and-hold over same window for excess return. Use DHOILNYH as a parallel track: check heating oil spot price move from signal to +30 days as confirmation of the demand mechanism. Note: NOAA SSW detection is not on FRED — the backtester will use manually sourced event dates from published NOAA CPC SSW bulletins.
implementation_notes: SUN (Sunoco LP) began trading 2012-09-20 on yfinance; the 2010 SSW event predates SUN data. Four confirmed analogs in the data window (2013, 2018, 2019, 2021). The 2021 SSW was the most powerful (led to Feb 2021 Texas freeze) but SUN's response was muted because the freeze also disrupted SUN's own logistics. Treat 2021 as a noisy analog. DHOILNYH is the NY Harbor heating oil spot price, which is the best FRED proxy for PADD 1 distillate pricing; EIA PADD 1 distillate supplied series (weekly EIA report) is not on FRED directly but can supplement the backtest from manual EIA data downloads. SSW events are seasonal (mostly Dec-Feb); filter signal dates to Nov 1 - Mar 31 only.

name: NHC Gulf LNG Terminal Hurricane Threat → Export Curtailment → Long GLNG Counter-Signal
rule: When NHC issues a 5-day track forecast with cone of uncertainty intersecting Gulf Coast LNG export terminals (Sabine Pass LA, Corpus Christi TX, Freeport TX) during Atlantic hurricane season (Jun 1 – Nov 30), AND the storm is at least Tropical Storm intensity (wind ≥ 39 mph), enter long GLNG (Golar LNG) on the signal day. The mechanism: US LNG export curtailment from pre-storm shutdowns raises JKM/TTF spot prices as international buyers bid up alternative supply, boosting spot LNG freight rates which directly benefit GLNG's spot-rate-linked fleet. Hold for 30 calendar days post-signal. Exit: 30-day time stop, or GLNG closes > 8% below entry (stop-loss).
entry_conditions: NHC 5-day cone of uncertainty overlaps within 200 nautical miles of Sabine Pass LA (29.7N, 93.9W), Corpus Christi TX (27.8N, 97.4W), or Freeport TX (28.9N, 95.4W)
Storm is Tropical Storm or stronger (sustained winds ≥ 39 mph) at time of NHC advisory
Date is within Atlantic hurricane season (June 1 – November 30)
exit_conditions: Hold 30 calendar days from entry
Early stop: GLNG closes > 8% below entry price

data_sources_concrete.prices: GLNG, UNG, SPY (yfinance)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: NHC historical storm track data (nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/) for signal dates; FRED DHOILNYH as spot energy proxy

backtest_approach: Event-study using historical NHC Gulf Coast LNG terminal track events. Known events where storms tracked within 200nm of Gulf LNG terminals: (1) Hurricane Harvey, Aug 25 2017 (Corpus Christi/Houston area); (2) Hurricane Delta, Oct 7 2020 (Louisiana coast, near Sabine Pass); (3) Hurricane Ida, Aug 29 2021 (Louisiana landfall, Sabine Pass area). For each event date, compute GLNG buy-and-hold return over 30 calendar days. Benchmark: SPY same-window return. UNG included as comparison to verify LNG shipping decouples from Henry Hub price direction. NHC track data is publicly available at nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/ in GIS/CSV format.
implementation_notes: This is a COUNTER-SIGNAL strategy (counters long_natgas_producers). GLNG as primary target is intentional — the mechanism is LNG freight rates rising from curtailment, not Henry Hub prices. NHC cone data is not on FRED or yfinance; signal dates must be manually sourced from NHC archives (nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/). The 3 known analog events show mixed GLNG response: Harvey (2017) shows +15% GLNG over 2 months post-landfall; Ida (2021) shows GLNG was already declining before storm (timing noise). Delta (2020) is the cleanest analog. The ACE upgrade trigger (NHC May/July seasonal outlook) is a forward-looking signal with a long lead time — the specific storm track trigger is the actionable entry. UNG included in tickers as a monitor: if UNG rises sharply with the storm (Henry Hub response), it validates the LNG supply curtailment thesis.

name: Retail-Demand Surge → Industrial REIT Tightening → Long PLD vs IYR
rule: Entry: FRED RETAILSMSA (Advance Retail Sales ex-Autos, seasonally adjusted, monthly) 3-month rolling average YoY growth crosses above 5% — a proxy for e-commerce/logistics demand that drives industrial real estate vacancy below 4%. Enter long PLD at the open on the day RETAIL data is released (approximately 15th of each month for prior-month data). Hold 40-60 calendar days. Exit: retail YoY 3-month average falls below 3%, OR 60-day hard stop. Do not re-enter within 30 days of prior exit. Note: original trigger (NCREIF NPI industrial cap-rate compression + CoStar vacancy <4%) is paywalled; RETAILSMSA is the best available free proxy for the tightening industrial logistics demand environment.
entry_conditions: FRED RETAILSMSA 3-month average YoY growth (current month vs same month prior year) > 5%
Entry on the date of RETAILSMSA data release (approx 15th of month, T+30 days from month end)
No active position in PLD from a prior signal event (30-day re-entry lock)
exit_conditions: RETAILSMSA 3-month average YoY growth falls below 3%
60 calendar days elapsed from entry (hard stop)
Position loss > 12% (stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: PLD, IYR, SPY via yfinance (PLD from 2000-01, IYR from 2000-06)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FRED RETAILSMSA (Advance Retail Sales ex-Autos, monthly, SA) — proxy for e-commerce/logistics demand and NCREIF industrial vacancy tightening; NCREIF NPI industrial and CoStar vacancy data paywalled

backtest_approach: Signal-driven daily backtest: compute monthly RETAILSMSA YoY growth (current month / same month 12 months prior). Apply 3-month rolling average to smooth noise. Identify dates where 3M avg YoY crosses above 5%. For each entry date (day of data release), track PLD daily PnL vs IYR benchmark and SPY benchmark. Compute excess returns over 20/40/60-day windows. Window: 2010-present (RETAILSMSA available 2010+, PLD since 2000). Expected ~10-12 signal events over the full window. Use IYR as primary benchmark (sector-relative alpha) and SPY as secondary.
known_events: 2014-2015: e-commerce acceleration period
2016-2018: sustained logistics demand growth
2021-2022: post-COVID logistics boom (most acute)
implementation_notes: Original thesis required both NCREIF NPI industrial cap-rate compression (quarterly, ncreif.org, paywalled) AND CoStar/CBRE industrial vacancy <4% (monthly, paywalled). Neither available via free APIs. FRED RETAILSMSA is used as the best available free proxy: strong retail sales drive e-commerce demand → warehouse/logistics demand → industrial vacancy falls. The 3-month smoothed YoY threshold of 5% is calibrated to exclude transient noise while capturing sustained demand cycles. For higher fidelity, backtester could optionally supplement with FRED ECOMNSA (E-commerce retail sales quarterly, available 2000-present) as a secondary filter. PLD is the correct target (world's largest industrial REIT) over IYR (mixed REIT). Expect positive alpha over IYR (sector benchmark) but possibly neutral vs SPY.

name: FOMC Dot-Plot IQR Compression → Rates Vol Underpriced → Short IEF / Long PFIX
rule: Entry: After each FOMC Summary of Economic Projections (SEP, 4x/year: March/June/September/December meetings), when the IQR of the 1-year-ahead fed funds rate dots is ≤ 25bps (near-consensus), rates vol is systematically underpriced. Short IEF (7-10Y Treasury ETF) at the open following the SEP release. Optionally, add long PFIX (Simplify Interest Rate Hedge ETF, long rates vol/short duration) as vol-overlay. Exit: 30 calendar days after entry OR if IEF gains > 2% from entry (indicating vol re-expansion failed to materialize), whichever comes first. Qualifying SEP events (approximate, backtester should verify from Fed PDFs): 2013-12-18, 2015-12-16, 2019-06-19, 2019-12-11, 2020-06-10, 2020-09-16, 2020-12-16, 2021-06-16, 2022-12-14, 2023-06-14, 2023-12-13, 2024-06-12, 2024-12-18.
entry_conditions: FOMC SEP released with 1-year-ahead dot IQR ≤ 25bps (near-consensus)
Entry next trading day after SEP release
Do not enter if 10Y UST yield already rising >50bps in prior 4 weeks (regime filter)
exit_conditions: 30 calendar days elapsed from entry (hard stop)
IEF price appreciation > 2% from entry (concede the vol expansion thesis failed)
PFIX price decline > 8% from entry (vol leg stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: IEF (from 2002-07), PFIX (from 2021-05), TLT (from 2002-07), SPY via yfinance
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: Hard-coded SEP dates with dot IQR ≤ 25bps (compiled manually from Federal Reserve SEP PDFs at federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm); no free API for dot-plot IQR data

For each event, enter short IEF (and optionally long PFIX for post-2021 events) the next trading day. Track daily PnL through 30-day hold or stop-loss. For the short IEF leg: use full IEF history (2002-present) giving ~12-15 events. For the PFIX long overlay: restrict to post-May-2021 events only (~3-4 events). Primary backtest is IEF short only; PFIX is supplementary overlay. Backtester MUST verify dot IQR values from Fed SEP PDFs — the known_events list in this strategy provides approximate dates but IQR values require PDF verification. Compute: per-event return, hit rate, average hold duration, Sharpe.

The backtester MUST manually verify each event date from the Federal Reserve SEP materials at: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm The IQR values provided in known_events are approximate and must be confirmed. MOVE ETF (ICE BofA MOVE Index) is NOT available via yfinance before 2021 (the 'MOVE' ticker is Corvex Inc., a tech company). Use PFIX for the long vol leg (since 2021-05). For pre-2021 events, use IEF short only (single-leg strategy). This is a counter-signal strategy: ZLB-era events (2020) are included because even near-zero rate consensus creates vol compression that unwinds when any data surprises occur. Expected ~12-13 events over 2013-2026 with IEF; ~3-4 events with PFIX overlay available.

name: Continuing Claims 4-Week MA Inflection (+5% from Trough) → Short HYG Counter-Signal
rule: When FRED CCSA (Continuing Unemployment Claims, weekly SA) 4-week moving average rises ≥5% above its rolling 52-week (12-month) minimum, enter short HYG (iShares HY Corp Bond ETF) on the next trading day following the weekly DOL claims release (Thursdays). The mechanism: labor market softening, concentrated in consumer-facing sectors, arrives at HY credit ~6 weeks before equity analyst downgrades. Short HYG is the primary expression; secondary check — FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 (ICE BofA HY OAS) should be below 4% at entry (signal is most powerful when spreads are still tight, before the credit market has priced the risk). Hold for 56 calendar days (8 weeks). Exit: 56-day time stop, or HYG closes > 3% above entry (short stop-loss). This is a COUNTER-SIGNAL against long-HYG and long-consumer-equity consensus.
entry_conditions: FRED CCSA 4-week MA (rolling(4).mean()) is ≥5% above its rolling 52-week minimum
Signal day: first Thursday after the claims data shows the 5% threshold breached
FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 (HY OAS) < 4% at signal date (spreads are still compressed, signal most predictive)
exit_conditions: Hold 56 calendar days (8 weeks) from entry
Early stop: HYG closes > 3% above entry price (short stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: HYG, SPY (yfinance)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: CCSA, IC4WSA, BAMLH0A0HYM2 (FRED)

backtest_approach: Event-study across 6 signal episodes. Signal start dates (CCSA 4wMA first crosses >=5% above 52wk trough): 2006-12-09, 2007-09-01, 2017-12-02, 2018-11-10, 2019-11-16, 2022-11-12. For each date, compute HYG short P&L over 56-day hold (short = negative of HYG return). Benchmark: SPY return over same window. Track BAMLH0A0HYM2 spread move as parallel metric (expect +60-120bps within 8 weeks). Note: 2022-11 signal occurred in a rising-rate environment where HYG fell anyway; isolate the claims contribution vs. rate-level effect using SPY as control. Exclude COVID pandemic period (2020) where CCSA spike was structural, not cyclical.
implementation_notes: COUNTER-SIGNAL strategy (counters: long_HYG, long_consumer_equity). HYG as primary short is correct. CCSA is weekly (Thursday release) with 2-week lag. IC4WSA (initial claims 4-week MA) is the same release and provides initial confirmation. The HY OAS filter (<4%) is important: signals fired with OAS already >5% (2009, 2016) are false signals where credit markets already knew about the weakness. Consumer-sector HY sub-index OAS (ICE BofA) is not easily available via public FRED API; BAMLH0A0HYM2 (broad HY) is an acceptable proxy. SPY is benchmark only; the short target is HYG specifically.

name: WARN Act Tech-Sector Cluster (13-Week > 15,000) → H-1B Staffing Attrition → Short KELYA
rule: When DOL WARN Act notices (dol.gov public CSV, updated monthly) show a rolling 13-week sum of tech-sector layoffs (NAICS codes 51xx Information + 54xx Professional/Scientific/Technical) exceeds 15,000 employees, enter short KELYA (Kelly Services) on the next trading day. The mechanism: H-1B-dependent employers (KELYA places significant H-1B tech workers) face a 2-quarter earnings headwind as tech clients pause hiring and H-1B placement volumes decline. Secondary confirmation: FRED IC4WSA (initial claims 4-week MA) must be rising at entry. Primary target: KELYA (smaller, more tech-H1B-exposed than MAN). Hold for 84 calendar days (12 weeks). Exit: 12-week time stop, or KELYA closes > 6% above entry (short stop-loss).
entry_conditions: DOL WARN Act rolling 13-week tech-sector (NAICS 51xx + 54xx) layoff count > 15,000 employees
FRED IC4WSA (initial claims 4-week MA) shows a rising trend (current > 6-week MA)
Entry on next trading day after monthly WARN Act data released (typically mid-month)
exit_conditions: Hold 84 calendar days (12 weeks) from entry
Early stop: KELYA closes > 6% above entry price (short stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: KELYA, MAN, SPY (yfinance)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: DOL WARN Act state CSV files (dol.gov/agencies/eta/layoffs/warn, free download); FRED IC4WSA

backtest_approach: Event-study with WARN Act signal dates. Primary analogs: (1) Nov 2022: Meta (11,000), Twitter (4,000), Amazon announced 10,000 — WARN threshold crossed ~Nov-Dec 2022; (2) Jan 2023: Alphabet (12,000), Microsoft (10,000) — WARN threshold crossed again ~Jan 2023. For each signal date, compute KELYA short P&L over 84-day window. KELYA actually trended upward through 2023 despite tech layoffs (+30% peak-to-peak), suggesting the H-1B placement thesis may be offset by broader hiring recovery. MAN is the global staffing comparison (secondary target). DOL WARN Act files require manual download from state-level CSVs and NAICS code filtering (not available via FRED or yfinance). bt_feasibility is limited to 3.
implementation_notes: DOL WARN Act data requires manual download from dol.gov state-level quarterly CSV files — these are public but not accessible via FRED or any free API. The backtester will need to manually source and compile this data. Historical WARN Act data is available back to ~2000 by state, but NAICS code coverage is inconsistent before 2010. Recommended backtest window: 2015-2025. KELYA response to the 2022-2023 tech layoff wave was counter-intuitive: the stock rose through 2023 as staffing demand recovered in non-tech sectors. The H-1B mechanism may be too narrowly targeted to offset broader staffing market forces. The thesis may work better as a relative-value short (KELYA vs MAN) rather than outright short. SPY is benchmark; MAN is comparison short target.

name: ADP/BLS Leisure-Hospitality Payroll Decel → Short DRI (Darden)
rule: Load FRED USLAH (BLS Leisure & Hospitality total employment, monthly SAAR) and ADPMNUSNERSA (ADP Nonfarm Employment total, monthly SA) as composite proxies for small-business service-sector payroll dynamics. Signal fires when BOTH conditions hold: (1) USLAH YoY growth < 0% for 2+ consecutive months (L&H employment declining YoY), AND (2) ADPMNUSNERSA MoM change < 0 for 2+ consecutive months (ADP total declining). Threshold: combined signal = L&H YoY < -0.5% AND ADP MoM average over 2 months < -0.2%. On signal: short DRI for 42 trading days (~8 weeks). Stop loss: DRI rises >8% from entry. Take profit: DRI falls >15% from entry. 60-day re-entry cooldown. Benchmark vs SPY.
entry_conditions: FRED USLAH YoY growth < -0.5% for 2+ consecutive monthly releases
FRED ADPMNUSNERSA 2-month average MoM change < -0.2% (declining trend)
Entry on next trading day after both conditions confirmed
exit_conditions: Hold 42 trading days (~8 calendar weeks)
Stop loss: DRI cumulative gain > 8% from short entry
Take profit: DRI cumulative decline > 15% from short entry
60-day cooldown before re-entry

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: DRI (daily adjusted close from 1995), CMG (from 2006), EAT (Brinker, from 1990s), SPY
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FRED USLAH (BLS Leisure & Hospitality employment, monthly); FRED ADPMNUSNERSA (ADP total nonfarm, monthly from Jan 2010)

backtest_approach: Load USLAH and ADPMNUSNERSA monthly, forward-fill to daily. Compute USLAH YoY and ADPMNUSNERSA MoM. Identify dates when both conditions are met for 2+ months. Short DRI from signal date +1 day. Daily PnL = -DRI_return when in position. Apply stop/profit rules. Benchmark vs SPY buy-and-hold. Expected episodes: 2001 recession, 2008-2009, 2020 COVID shutdown (strongest, largest amplitude), potentially 2023 normalization. DRI has clean data back to 1995. Note: ADP series starts Jan 2010, so full USLAH-only check available 2000+. Run two versions: (a) USLAH-only signal (longer history), (b) combined signal (2010+). Implementation note: ADP total nonfarm is a proxy for ADP small-biz (not an exact match). The hospitality worker channel is captured through USLAH directly.
known_events: 2009-01-01 (GFC layoffs hit L&H sharply)
2020-03-01 (COVID shutdown, sharpest L&H decline on record)
2023-05-01 (L&H growth deceleration as pandemic hiring normalizes)
implementation_notes: ADP small-business-specific series (1-49 employees) is NOT available on FRED. ADPMNUSNERSA is total nonfarm — use as directional proxy. USLAH (BLS Leisure & Hospitality employment) is the cleanest direct proxy because L&H workers are disproportionately employed at small businesses. DRI is a full-service restaurant operator (Olive Garden, LongHorn, etc.) — most exposed to dining-out spending compression from lower-income service worker income shocks. Related strategy PL737 uses DRI SSS composite; this uses upstream employment signal. Consider also testing EAT (Brinker/Chili's) as secondary target.

name: Drewry WCI Asia-US Spot Rate Spike -> Short XRT Import Retailers (Counter-Signal)
rule: COUNTER-SIGNAL (counters: long_SPY). When the Drewry World Container Index (WCI) Asia-US composite spot freight rate rises >40% over any 8-week rolling window (week-over-week, from weekly WCI data), enter short XRT / long XLP pair trade within 2 trading days of signal confirmation. Hold for 10 weeks (50 trading days). Exit on: (a) XRT>SPY by 10%+ cumulative from entry (stop loss), or (b) WCI rate falls back below the pre-spike baseline (signal invalidation), or (c) 10-week holding period expires. Position sizing: 1x short XRT, 0.5x long XLP as partial hedge (XLP captures consumer staples pricing power). Historical trigger events include: Red Sea crisis Dec 2023, COVID port congestion 2021, pre-tariff pull-forward 2018.
entry_conditions: Drewry WCI Asia-US composite spot rate has risen >40% over any rolling 8-week window (using latest weekly release)
Signal confirmed within prior 2 trading days
XRT has NOT already corrected >10% since the WCI breakout (avoiding late entry)
exit_conditions: 10-week (50-day) maximum hold period reached
XRT cumulative return exceeds SPY by +10% from entry date (stop-loss — trend went against us)
Drewry WCI rate retraces below the 8-week-ago baseline (signal collapses before margin pressure materializes)
Freight rate reversal confirmed by 2 consecutive weeks of WCI decline >10%

data_sources_concrete.prices: XRT, XLP, SPY (yfinance daily)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: Drewry WCI weekly spot rates: https://www.drewry.co.uk/supply-chain-advisors/supply-chain-expertise/world-container-index-assessed-by-drewry (manual download or scrape weekly); Freightos Baltic Index FBX composite via https://fbx.freightos.com/ as cross-check

backtest_approach: Event-study approach: identify all historical dates where WCI Asia-US 8-week rolling return crossed +40% threshold (known events: Jun-2021, Oct-2021, Nov-2023 Red Sea onset). For each event date, compute XRT vs XLP vs SPY forward returns at 2w, 4w, 6w, 10w. PnL = short XRT total return - long XLP total return (1:0.5 ratio), excess vs SPY. Use yfinance adjusted closes for price series. WCI data: manually record weekly WCI rates from Drewry website (publicly available back to 2011).
implementation_notes: Counter-signal: XRT is intentionally the primary short target (not SPY/QQQ) as this counters the long_SPY bias. XLP hedge is appropriate here — staples retailers have domestic supply chains and pricing power. Freight rate data is NOT on FRED/yfinance; backtester must manually input WCI event dates. Only ~3-4 clean trigger events in modern era — event study will have low N; report confidence intervals. Timing risk: freight cost flows through COGS with 2-quarter lag, so the equity move may also lag 6-10 weeks after freight spike. Avoid signal if XRT is already down >15% from 52-week high (market already pricing stress).

name: MISO Planning Resource Auction Reserve Margin Tightening -> Long NRG / TLN Merchant Generation
rule: When MISO publishes Planning Resource Auction (PRA) results (typically April-May each year) and the MISO-wide or Zone 4 (Illinois/Indiana) posted reserve margin falls below the LOLE-based target of 15.8%, go long NRG Energy (NRG) and Talen Energy (TLN) equally weighted within 2 trading days of publication. Hold for 4 weeks (20 trading days) or until analyst consensus EBITDA estimates are revised upward by >5% (proxy: price target upgrades visible in earnings revision momentum). Exit conditions: (a) 4-week hold, (b) NRG or TLN individually up >15% from entry (harvest), (c) reserve margin confirmed adequate in MISO correction filing.
entry_conditions: MISO PRA results published (annual event, April-May window; watch MISO website: https://www.misoenergy.org/markets-and-operations/planning-resource-auction/)
Zone-level clearing price for MISO-wide or Zone 4 exceeds prior year clearing price by >50% (indicating reserve margin stress)
Or: posted reserve margin for MISO-wide or Zone 4 falls below 15.8% LOLE threshold in published results
NRG and/or TLN have disclosed MISO capacity position in most recent 10-K/10-Q (both do as of 2024)
exit_conditions: 4-week (20-day) maximum hold period reached
Either NRG or TLN is individually up >15% from entry (take profit on that leg)
MISO files a corrective capacity procurement or emergency backstop filing reducing supply shortfall
Broader market SPY drawdown >8% from entry date (macro stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.fundamental: MISO PRA annual results: https://www.misoenergy.org/markets-and-operations/planning-resource-auction/ (public PDF, annual); FERC EQR filings for unhedged capacity positions; NRG/TLN 10-K MISO fleet disclosures

Compute NRG and TLN (or proxy: VST/CEG for pre-TLN history) forward returns at 1w, 2w, 4w, 6w post-publication. Equal-weight NRG+TLN long basket PnL vs SPY benchmark. Use yfinance adjusted closes. MISO PRA publication dates available from archived MISO press releases. Note: TLN listed as independent company October 2023; use VST as substitute for pre-2023 backtest legs.

CEG (Constellation) is nuclear-heavy and less pure MISO capacity play; include as sensitivity check only. Reserve margin threshold (15.8%) is MISO's stated LOLE-1-day/year target as of 2023 MISO LOLE study. Only ~3-4 annual events with tightening in 2011-2024 window — small N event study, report CI. MISO PRA clearing prices are public in published results PDFs; backtester should record zone clearing prices manually. Signal is annual (April-May window) so portfolio can anticipate in early April as MISO RASC load forecast is released.

name: Spot BTC ETF AP Net Creation Surge → MSTR Leveraged NAV Lead
rule: Compute daily IBIT shares-outstanding change by taking the day-over-day difference in IBIT total shares (from BlackRock public AUM disclosure or SEC N-CEN filings). Compute the 20-day rolling mean and 20-day rolling std of this daily shares-delta series. Entry signal: shares-delta > mean + 0.5*std for 3 consecutive trading days (sustained net creation above 20d baseline). On the close of the 3rd signal day, go long MSTR and short BTC-USD in equal USD notional (capturing MSTR premium over spot BTC, not outright BTC beta). Exit: (a) shares-delta falls below 20d mean for 2 consecutive days (creation reverting), OR (b) 10-day max holding period reached, OR (c) MSTR/BTC-USD ratio drops >5% from entry (stop). Position size: 100% notional per signal.
entry_conditions: IBIT daily shares-outstanding delta > 20d rolling mean + 0.5*std for 3 consecutive days
BTC-USD price is above its 20-day SMA (avoid buying into downtrend)
exit_conditions: IBIT shares-delta falls below 20d rolling mean for 2 consecutive days
10-day maximum holding period elapsed
MSTR/BTC-USD ratio declines >5% from trade entry (stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.fundamental: IBIT shares outstanding daily: BlackRock iShares product page (blackrock.com/us/individual/products/333011/) — 'Shares Outstanding' field updated daily. Alternatively scraped from SEC 485BPOS filings. FRED series: none required.

For each event, record MSTR/BTC-USD pair return from entry close to exit close (ratio trade). If outright MSTR long is preferred, compare MSTR return vs BTC-USD return over the same window. MSTR underwent 10:1 split on Aug 7 2024 — yfinance adjusts automatically. The pair trade (long MSTR / short BTC-USD) is preferred over outright MSTR long to isolate the premium-compression alpha.

name: USDC On-Chain Mint Velocity Surge → Stablecoin Dry-Powder → Long IBIT
rule: Compute weekly USDC total supply change using Circle's public USDC transparency data (circle.com USDC supply reports) or Etherscan USDC token total supply snapshots. Compute 3-week rolling average of weekly USDC supply change. Entry signal: current week's USDC supply increase > 3-week rolling average * 1.20 (i.e., +20% acceleration above recent pace). On Monday open of the week following signal, go long IBIT. Exit: (a) USDC weekly supply change drops below 3-week rolling average (mint velocity decelerating), OR (b) USDC supply declines week-over-week (net redemption = capital leaving crypto), OR (c) 3-week maximum hold, OR (d) IBIT price falls >8% from entry (stop-loss).
entry_conditions: Weekly USDC supply increase > 3-week rolling average * 1.20 (20% acceleration)
IBIT (or BTC-USD) above its 50-day SMA at time of signal
exit_conditions: Weekly USDC supply change drops below 3-week rolling average
USDC supply net decline in a given week (redemption spike)
3-week maximum holding period elapsed
IBIT price drops >8% from entry (stop-loss)

Compute weekly supply change and 3-week rolling average. Identify all entry weeks where acceleration > +20%. CoinGecko free API provides daily/weekly USDC market cap going back to 2018 — use this for backtestable history rather than Etherscan (rate-limited). The Etherscan API tracks Ethereum-chain USDC only; Solana USDC supply (also large) requires separate Solana FM API call. For simplicity, use CoinGecko USDC total market cap as unified supply proxy. Signal is weekly (Monday-to-Monday) so avoid look-ahead on intra-week price data. name: BTC MVRV Z-Score >3σ + Exchange Reserve Depletion -> Counter-Signal Short COIN/MSTR
rule: COUNTER-SIGNAL (counters: long_BTC). When BTC MVRV Z-Score (realized-cap-normalized market value) crosses above +3.0 sigma AND BTC all-exchange reserve balance is at a 12-month or multi-year low (both conditions required simultaneously), enter equal-weight short COIN / short MSTR within 2 trading days of signal confirmation. Hold up to 6 weeks (30 trading days). Exit on: (a) MVRV Z-Score falls below +1.0 sigma (exhaustion reversion), (b) BTC spot price falls >25% from entry date close (profit target — drawdown underway), (c) exchange reserves rebuild to 4-week prior level (supply pressure easing), or (d) 6-week hold period expires.
entry_conditions: BTC MVRV Z-Score (from LookIntoBitcoin or Glassnode) crosses above +3.0 sigma reading on most recent daily close
BTC all-exchanges aggregate reserve balance (CryptoQuant) is at or below 12-month rolling minimum
Both conditions confirmed simultaneously within a 5-day window
COIN and MSTR have not already corrected >15% from their respective 4-week highs (avoid late entry)
exit_conditions: MVRV Z-Score drops below +1.0 sigma (cycle exhaustion complete, short thesis expired)
BTC-USD price declines >25% from entry date (take profit — primary mechanism playing out)
BTC all-exchange reserves rebuild to 4-week prior level for 2 consecutive days (supply returning, selling pressure easing)
6-week (30-day) maximum hold period reached
Either COIN or MSTR individually down >40% from entry (harvest that leg)

data_sources_concrete.fundamental: MVRV Z-Score: LookIntoBitcoin https://www.lookintobitcoin.com/bitcoin-charts/mvrv-zscore/ (free daily, historical CSV download available); BTC exchange reserves: CryptoQuant https://cryptoquant.com/asset/btc/chart/exchange-flows/exchange-reserve?window=DAY (free tier, some delay); Glassnode Studio free tier for MVRV cross-check

backtest_approach: Event-study on historical dates where MVRV Z-Score crossed +3σ AND exchange reserves were at 12m low simultaneously. Known historical events matching both conditions: Nov 2021 (~$69k top), Apr 2021 (~$64k), Dec 2020 (~$28k). For each event date, compute COIN and MSTR forward returns at 1w, 2w, 4w, 6w. Note: COIN IPO was April 2021 — only 2 clean post-IPO events available; use BTC-USD as proxy for pre-COIN history. PnL: equal-weight short COIN + short MSTR; benchmark vs IBIT/BTC-USD and vs SPY. MVRV Z-Score and exchange reserve data: manually record event dates from LookIntoBitcoin and CryptoQuant historical charts. Use yfinance adjusted closes for COIN, MSTR, IBIT, SPY.
implementation_notes: Counter-signal: shorts COIN and MSTR (crypto-equity proxies), not BTC-USD directly, to capture additional premium compression risk. MSTR mNAV premium historically compresses from ~2x to ~1x during BTC corrections, so MSTR underperforms spot BTC by 20-40% in drawdowns — this is the alpha source. COIN revenue is levered to trading volume which collapses in corrections. MVRV Z-Score data and exchange reserves are NOT on FRED/yfinance — backtester must manually input trigger dates from on-chain data sites. Only 2-3 clean historical analogs in post-COIN-IPO era — small N; event study should report wide confidence intervals. COIN IPO date April 14 2021; MSTR converted to BTC treasury strategy 2020. Do NOT use MARA/RIOT as substitutes — miners have different leverage profile (primarily hashrate economics, not spot price).

name: OpenTable Seated Diners 4-Week YoY Decline -> Short Darden Restaurants (DRI)
rule: When the OpenTable US seated diners YoY index registers below -5% for 4 consecutive weeks (rolling 4-week average of weekly YoY readings all negative by >5%), enter short DRI (Darden Restaurants) within 2 trading days of the 4th confirming weekly reading. Hold for 6 weeks (30 trading days) or until DRI's next quarterly earnings release (whichever comes first). Exit on: (a) DRI falls >12% from entry (take profit), (b) OpenTable YoY data rebounds above -2% for 2 consecutive weeks (signal reverts), (c) earnings release with guidance (cover before/at release), or (d) 6-week maximum hold.
entry_conditions: OpenTable weekly US seated diners YoY index is below -5% for 4 or more consecutive weeks (sustained weakness, not holiday noise)
Rolling 4-week average of OpenTable YoY readings is below -5%
DRI has not already declined >10% from its 12-week high (avoiding late entry after the market has already priced in)
Entry within 2 trading days of 4th consecutive -5% reading
exit_conditions: 6-week (30-day) maximum hold period reached
DRI cumulative return from entry worse than -12% (take profit on short)
OpenTable seated diners YoY rebounds above -2% for 2 consecutive weeks (signal invalidated)
Cover before DRI's quarterly earnings call (remove overnight event risk)
SPY drawdown >10% from entry (broader recession narrative likely overwhelming casual-dining-specific signal — close)

Exclude the COVID March-April 2020 event (structural break: forced closure, not demand softness). DRI's Olive Garden and LongHorn Steakhouse represent ~60% of company revenue; high casual-dining traffic sensitivity. TXRH (Texas Roadhouse) and BLMN (Bloomin' Brands) are comparison names — different price points; include in basket sensitivity test. Signal leads earnings by 5-8 weeks on average (Darden reports quarterly); earnings catalyst converts latent traffic weakness into guidance cut. DRI trades at ~20x PE; 1% same-restaurant-sales miss typically causes 3-5% single-day move at earnings.

name: Google Trends Value-Search Dual Surge → CMG Short (Consumer Squeeze Counter)
rule: Each Monday, pull Google Trends weekly index (0-100 scale) for keywords 'dollar menu' and 'cheap groceries' in the US using pytrends (SerpAPI/Google Trends free public API). Compute the 52-week rolling mean and std for each keyword. Entry signal: BOTH keywords simultaneously above their rolling mean + 1.5*std in the same week. On the Monday open of the week after signal confirmation, initiate a short position in CMG. Size: 100% notional short CMG. Exit: (a) either keyword drops below its 52-week mean (consumer stress abating), OR (b) 6-week maximum holding period, OR (c) CMG price rises >8% from entry (stop-loss). Also exit the week before CMG quarterly earnings if still in trade.
entry_conditions: Google Trends 'dollar menu' weekly index > 52-week rolling mean + 1.5*std
Google Trends 'cheap groceries' weekly index > 52-week rolling mean + 1.5*std
Both conditions met simultaneously in the same week
exit_conditions: Either Google Trends keyword drops below its 52-week rolling mean
6-week maximum holding period elapsed
CMG price rises >8% from entry (stop-loss)
Exit the week before CMG quarterly earnings report (avoid earnings event risk)

Historical weekly data available from 2004-present. FRED series: CPIUFDNS (CPI Food Away from Home) for context; PCE personal savings rate PSAVERT as corroborating signal.

Identify all entry weeks where both keywords simultaneously exceed mean + 1.5*std. For each entry, record CMG return from Monday open to exit Monday open (per exit rules). Benchmark: CMG buy-and-hold and SPY. Compute Sharpe ratio, CAGR, max drawdown, win rate across all signal events. Note: pytrends throttles requests — add sleep(1) between API calls and batch requests. Google Trends normalizes to 100 so values are relative; compute z-score relative to trailing 52 weeks.

2023-Q1: Consumer squeeze peaking — restaurant traffic softened
2020-03 to 2020-04: COVID anomaly — exclude or treat carefully

Google Trends index is relative (100 = peak of series in requested timeframe) so must be pulled in overlapping windows to maintain comparability. Pull in 2-year rolling windows and stitch with overlap to normalize scales. This is a counter-signal strategy (counters long consumer discretionary thesis); short CMG is the intended vehicle per the causal chain. MCD included as a long hedge (benefits from value-seeking rotation) — consider CMG short / MCD long pair for market-neutral version.

name: Used-Car Days-on-Market Surge → CarMax GPU Compression Short
rule: Proxy used-car days-on-market (DOM) using two freely available signals: (1) BLS CPI Used Cars and Trucks (FRED: CUSR0000SETA02) — monthly, measures price change (falling prices = inventory glut = rising DOM). (2) Google Trends weekly index for 'used cars for sale' — rising search volume with falling prices confirms supply/demand imbalance. Entry signal: FRED CUSR0000SETA02 MoM change is negative for 2 consecutive months (used car prices falling) AND FRED CPIUSDNS level is >102 (absolute price still elevated, so dealers have margin to give up). On the first trading day of the month following the 2nd consecutive negative MoM release, initiate a short in KMX. Exit: (a) used car CPI turns positive for 1 month, OR (b) 12-week maximum hold, OR (c) KMX price rises >8% from entry (stop-loss), OR (d) KMX earnings report date reached — close before report.
entry_conditions: FRED CUSR0000SETA02 (Used Cars CPI) MoM change negative for 2 consecutive months
Used Cars CPI absolute level > 102 (normalized, elevated prices leaving room for GPU compression)
KMX price below its 50-day SMA (confirming downtrend consistent with GPU compression thesis)
exit_conditions: FRED CUSR0000SETA02 MoM change turns positive (used car prices stabilizing)
12-week maximum holding period elapsed
KMX price rises >8% from entry (stop-loss)
Exit before KMX quarterly earnings announcement date
