name: Cat-Bond Secondary Spread Spike -> Reinsurer Premium Hardening Long RNR/AXS
rule: When cat-bond secondary market spreads widen materially (>50bps in a 30-day window) without a corresponding major loss event triggering that spread — indicating risk-appetite withdrawal by ILS investors rather than loss realization — enter equal-weight long RNR (RenaissanceRe) and AXS (Axis Capital) within 3 trading days of the spread widening confirmation. The mechanism: ILS capacity withdrawal forces primary insurers to cede more risk to traditional reinsurers at harder prices, improving reinsurer combined ratios into the next Jan/Apr renewal cycle. Hold 8 weeks (40 trading days) or through next renewal cycle quarter-end, whichever comes first. Exit on: (a) 8-week hold, (b) either RNR or AXS up >15% from entry (take profit), (c) cat-bond spreads normalize (major ILS fund re-enters buying secondary), or (d) actual large catastrophe event occurs post-entry (ILS stress changes to realized-loss environment — close and reassess).
entry_conditions: Artemis.bm weekly cat-bond market report shows secondary spread widening >50bps over 30-day rolling window
Spread widening is NOT preceded by a qualifying catastrophe event (>$5B insured loss) in the prior 4 weeks — i.e., it is risk-appetite driven, not loss-driven
Entry within 3 trading days of confirmed spread-widening signal
RNR and AXS combined are not up >10% already from 8-week lows (avoiding late entry into a front-run)
exit_conditions: 8-week (40-day) maximum hold period reached
Either RNR or AXS individually up >15% from entry (harvest that leg)
Artemis weekly report shows cat-bond secondary spreads reverting to pre-widening levels
Major catastrophe event occurs post-entry with insured loss >$10B (loss environment changes thesis)
SPY down >8% from entry (macro stop-loss)

data_sources_concrete.prices: RNR, AXS, EG, RLI, SPY (yfinance daily)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: Artemis.bm weekly cat-bond market update reports: https://www.artemis.bm/news/ (free HTML, narrative spread commentary); Swiss Re ILS quarterly sigma reports for cross-validation; FRED: none required; insured loss database: PCS/Verisk (institutional) or Wikipedia for major cat events

backtest_approach: Event-study using known ILS market stress episodes where cat-bond secondary spreads widened materially without immediate major loss: Jan 2020 (COVID uncertainty onset for ILS), Q1 2017 (model update cycle), post-Ida 2021 (secondary spread widening beyond initial loss expectations), Q3 2022 (Hurricane Ian — note: this IS a loss event so exclude from 'pure ILS appetite' trigger, but post-Ian normalization lap is a second event). For each event date, compute RNR and AXS forward returns at 2w, 4w, 8w, 12w vs SPY. Use yfinance daily adjusted closes. Artemis event dates: manually identify from Artemis.bm news archive (free, searchable). Note: bt_feasibility rated 3 — event dates are identifiable but the spread series itself is not structured/downloadable; backtester must use qualitative Artemis narrative dates.
implementation_notes: Cat-bond secondary spread data is NOT a structured time series on any free platform; Artemis.bm publishes narrative weekly market updates but no downloadable spread CSV. The backtester must manually record event dates from Artemis archive where 'spread widening' is mentioned without concurrent major loss. RNR is the highest-quality pure-play traditional reinsurer; AXS has higher specialty insurance mix. EG (Everest Group) and RLI are optional basket additions for diversification. Jan 1 and Apr 1 renewal dates are the key 'pricing realization' catalysts; ILS withdrawal in prior quarter amplifies reinsurer pricing at renewals. Do NOT use RLI for small-N backtests — it has lower liquidity. Use RNR/AXS as primary.

name: BLS Medical Care CPI Surge -> Medicare Advantage MLR Breach Short HUM/ELV (Counter-Signal)
rule: COUNTER-SIGNAL (counters: long_SPY, long_quality). When FRED series CPIMEDSL (CPI Medical Care, SA) or CUSR0000SAM (NSA) shows MoM gains >0.4% for 2 consecutive months, AND the most recent MA insurer 10-Q discloses a medical loss ratio at or above 89% (for HUM) or 88% (for ELV), enter equal-weight short HUM / short ELV within 5 trading days of the second confirming CPI print. The mechanism: sustained medical cost inflation pushes MA MLRs above ACA-mandated 85% floor or internal target ranges, forcing EPS cuts at the next quarterly earnings. Hold until next quarterly earnings release (typically 4-8 weeks) and cover at/after earnings. Exit on: (a) earnings date (mandatory close), (b) HUM or ELV down >15% from entry (take profit), (c) CPI medical care reverses to <0.2% MoM for 2 months.
entry_conditions: FRED CPIMEDSL MoM change >0.4% for 2 consecutive monthly releases
Most recent HUM or ELV 10-Q shows reported MLR at or above 89% (HUM) / 88% (ELV) — check SEC EDGAR
HUM and ELV are not already >15% below their 52-week highs (avoid adding to an already-sold position)
Entry within 5 trading days of second consecutive >0.4% CPI medical care print
exit_conditions: Next quarterly earnings release date reached (HUM and ELV both report quarterly — exit before or at open on earnings day)
Either HUM or ELV down >15% from entry (take profit on that leg)
CPI medical care reverts: 2 consecutive months of MoM change <0.2% (signal invalidated)
CMS announces emergency MA rate corridor adjustment (removes thesis anchor)
SPY down >10% from entry (macro stop-loss — recession may actually improve MLR via utilization deferral)

data_sources_concrete.prices: HUM, ELV, CNC, MOH, SPY (yfinance daily)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: FRED series CPIMEDSL (CPI for All Urban Consumers: Medical Care, SA, monthly); cross-check with CUSR0000SAM (NSA); HUM and ELV 10-Q MLR disclosures from SEC EDGAR (quarterly); CMS MA enrollment and RADV audit results (cms.gov)

backtest_approach: Identify historical dates where CPIMEDSL printed >0.4% MoM for 2 consecutive months (FRED series, monthly frequency). Known trigger periods: 2022 Q1-Q2 medical care inflation surge, 2023 Q1 post-COVID utilization catch-up, 2024 Q1 pharmacy/site-of-care cost spike. For each trigger date, compute HUM and ELV forward returns at 2w, 4w, 6w vs SPY. Cross-validate with 10-Q MLR disclosures from SEC EDGAR for those quarters (HUM and ELV both report quarterly). PnL: equal-weight short HUM + short ELV, benchmark vs SPY. CNC (Centene) and MOH (Molina) can be included as Medicaid-heavy alternatives for sensitivity check. FRED CPIMEDSL is monthly — the strategy fires approximately monthly at CPI release (usually mid-month).
implementation_notes: CPIMEDSL is on FRED, monthly frequency — use via fredapi or FRED direct download. MLR disclosure is in 10-Q filings; HUM reports in 'Health care costs ratio' line; ELV in 'Benefit expense ratio'. Note: CMS ACA 85% MLR floor applies to fully-insured MA products — if MLR breaches 85% floor, insurer must issue premium rebates reducing future revenue. HUM has ~50% revenue from Medicare Advantage; ELV has ~35% from Medicare. Both are maximally exposed. CNC (Centene) and MOH (Molina) are more Medicaid-exposed and react to different signals (FMAP changes, redetermination cycles). The 2022 'medical utilization normalization' and 2024 'MA overpayment audit' periods provide the cleanest analogs. This is a counter-signal to quality/SPY: managed care stocks often track SPY positively; the short thesis specifically bets against that relationship breaking down.

name: Utility Sector Capex Excess + Equity Dilution Cycle → Short XLU Counter-Signal
rule: This is a counter-signal to long_XLU / long_utilities. Quantitative proxy: FRED TLNRESCONS YoY > +15% for 3+ months AND XLU trailing P/E > 1.1x SPY trailing P/E
Entry on next trading day after signal confirmation

exit_conditions: Hold 126 trading days (~6 calendar months)

Entry next trading day after official DOE press release

name: Reinsurer ROE Cycle Peak + P/B >1.5x → Counter Short RNR/AXS
rule: Entry requires ALL of the following conditions simultaneously: (1) RNR or AXS trailing 12-month ROE > 20% (computed from last 4 quarterly earnings: net income / avg book value per share * 4 quarters of data); (2) RNR or AXS price-to-book ratio > 1.5x (market cap / (shares * book value/share from most recent 10-Q)); (3) NOAA NCEI billion-dollar disaster count trailing 12 months < 10-year average (approximately 12-16 events/year; use count from ncei.noaa.gov free CSV); (4) Neither RNR nor AXS has reported a major nat-cat loss quarter in the last 2 qtrs. On the first trading day after the quarterly earnings release that confirms ROE > 20% with P/B > 1.5x, short the qualifying name(s) (RNR, AXS, or both). Exit: (a) P/B ratio falls below 1.1x (mean-reversion achieved), OR (b) ROE falls below 15% (soft market materializing faster), OR (c) 26-week maximum holding period, OR (d) Major cat event occurs (hurricane/earthquake causing >$5B insured loss) — cover immediately as reinsurers may rally on hard market repricing.
entry_conditions: Trailing 12-month ROE > 20% for RNR or AXS (from quarterly earnings data)
Price-to-book ratio > 1.5x at time of signal
NOAA trailing 12-month billion-dollar disaster count < 10-year annual average (~14)
No major cat loss quarter reported in prior 2 quarters
exit_conditions: Price-to-book falls below 1.1x (mean-reversion complete)
Trailing ROE falls below 15% (business deteriorating faster than expected)
26-week maximum holding period elapsed
Major catastrophe event occurs (>$5B insured loss) — short cover immediately

data_sources_concrete.prices: RNR, AXS, SPY via yfinance. Book value per share from yfinance .info['bookValue'] or quarterly financials.
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: RNR/AXS quarterly earnings: yfinance Ticker.quarterly_financials and Ticker.quarterly_balance_sheet for net income and book value. NOAA NCEI billion-dollar disaster events: free CSV download at https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/billions/events.csv (updated monthly). Alternatively, FRED series: none directly covers cat disasters; use NOAA CSV as the primary data source for disaster count. P/B ratio: compute as (RNR_price * shares_outstanding) / book_value using yfinance .info fields.

backtest_approach: Quarterly-triggered event study from 2003-present (AXS IPO Jul 2003; RNR from 1995). For each quarter-end, compute trailing 12M ROE and P/B ratio for RNR and AXS using yfinance quarterly financials. Identify all quarters where ROE > 20% and P/B > 1.5x. Cross-reference NOAA billion-dollar disaster count for trailing 12M. For each qualifying entry date (earnings release day), measure forward returns over 8, 13, and 26 weeks. Compare to SPY over same periods. Primary metric: average excess return of short RNR/AXS vs SPY over 13-week window. Secondary: max drawdown on the short side (key risk: cat event causes hard market rally while short is on).
known_events: 2006-2007: Post-Katrina hard market with high ROE; cycle softened by 2007-2008
2018: Post-Harvey/Irma/Maria hard market — ROE spiked before 2019 softening
2022-2023: Inflation-driven hard market; RNR/AXS ROE elevated above 20%
2024: RNR P/B approached 1.4-1.5x as pricing remained firm
implementation_notes: yfinance quarterly financials may have gaps or lags; supplement with SEC EDGAR if needed. NOAA NCEI CSV is updated monthly and provides events going back to 1980. The 10-year average of ~12-16 events/year as of 2024 should be computed dynamically from trailing 10 years of NOAA data, not hardcoded. This is a counter-signal strategy (counters long SPY/quality thesis); shorts specific reinsurer names, not a broad index. RNR and AXS are Bermuda-based; they tend to move together in the reinsurance cycle. Consider equal-weighted short of both names for diversification. Key risk: a major cat event while short can cause 20-40% gap-ups — hard stop required.

name: BCB Selic Hike Inflection → BRL Carry Rebound → Long EWZ
rule: Monitor BCB COPOM decisions (8 meetings/year, roughly every 6 weeks). Entry signal: The BCB raises the Selic rate for the 2nd consecutive meeting, coming off a prior easing cycle (i.e., at least 2 prior consecutive cuts before the inflection). This defines a confirmed hiking pivot. On the next trading day after the 2nd consecutive COPOM hike confirmation, go long EWZ. Exit: (a) BCB cuts Selic at any subsequent meeting (pivot back to easing), OR (b) 8-week maximum holding period, OR (c) EWZ price falls >10% from entry (stop-loss), OR (d) BRL weakens >5% vs USD from entry level (USD/BRL rises >5% from entry). Position sizing: 100% notional long EWZ.
entry_conditions: BCB COPOM raises Selic for the 2nd consecutive meeting
Prior easing cycle: at least 2 consecutive cuts preceded this hiking sequence
BRL/USD not in extreme stress (USD/BRL not >10% above 52-week high at entry)
exit_conditions: BCB cuts Selic at any subsequent COPOM meeting
8-week maximum holding period elapsed
EWZ price falls >10% from entry (stop-loss)
USD/BRL rises >5% from entry level (BRL weakens vs USD)

data_sources_concrete.prices: EWZ, BRL=X (USD/BRL spot), SPY via yfinance
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: BCB COPOM historical decisions: BCB public API: https://api.bcb.gov.br/dados/serie/bcdata.sgs.432/dados?formato=json (series 432 = Selic target rate, daily, free, no API key required, available from 1986). Alternatively FRED series IRSTCB01BRM156N (Brazil Lending Rate) or INTDSRBR193N (Brazil Discount Rate) — check availability via fredapi. COPOM meeting calendar and minutes: https://www.bcb.gov.br/en/monetary-policy/copom (historical decisions available as PDF/HTML going back to 1996). Exact Selic target rate by meeting date available from BCB SGS series 432.

backtest_approach: Event-study backtest from 2000-present (EWZ data available from Jul 2000). Pull BCB Selic rate daily from BCB SGS API (series 432). Identify all COPOM meetings by detecting discrete step-changes in the daily rate. Find all confirmed 2nd-consecutive-hike events following a prior easing cycle. Record EWZ return from entry (day after 2nd hike) to exit per exit rules. Also compute BRL=X return over same windows to decompose equity vs FX contribution. Benchmark: SPY over same windows. Key historical events to validate: 2003 Lula inauguration hike cycle, 2010-2011 post-GFC recovery hiking, 2021-2022 Selic hiking cycle from 2% to 13.75%, 2024-2025 hiking cycle from 10.5% to 14.75%.
known_events: 2009-04: First BCB hike after GFC cuts — EWZ rallied ~30% in 8 weeks
2010-04: Second post-GFC hiking cycle start — BRL strengthened, EWZ up ~15%
2021-03: Selic hike inflection from 2% (historic low) — EWZ lagged due to COVID
2024-09: BCB resumed hikes from 10.5% amid inflation concerns
implementation_notes: BCB SGS API series 432 provides daily Selic target rate — step-changes identify exact COPOM meeting decision dates. This is more reliable than FRED for Brazil. EWZ returned ~7% dividend yield historically; total return matters. BRL=X tracks USD/BRL spot, not the carry — the strategy captures both FX and equity appreciation from the hiking pivot. Brazil political risk (elections, fiscal crises) can overwhelm the rate signal; consider adding a political risk filter (e.g., CDS spread < prior 12M average). 2003 and 2016 Brazilian political crises caused EWZ dislocations uncorrelated with rate cycles — treat as special cases. This is a counter-signal strategy (counters short EM / long USD); EWZ is the specific vehicle rather than a broad EM basket.

name: NASA/GAO Artemis Schedule Slip Report with Nuclear Propulsion Citation → Long BWXT DRACO Contract Pull-Forward

name: DOT BTS Form 41 RASM-CASM Divergence → Short Margin-Laggard Airline vs Long DAL
rule: After each quarterly DOT BTS Form 41 Schedule P-12 data release (~75 days post quarter-end), compute trailing-2-quarter RASM growth minus CASM growth for AAL, JBLU, DAL, LUV, UAL. If AAL or JBLU shows RASM-CASM spread ≤ -300bps for 2 consecutive quarters while DAL shows RASM-CASM spread ≥ 0bps (positive), enter a dollar-neutral pair: SHORT $1 of the laggard (AAL or JBLU), LONG $1 of DAL. Hold 30-45 trading days or until BTS data for the next quarter is released and spread normalizes (RASM-CASM spread returns to > -100bps for the laggard). If both AAL and JBLU trigger simultaneously, short the one with the larger negative spread.
entry_conditions: DOT BTS Form 41 Schedule P-12 quarterly data published for quarter Q
AAL or JBLU trailing-2-quarter average (RASM growth - CASM growth) ≤ -300bps
DAL trailing-2-quarter average (RASM growth - CASM growth) ≥ 0bps (positive spread)
Trigger occurs at BTS data release date, not the underlying quarter-end date (use ~75-day lag for signal date)
exit_conditions: Next quarterly BTS Form 41 data released and laggard carrier RASM-CASM spread improves above -100bps
Laggard carrier files negative earnings pre-announcement (8-K) — close immediately (alpha already captured)
45 trading days from entry (time stop)

Flag quarters where AAL or JBLU spread ≤ -300bps and DAL ≥ 0bps. Go short laggard / long DAL on BTS release date at closing prices. Close at next BTS release or 45-day stop. name: BanRep Rate Cut + WTI ≥ $65/bbl → Colombia Carry Convergence → Long GXG
rule: Go LONG GXG (iShares MSCI Colombia ETF) within 2 trading days of a Banco de la República (BanRep) Monetary Policy Board rate cut announcement, conditional on WTI crude spot price ≥ $65/bbl (Colombia fiscal break-even) at the time of the announcement. Hold for 8 weeks from entry date. Exit if: (a) WTI falls below $60/bbl (oil support leg breaks), (b) BanRep signals a pause or hike at subsequent meeting, (c) USD/COP (COP=X) rises more than 8% from entry (COP stress), or (d) 8-week maximum holding period.
entry_conditions: BanRep Monetary Policy Board announces rate cut of ≥25bps (banrep.gov.co press release)
WTI crude spot price (FRED DCOILWTICO) ≥ $65/bbl on cut announcement date
GXG has not already run >10% in the prior 3 weeks (no chasing an extended move)
USD/COP spot (COP=X) not in extreme stress — USD/COP not more than 8% above its 52-week moving average
exit_conditions: WTI crude spot drops below $60/bbl (Colombia fiscal backstop deteriorates)
BanRep signals rate pause or hike reversal at subsequent Monetary Policy Board meeting
USD/COP rises >8% from entry price (COP stress threshold)
8-week maximum holding period from entry date (time stop)
GXG falls >12% from entry (stop-loss)

name: MNB Rate Cut While ECB Holds → EURHUF Depreciation → Short OTP Bank (OTP.F) vs Long EPOL Pair
rule: Counter-signal: When Hungary's Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) cuts its base rate AND the ECB in the same 6-week window either holds or raises rates (ECB Governing Council decision), creating a EUR-HUF rate differential that widens in EUR's favor by ≥75bps, enter: SHORT OTP.F (OTP Bank Frankfurt listing) / LONG EPOL (Poland ETF as CEE benchmark) dollar-neutral pair. Entry at next-day open following MNB cut confirmation. Hold 25-35 trading days. Exit when: (a) MNB signals a pause at subsequent meeting, (b) EURHUF=X falls (HUF strengthens) more than 3% from entry (carry unwind), or (c) 35-day time stop. Note: The idea title referenced 'EWH' but EWH is Hong Kong — there is no single US-listed Hungary ETF. OTP Bank (OTP.F) is the correct primary vehicle as it represents ~35-40% of Hungarian market cap.

ECB Governing Council in the same 6-week window holds or raises the deposit facility rate (FRED ECBDFR or ecb.europa.eu press release)
EUR-HUF rate differential (ECB rate minus MNB rate post-cut) widens by ≥75bps on this decision
EURHUF=X spot is not already >5% above its 52-week moving average (avoid late entry into extreme HUF weakness)
exit_conditions: MNB signals rate pause or rate hike at next Monetary Council meeting
EURHUF=X falls >3% from entry (HUF unexpectedly strengthens — carry unwind risk, exit immediately)
35 trading days from entry (time stop)
OTP.F falls >12% in isolation (not pair-driven, idiosyncratic OTP risk — reduce exposure)

name: USDA Dec 1 Potato Stocks Glut -> Lamb Weston (LW) Frozen-Fry Margin Squeeze
rule: Each December, take the USDA NASS Potato Stocks report (Dec 1 reference date, released mid-December). Compute YoY % change in US national Dec 1 potato stocks. If YoY > +4% (glut), SHORT LW; if YoY < -4% (short crop), LONG LW; otherwise flat. Enter at the close of the first trading day on/after Dec 21 (conservative lag past the release). Hold 126 trading days (~2 quarters / through LW's Jan and Apr earnings), then exit at close. One signal per year; unit notional, optionally scaled by min(2, |YoY%|/4).
entry_conditions: USDA NASS Dec 1 national potato stocks YoY change > +4% -> enter SHORT LW at close of first trading day on/after Dec 21
USDA NASS Dec 1 national potato stocks YoY change < -4% -> enter LONG LW at close of first trading day on/after Dec 21
|YoY change| <= 4% -> no position that year
exit_conditions: Exit at close 126 trading days after entry (time stop, ~2 quarters)
No intermediate stop; one round-trip per year (next Dec signal cannot overlap since hold ends by late June)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: LW (primary, history from 2016-11-10), SPY (benchmark/hedge)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: USDA NASS Quick Stats API (free key, instant signup at quickstats.nass.usda.gov/api): source_desc=SURVEY, sector_desc=CROPS, commodity_desc=POTATOES, statisticcat_desc=STOCKS, agg_level_desc=NATIONAL, reference_period_desc=FIRST OF DEC, unit_desc=CWT. Fallback/confirmation (no key needed): FRED WPU011306 (PPI Farm Products: Potatoes, monthly, 2011-present) — December YoY < -10% is a glut proxy (price collapse => short LW), December YoY > +15% is a short-crop proxy (long LW).

backtest_approach: Annual event study, ~9-10 events (Dec 2016 through Dec 2025; LW IPO 2016-11-10 so every December is usable — NASS provides full prior-year stocks history for the YoY base). For each December: compute signal from Dec 1 stocks YoY, enter signed LW position at close of first trading day on/after Dec 21, hold 126 trading days, compute raw PnL and SPY-beta-hedged excess return (beta from trailing 252d OLS). Aggregate into a daily PnL series across years for Sharpe/CAGR; also report per-event hit rate and mean excess return. Sanity anchors: Dec 2021 (heat-dome short crop => long, LW rallied through 2022-23) and Dec 2023 (record crop => short, preceded LW's FY2024-25 guidance cuts and share collapse).

2023-12 record 2023 crop / elevated stocks (expect SHORT signal; LW collapsed in 2024)
2024-12 continued oversupply, LW FQ2-2025 guidance cut Dec 2024 citing raw potato oversupply
implementation_notes: NASS Quick Stats API key is free and instant but required (anonymous probe returns 'unauthorized'); if the backtester has no key, use the documented FRED WPU011306 fallback thresholds — verified live (monthly, current through May 2026; note May 2026 print of 67.6 vs ~83 in early 2026 implies an ongoing potato price collapse). Do NOT use the Dec 1 reference date as the trade date — the report is released mid-December (typically Dec 17-19); the Dec 21 entry rule avoids lookahead. Only ~9-10 events, so report per-event stats alongside aggregate Sharpe; do not over-tune the 4% threshold (check 2%/6% for robustness, not optimization). LW is the dominant pure-play NA fry processor (McCain and Simplot are private), so no basket dilution needed — single name is the correct target per the causal chain.

name: IRS Daily Treasury Statement Refund Pace YoY -> Dollar Store Q1 Comps (DG/DLTR/FIVE)
rule: Each year, sum daily individual income-tax refund disbursements from the Daily Treasury Statement (income_tax_refunds_issued table, all rows whose tax_refund_type contains 'Individual') from Feb 1 through the last business day of February, and compute the YoY gap vs the same Feb 1-28/29 window of the prior year. If cumulative refunds are running >= +5% ahead of prior year, go LONG an equal-weight basket of DG/DLTR/FIVE (whichever are listed that year) at the open of the first trading day of March; if running <= -5% behind, go SHORT the basket; otherwise stay flat. Hold the position, beta-hedged with SPY (hedge ratio = trailing 252d basket beta), until the close of the last trading day of May (captures Q1 earnings reactions in late May).
entry_conditions: Compute CUM_t = sum of DTS 'tax_refund_today_amt' for all tax_refund_type rows containing 'Individual' (case-insensitive), Feb 1 through last business day of February of year t
GAP_t = CUM_t / CUM_{t-1} - 1
GAP_t >= +0.05 -> enter LONG equal-weight DG/DLTR/FIVE at open of first trading day of March
GAP_t <= -0.05 -> enter SHORT equal-weight DG/DLTR/FIVE at open of first trading day of March
-0.05 < GAP_t < +0.05 -> no position that year
Beta-hedge with SPY: opposite SPY position sized at trailing 252-day basket beta
exit_conditions: Close all legs at the close of the last trading day of May of year t
No intra-period stop; this is an annual seasonal event trade

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: DG (from 2009-11), DLTR (full), FIVE (from 2012-07), OLLI (optional, from 2015-07), SPY
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: Treasury Fiscal Data API v1/accounting/dts/income_tax_refunds_issued (daily since 2005-10-03, amounts in $MM); no FRED series needed

backtest_approach: Annual event study, one observation per year 2007-2026 (first YoY comparison needs Feb 2006 vs Feb 2007). For each year compute the Feb cumulative individual-refund YoY gap, take the signed basket-vs-SPY position Mar 1 -> May 31, and record beta-hedged excess return. Basket membership is point-in-time: DLTR only pre-2010, DG added 2010 (allow ~3 months post-IPO seasoning so DG enters 2010), FIVE added 2013. Daily PnL within each Mar-May window; aggregate to per-year event returns plus a stitched daily equity curve (flat outside windows). Compare hit rate and mean event return vs unconditional Mar-May basket drift.

2019: post-TCJA withholding-table confusion depressed early-season average refunds

implementation_notes: DTS category labels change across vintages: early years use 'Individual'/'Individual (EFT)', later 'IRS Tax Refunds Individual (EFT)', current vintage 'Taxes - IRS Tax Refunds Individual (EFT)' and '(Checks)'. Match with case-insensitive substring 'individual' on tax_refund_type and sum ALL matching rows (checks + EFT) to stay consistent across regimes. Use tax_refund_today_amt (daily flow, $ millions), NOT mtd/fytd columns. API verified live: https://api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov/services/api/fiscal_service/v1/accounting/dts/income_tax_refunds_issued?filter=record_date:gte:YYYY-02-01,record_date:lte:YYYY-02-28&page[size]=900 (18,776 total rows as of 2026-06). Compare identical calendar windows (Feb 1-28; include Feb 29 in leap years or truncate both years at day 28 for symmetry - truncating at 28 is cleaner). Signal is fully known by Feb 28 so the Mar 1 open entry has no lookahead. The +/-5pct threshold is on cumulative dollars, robust to single-day EFT batch timing. 2020 Mar-May window overlaps the COVID crash; report results with and without 2020. SPY is benchmark/hedge only - primary targets are the specific dollar-store names per causal chain.

name: CFTC TFF Bitcoin Asset-Manager Net-Long Extreme -> Short BTC/IBIT (counter long_BTC)
rule: Each Tuesday-dated CFTC Traders in Financial Futures report (released Friday ~3:30pm ET) for CME Bitcoin futures (contract code 133741), compute institutional net-long share NL = (Asset_Mgr_Positions_Long_All - Asset_Mgr_Positions_Short_All + Lev_Money_Positions_Long_All - Lev_Money_Positions_Short_All) / Open_Interest_All. Compute the percentile rank of NL within a trailing 104-week window (expanding, minimum 52 observations). When the percentile rank exceeds 0.90, go SHORT BTC at the next Monday open (BTC-USD spot as backtest proxy; IBIT for live trading post-2024). Hold until NL percentile falls below 0.50 or 6 weeks elapse, whichever comes first; then return to flat.
entry_conditions: Weekly TFF futures-only report for CFTC contract code 133741 (BITCOIN - CHICAGO MERCANTILE EXCHANGE)
NL = (AssetMgr_Long - AssetMgr_Short + LevMoney_Long - LevMoney_Short) / Open_Interest_All
Percentile rank of NL over trailing 104 weekly reports (expanding window, min 52) > 0.90
Enter SHORT BTC-USD at the open of the first Monday following the Friday report release (3-business-day publication lag respected: Tuesday data -> Friday release -> Monday execution)
exit_conditions: NL percentile rank drops below 0.50 (positioning normalized) -> cover at next Monday open
OR 6 weeks (30 trading days) elapsed since entry -> cover
Flat otherwise; no leverage, single unit short

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: BTC-USD (daily, from 2014; trades 7d/week - align to report calendar), IBIT (from 2024-01-11, live-trading vehicle), SPY (benchmark)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: CFTC TFF futures-only yearly archives https://www.cftc.gov/files/dea/history/fut_fin_txt_YYYY.zip (file FinFutYY.txt inside), 2018-2026; columns Asset_Mgr_Positions_Long_All/Short_All, Lev_Money_Positions_Long_All/Short_All, Open_Interest_All, Report_Date_as_YYYY-MM-DD; filter CFTC_Contract_Market_Code == 133741. No FRED series.

backtest_approach: Weekly-rebalanced daily-PnL backtest. Build the weekly NL series from TFF reports Dec 2017-present (~440 weekly obs); with 52-week burn-in, tradable signal starts ~Dec 2018. Position state machine: flat -> short on entry trigger, short -> flat on exit trigger; daily short BTC-USD returns while active (use close-to-close on calendar days, or restrict to weekdays to match equity comparison - document choice). Report total/annualized return, Sharpe, max drawdown, exposure fraction, and per-episode table. Also report the counter-signal overlay variant: long BTC baseline that goes to CASH (not short) when signal is active, vs buy-and-hold BTC - this matches the counters:long_BTC intent.
known_events: 2021-04 (Q1 2021 local top ~64k then -50%)
2021-11 (all-time-high ~69k then 2022 bear)
2024-03 (post-ETF-launch ~73k local top, crowded basis trade)
implementation_notes: Use FUTURES-ONLY TFF files (fut_fin_txt_YYYY.zip), not futures+options, for the full Dec-2017 history. CME Micro Bitcoin (separate contract code) must NOT be summed in - use 133741 only; contract unit 5 BTC but NL is a ratio so units cancel. Combining AssetMgr+LevMoney net-long captures both the institutional bid and the crowded leveraged long; an AssetMgr-only variant is a reasonable robustness check (LevMoney is typically the basis-trade short leg, so the combined measure partly nets carry crowding - report both if cheap). Some 2017-2018 weeks may have thin OI - guard against div-by-zero. BTC-USD trades weekends: enter/exit at Monday 00:00 UTC bar open from yfinance daily data. IBIT history too short to backtest (2024-01 start) - backtest on BTC-USD, note IBIT as the live instrument. Counter-signal: short/cash on broad BTC is the intended target per counters:long_BTC, so the broad-crypto target is correct here.

name: Fed Excess Bond Premium Positive & Rising With SPY Near Highs -> Short SPY / Long IEF (counter long_SPY)
rule: Monthly, using the Fed FEDS Notes EBP CSV (column 'ebp'): if month-t EBP >= +0.20 AND EBP(t) > EBP(t-3) (3-month slope positive) AND SPY's month-t-end close is within 3% of its trailing 252-trading-day high, then enter equal-notional short SPY / long IEF at the close of the 5th trading day of month t+1 (publication lag buffer). Exit at the close of the 5th trading day of the month after EBP(t) <= EBP(t-3) (slope turns non-positive), OR intramonth if SPY closes 10% below its value on the entry date, whichever comes first. Re-enter whenever conditions re-trigger. Flat otherwise.
entry_conditions: EBP level for month t >= +0.20 (Fed FEDS Notes ebp_csv.csv, column 'ebp')
EBP(t) > EBP(t-3): positive 3-month slope
SPY month-end close within 3% of its rolling 252-trading-day closing high
Execute at close of the 5th trading day of month t+1 (data publication lag)
exit_conditions: EBP(t) <= EBP(t-3): 3-month slope turns non-positive (exit at close of 5th trading day of month t+1)
Hard stop: SPY closes 10% below its entry-date close (exit next close)

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: SPY, IEF (IEF inception 2002-07; backtest window 2003-01 onward)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: Fed EBP monthly CSV: https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/notes/feds-notes/ebp_csv.csv (columns date, gz_spread, ebp, est_prob; 1973-01 through 2026-05, verified live 2026-06-12). FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 optional for validation only.

backtest_approach: Daily PnL long/short overlay: position is -1.0x SPY +1.0x IEF (equal notional, rebalanced at entry) when signal active, else flat; signal state machine evaluated monthly with execution lagged to the 5th trading day of the following month to respect EBP publication timing; compute Sharpe/CAGR/maxDD vs SPY buy-and-hold benchmark over 2003-present; report per-episode stats (2007-08, 2011, 2015-16, 2018, 2020, 2022 are the likely active windows).
implementation_notes: COUNTER-SIGNAL (counters long_SPY) so SPY as primary short target is correct per spec. EBP CSV is monthly and updated early the following month -- the 5-trading-day execution lag is mandatory to avoid lookahead; do NOT use month-t prices on month-t EBP. CSV has no API key, plain HTTPS GET. The historical EBP vintage is revised (full-history re-estimation each update); treat results as in-sample-revised and note this in the report. If federalreserve.gov blocks the fetch, cache /tmp/ebp_csv.csv or use FRED gz-spread proxies only for validation, not the signal.

name: USDA Broiler Hatchery Chicks-Placed YoY Contraction -> 9-Week Supply Cliff -> Long PPC
rule: Weekly, using USDA NASS Broiler Hatchery chicks placed (19-state, head): compute the 4-week moving average and its YoY change vs the same 4-week window a year earlier. When YoY change of the 4-week average is negative for 4 or more consecutive weekly reports, go long PPC at the next Thursday close (report is released Wednesday ~3pm ET). Hold until the 4-week-average YoY turns positive (exit next Thursday close) OR a maximum of 60 trading days (~12 weeks), whichever comes first. Re-entry allowed after exit if the condition re-establishes (4 fresh consecutive negative weeks).
entry_conditions: 4-week MA of weekly chicks placed (head, 19-state total) YoY < 0 for >= 4 consecutive weekly reports
Enter long PPC at the first Thursday close following the 4th qualifying Wednesday report
exit_conditions: 4-week MA YoY turns positive: exit at next Thursday close
Time stop: 60 trading days after entry

data_sources_concrete.prices: yfinance: PPC (history 1987-12 to present, verified), TSN (secondary/comparison), SPY (benchmark)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: USDA NASS QuickStats API, https://quickstats.nass.usda.gov/api/api_GET/ -- short_desc='CHICKENS, BROILERS - PLACEMENTS, MEASURED IN HEAD', freq_desc='WEEKLY', agg_level_desc='NATIONAL' (or 19-state program total). REQUIRES FREE API KEY (instant email registration at quickstats.nass.usda.gov/api). Verified 2026-06-12 that keyless requests return {'error':['unauthorized']}. Fallback: USDA ESMIS/Cornell archive of Broiler Hatchery releases, or event-study seeding from known_events below.

backtest_approach: Primary: daily PnL of the long-PPC state machine driven by the weekly placements series (signal lagged to Thursday close after each Wednesday release), 2010-present; Sharpe/CAGR/maxDD vs SPY and vs PPC buy-and-hold. Fallback if NASS key unavailable: event study on known placement-contraction episodes (see known_events) measuring PPC forward 6/9/12-week returns vs SPY and TSN.
known_events: 2011-11 to 2012-07: industry-wide placement cutbacks after 2011 margin collapse (cleanest episode)
2022-01 to 2022-06: hatchability shortfall (Ross breeder male fertility problem) contracting placements
2008-10 to 2009-06: recession/feed-cost cutbacks -- EXCLUDE or flag: PPC was in Chapter 11 (filed 2008-12) with delisting/dilution; price series not representative
implementation_notes: PPC equity caveats: Chapter 11 Dec-2008 to Dec-2009 reorganization (JBS took control) -- restrict the backtest window to 2010-01 onward to avoid the discontinuity. JBS owns ~80%+ of PPC float, so the stock is thin; use closes only, no intraday assumptions. NASS QuickStats key is free but must be obtained by the backtester (env var NASS_API_KEY suggested); if blocked, run the event-study fallback rather than skipping. Placements are biology-fixed ~9 weeks ahead of slaughter, so the 6-12 week hold matches the supply-trough timing. Watch for HPAI headline weeks: avian-flu-driven placement drops can coincide with demand scares that hit PPC despite the supply mechanism -- note any 2022 anomalies in the report.

name: Banxico Remittance YoY Deceleration -> Short EWW / Long USDMXN
rule: Each month, compute YoY % growth of Banxico monthly family remittances (SE27803, USD mm) and its 3-month moving average. ENTER short EWW (and notionally long USD/MXN) when the 3m-avg YoY crosses below 0% from above AND the 3m-avg was >= +5% at some point in the prior 6 months (regime-break filter). Position taken at the close of the first trading day on or after the 1st of month M+2 relative to data month M (publication lag). EXIT (go flat) when the 3m-avg YoY recovers above +2%, same M+2 timing. Benchmark: SPY buy-and-hold.
entry_conditions: 3-month moving average of remittance YoY growth (SE27803) crosses below 0% from above
3m-avg YoY was >= +5% at least once in the prior 6 monthly observations (ensures it is a deceleration regime break, not chronic stagnation)
Execute at close of first trading day on or after the 1st of month M+2 (data month M is published ~5 weeks later; M+2 timing is conservative and look-ahead-safe)
exit_conditions: 3m-avg remittance YoY growth recovers above +2% (evaluated with the same M+2 publication-lag timing)
No stop-loss; signal is regime-based and monthly-evaluated

data_sources_concrete.prices: EWW (yfinance, history from 1996-03), MXN=X (yfinance, from 2003-12, secondary FX leg), UUP (from 2007, optional), SPY (benchmark)
data_sources_concrete.fundamental: Banxico SIE series SE27803 (total family remittances, monthly, USD millions, from 1995-01) via token-free endpoint: https://www.banxico.org.mx/SieInternet/consultasieiqy?series=SE27803&locale=en&formatoCSV.x=1&anoInicial=1995&anoFinal=2026 -- returns HTML, parse with pd.read_html(StringIO(r.text))[-1]; first row is header ['DATE','SE27803'], column 0 = 'M/YYYY' strings, column 1 = USD mm. FRED DEXMXUS (daily USD/MXN spot from 1995) for the FX-leg PnL with pre-2003 coverage.

backtest_approach: Regime-based daily PnL. Build the monthly signal series from SE27803 YoY 3mma, shift availability by 2 months (data month M tradable at first business day of M+2). While in-regime: primary PnL = -1x EWW daily total return; secondary/robustness leg = +1x daily USD/MXN return from FRED DEXMXUS (long USD). Report primary (short EWW) as headline, and a 50/50 short-EWW + long-USDMXN combo as variant. Flat (zero return) out of regime. Costs: 10 bps round-trip on position changes via compute_metrics(positions=...). Window: 1996-2026 (EWW inception caps start).
known_events: 2008-11 to 2009-12: GFC remittance contraction (YoY deeply negative; peso fell ~50% vs USD; EWW drew down hard)
2020-04: COVID one-month remittance dip (rebounded within 2 months -- 3mma filter likely never confirms; good false-positive test)
2025-H1: remittance YoY turned negative (Banxico data shows 2025 monthly prints flat-to-down vs 2024; most recent live regime)
implementation_notes: VERIFIED 2026-06-12: Banxico token-free endpoint returns full SE27803 history 1995-01..2026-04 (377 rows incl header) and parses with pd.read_html; do NOT use the SIE REST API (requires Bmx-Token). Cache the fetch to data/ like other loaders. Remittance publication lag is ~5 weeks (Apr-2026 was live in early Jun-2026), so M+2 first-business-day execution is conservative; do not use M+1. EWW is the primary target (unhedged peso + equity exposure compounds the move); MXN=X only starts 2003-12 so use FRED DEXMXUS for any pre-2003 FX leg. Remittances have strong seasonality (May/Oct peaks, Jan/Feb troughs) -- YoY transform removes it; do NOT use MoM. SE27803 confirmed as total family remittances in USD mm (e.g. Apr-2026 = 4978.05).
